punctuated:
嘉靖二年進士登科録

玉音

嘉靖二年三月初九日，禮部左侍郎臣賈詠等於奉天門奏：「為科舉事，會試天下舉人，取中四百名。本年三月十五日殿試，合請讀卷官及執事等官，少師兼太子太師、吏部尚書、華蓋殿大學士楊廷和等五十七員。其進士出身等第，恭依太祖高皇帝欽定資格：第一甲例取三名，第一名從六品，第二、第三名正七品，賜進士及第；第二甲從七品，賜進士出身；第三甲正八品，賜同進士出身。」奉聖旨：「是。」欽此。

讀卷官

特進光禄大夫、左柱國、少師兼太子太師、吏部尚書、華蓋殿大學士楊廷和，戌成進士。

光禄大夫、柱國、少傅兼太子太傅、戸部尚書、謹身殿大學士蔣冕，丁未進士。

光禄大夫、柱國、少保兼太子太保、戸部尚書、武英殿大學士毛紀，丁未進士。
translation_en:
Record of Metropolitan Graduates of the Second Year of Jiajing (1523)

The Imperial Pronouncement

On the ninth day of the third month of the second year of Jiajing, your servant Jia Yong, Left Vice Minister of Rites, and others submitted the following memorial at Fengtian Gate: “Concerning the civil-service examinations: the Metropolitan Examination of provincial graduates from throughout the empire has selected four hundred successful candidates. For the Palace Examination on the fifteenth day of the third month of this year, we request the appointment of fifty-seven officials as readers and other examination functionaries, including Yang Tinghe, Junior Preceptor, concurrently Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of the Huagai Hall. The grades of status conferred upon the metropolitan graduates shall respectfully follow the qualifications imperially established by Emperor Taizu Gao. In the first class, three men are selected according to precedent: the first receives lower sixth rank, and the second and third receive upper seventh rank, with all three granted the distinction ‘metropolitan graduate with honors.’ Those in the second class receive lower seventh rank and are granted ‘metropolitan graduate status.’ Those in the third class receive upper eighth rank and are granted ‘status equivalent to metropolitan graduate.’” The imperial rescript was received: “Approved.” Respectfully received.

Readers

Yang Tinghe held the titles Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Special Advancement and Left Pillar of State. He was Junior Preceptor, concurrently Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of the Huagai Hall; he became a metropolitan graduate in the year recorded as 戌成 [?].

Jiang Mian held the titles Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and Pillar of State. He was Junior Mentor, concurrently Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Revenue, and Grand Secretary of the Jinshen Hall; he became a metropolitan graduate in the dingwei year (1487).

Mao Ji held the titles Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and Pillar of State. He was Junior Guardian, concurrently Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Revenue, and Grand Secretary of the Wuying Hall; he became a metropolitan graduate in the dingwei year (1487).

translation_en:
Sequence of Imperial Favors and Honors
On the morning of the fifteenth day of the third month of the second year of Jiajing (1523), the tribute scholars proceeded to the inner palace for the Palace Examination. His Majesty took his seat in Fengtian Hall and personally bestowed the policy questions.
On the morning of the eighteenth day of the third month, all civil and military officials attended in their assigned ranks, wearing court robes. That day, the Embroidered-uniform Guard arrayed the ceremonial insignia and equipage within the vermilion steps and courtyard. His Majesty took his seat in Fengtian Hall. Officials of the Court of State Ceremonial transmitted the imperial decree and proclaimed the candidates’ names. Officials of the Ministry of Rites carried the yellow results placard out beyond Chang’an Left Gate, led by drums and music. After the placard had been posted, officials of Shuntian Prefecture escorted the first-place graduate (zhuangyuan) back to his residence with parasols, canopies, and a ceremonial retinue.
On the nineteenth day of the third month …

translation_en:
…An imperial banquet was bestowed at the Ministry of Rites. After the banquet, the graduates went to the Court of State Ceremonial to rehearse the rites.
On the twenty-first day of the third month, the first-ranked graduate was granted court robes, a cap, and a girdle, and the metropolitan graduates (jinshi) were granted paper currency.
On the twenty-second day of the third month, the first-ranked graduate led the other metropolitan graduates in submitting a memorial expressing gratitude for imperial favor.
On the twenty-third day of the third month, the first-ranked graduate led the other metropolitan graduates to the temple of Confucius, the First Teacher, to perform the vegetable-offering rite.
The Ministry of Rites submitted a request to the throne, and the Ministry of Works was ordered to erect a stone stele at the Directorate of Education and inscribe the graduates’ names upon it.

第一甲三名，賜進士及第。

姚淶〔貫浙江寧波府慈谿縣，軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字維東，行八，年三十六，四月二十三日生。〕曾祖悌〔贈右副都御史〕，祖堂〔贈主事，加贈右副都御史〕，父鏌〔工部右侍郎〕，母張氏〔贈安人，加贈淑人〕，繼母汪氏〔封安人，加封淑人〕。嚴侍下，弟汲、滾，娶王氏。浙江鄉試第七名，會試第二名。

王教〔貫河南開封府祥符縣，民籍，順天府良鄉縣人，國子生，治詩經，字庸之，行二，年四十五，二月二十四日生。〕曾祖士賢，祖斌〔前光祿寺署丞〕，父鶴，前母郭氏，母孟氏。永感下，兄玟、琇、璜、瑄、玹、琚、珮、元福、天敘，弟化、天祿、天爵、天瑞，娶扈氏。河南鄉試第六名，會試第二十四名。

徐階〔貫直隸松江府華亭縣，民籍，縣學生，治詩經，字子升，行二，年二十一，九月二十日生。〕曾祖賢，祖禮，父黼〔縣丞〕，前母林氏、錢氏，母顧氏。具慶下，兄隆，弟陳、陟，聘沈氏。應天府鄉試第七名，會試第五十名。
translation_en:
First Class: three men, granted the degree of metropolitan graduate with honors (jinshi jidi).

Yao Lai, registered in a military household in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Weidong; he ranked eighth in family order and was aged thirty-six, born on the twenty-third day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather Ti was posthumously appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief; his grandfather Tang was posthumously appointed Secretary, with the additional posthumous appointment of Right Vice Censor-in-Chief. His father Mo was Right Vice Minister of Works. His mother, née Zhang, was posthumously granted the title Lady of Peace (anren), subsequently elevated to Lady of Virtue (shuren); his stepmother, née Wang, was granted the same titles in succession. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brothers were Ji and Gun. He married a woman née Wang. He placed seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Jiao, registered in a civilian household in Xiangfu County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, was a native of Liangxiang County, Shuntian Prefecture, and a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Yongzhi; he ranked second in family order and was aged forty-five, born on the twenty-fourth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shixian; his grandfather Bin was formerly an Office Assistant in the Court of Imperial Entertainments; his father was He. His father's former wife was née Guo, and his mother was née Meng. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Wen, Xiu, Huang, Xuan, Xuan, Ju, Pei, Yuanfu, and Tianxu; his younger brothers were Hua, Tianlu, Tianjue, and Tianrui. He married a woman née Hu. He placed sixth in the Henan Provincial Examination and twenty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Jie, registered in a civilian household in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a county government school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Zisheng; he ranked second in family order and was aged twenty-one, born on the twentieth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xian; his grandfather was Li; his father Fu was a County Vice Magistrate. His father's former wives were née Lin and née Qian, and his mother was née Gu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Long; his younger brothers were Chen and Zhi. He was betrothed to a woman née Shen. He placed seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fiftieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Second Class: 142 men, granted the status of metropolitan graduate (jinshi).

Li Shunchen 李舜臣 was registered in a civilian household in Le’an County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Maoqin; he was second in birth order, aged twenty-five, and born on the seventeenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Jin, his grandfather Chao, and his father Yue, a prefectural Jail Warden. His father’s former wife was née Cao, his mother née Cai, and his stepmother née Meng. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Tianci, and his younger brothers were Shunjia, Shunyu, Shuntao, and Shunzi. He married a woman née Zhang. He ranked sixty-seventh in the Shandong Provincial Examination and first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hua Yue 華鑰 was registered in a civilian household in Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, Zhili, and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Deqi; he was first in birth order, aged twenty-six, and born on the twenty-sixth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Shoufang, his grandfather Jiong, his father Ji, and his mother née Zhao. His mother alone was living. His younger brother was Jian. He married a woman née Zou. He ranked first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 152nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Zhao 王召 was registered in a civilian household in Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, Zhili, and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zixing; he was first in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the first day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Jing, his grandfather Zong, who held an honorary official title for longevity, his father Ze, and his mother née Qian. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Wen, a tribute scholar (gongshi), and Zi. He married a woman née Deng. He ranked 101st in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 391st in the Metropolitan Examination.

張京安〔貫直隸蘇州府常熟縣，軍籍，國子生，治書經，字康甫，行二，年四十一，十月十一日生〕。曾祖衎，祖綵，父學〔知縣〕，母沈氏。慈侍下，兄善徵、善禮，弟福成、明揚，娶陳氏。應天府鄉試第五十名，會試第二百九十四名。
translation_en:
Shi Yingzhong, registered in Shanghai County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student. He specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zizhen; he ranked fifth in his family and was twenty-six sui, born on the twenty-seventh day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Ming; his grandfather was Tingyu; his father was Quan, Chief of Police; and his mother was née Zhang. Grandparents and parents were living. His elder brothers were Meizhong, Runzhong, Yunzhong, and Yanzhong, and his younger brother was Yizhong. He married a woman née Qiao. He placed thirty-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yao Wenzhao, registered in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a salt-producing household and was an additional student at the prefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zaiming; he ranked eighth in his family and was twenty-nine sui, born on the twenty-third day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Mian, Instructor; his grandfather was Qu, posthumously appointed Assistant Director of the Court of Imperial Studs; his father was Yong, Assistant Director of the Court of Imperial Studs; and his mother was née Yu, invested with the title Lady of Repose. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Wenye, a tribute scholar, Wenbiao, and Wenzhuo; his younger brothers were Wenyu, Wenyan, and Wenfu. He married a woman née Chen. He placed sixth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and two hundred twenty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Jiong, registered in Jishui County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Meizhong; he ranked first in his family and was thirty-nine sui, born on the twelfth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Suyu, an honorary official recognized for longevity; his grandfather was Shucheng, posthumously appointed Guard Registrar; his father was Quan, Prefectural Registrar; his mother was née Xu, posthumously granted the title Lady; and his stepmother was née Yi. His father and stepmother were living. His younger brothers were Jiu and Zu. He married a woman née Li and subsequently a woman née Yan. He placed sixty-fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and seventeenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Jing’an, registered in Changshu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Kangfu; he ranked second in his family and was forty-one sui, born on the eleventh day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Kan; his grandfather was Cai; his father was Xue, District Magistrate; and his mother was née Shen. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Shanzheng and Shanli; his younger brothers were Fucheng and Mingyang. He married a woman née Chen. He placed fiftieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and two hundred ninety-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Sun Jilu, registered in a military household of the Yunnan Right Guard in Yunnan and a native of Qiantang County, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Daofu; he ranked eighth among his brothers and male cousins and was twenty-six, born on the first day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Jue, his grandfather Duo, his father Xi, and his mother Lady Li. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jixian, Jizong, Jiyuan, Jizhou, and Jishu; his younger brothers were Jizhi and Jizou. He was betrothed to Lady Ma. He placed twelfth in the Yunnan–Guizhou Provincial Examination and 380th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Chen, registered in an officer household of the Baoding Left Guard under the Daning Regional Military Commission and a native of Shunyi County, Shuntian Prefecture, was a student of the Regional Military Commission school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Tingxian; he ranked third among his brothers and male cousins and was twenty-four, born on the seventeenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather Wang, grandfather Qing, and father Hong were all company commanders. His mother, Lady Wang, had been granted the title Lady of Peace. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yuan, a company commander, and Guan; his younger brother was Lian. He married Lady Sun. He placed fifty-fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fifty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dai Shibian, registered in a civilian household of Linhai County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Zhengfu; he ranked third among his brothers and male cousins and was twenty-three, born on the twentieth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Tingxiang; his grandfather Zhongren had been posthumously appointed Investigating Censor. His father was Cong; his father's former wife was Lady Zhang, his legal mother was Lady Ying, and his birth mother was Lady Zhou. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Yue; his younger brothers were Shixi, Shitai, Shijing, Shihe, Shichang, and Shiming. He married Lady Qin. He placed thirtieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ouyang De, registered in a military household of Taihe County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi, was an additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Chongyi; he ranked fifth among his brothers and male cousins and was twenty-eight, born on the second day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather Guanghong held an honorary official title conferred for longevity; his grandfather was Shimian, his father Yong, and his mother Lady Xiao. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Ta (𦐇) [?]. He married Lady Kang. He placed fortieth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and twenty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

楊惇〔貫四川成都府新都縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字用敘，行二，年三十五，正月十二日生〕。曾祖壽〔累贈光祿大夫柱國少師兼太子太師吏部尚書華蓋殿大學士〕，祖春〔湖廣按察司僉事，累贈光祿大夫柱國少師兼太子太師吏部尚書華蓋殿大學士〕，父廷和〔光祿大夫柱國少師兼太子太師吏部尚書華蓋殿大學士〕，母黃氏〔累贈一品夫人〕，繼母喻氏〔累封一品夫人〕。具慶下，兄慎〔翰林院修撰〕，弟愷〔貢士〕、恒〔中書舍人〕、恂〔會試中式舉人〕、忱〔貢士〕、悌、慥〔國子生〕、悅、惟，娶歐氏。四川鄉試第二名，會試第七十七名。
translation_en:
Wu Changling, registered in a military household in Liu’an Subprefecture, Luzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Deyuan, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged forty-two, born on the fourteenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Jian; his grandfather, Xuan, was a Magistrate; his father was Song; his mother was née Cao, and his stepmother née Dai. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Changguo, and his wife was née Qiao. He placed twenty-first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Wan, registered in a guardsman household of the Guangxi Ceremonial Guard Office and originally from Qingtian County, Zhejiang, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Defu, he ranked fifth among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-one, born on the eighth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Qi, his grandfather Rong, his father Jian, and his mother née Zhao. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Cong, Guan, and Ju; his younger brother was Qiong; and his wife was née Liu. He placed first in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and 273rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Hui, registered in a civilian household in Shanyang County, Huai’an Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zizhen, he ranked eighth among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-one, born on the twenty-second day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Qing; his grandfather, Jin, held a seventh-rank prestige title; his father, Zhang, held the honorary title of Official for Righteousness; and his mother was née Qian. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brothers were Hui, who died young, Hua, Chang, Dechou [?], and Deyi; his younger brothers were Delü, Dezui [?], a National University student, Demo, Deju, a Director of Foodstuffs, Desi, Dehuang, Deying, Dexian, and Deshi. His wife was née Ding. He placed fifteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Dun, registered in a civilian household in Xindu County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Yongxu, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-five, born on the twelfth day of the first month. His great-grandfather, Shou, had received successive posthumous grants of the titles Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Pillar of the State, Junior Preceptor concurrently serving as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of the Huagai Hall. His grandfather, Chun, had been Assistant Surveillance Commissioner in Huguang and had received successive posthumous grants of the same titles. His father, Tinghe, held those titles and offices. His mother, née Huang, had received successive posthumous grants of the title Lady of the First Rank; his stepmother, née Yu, had received successive grants of that title. Both parents were living. His elder brother, Shen, was a Senior Compiler in the Hanlin Academy. His younger brothers were Kai, a tribute scholar (gongshi); Heng, a Secretariat Drafter; Xun, a provincial graduate who had passed the Metropolitan Examination; Chen, a tribute scholar; Ti; Zao, a National University student; Yue; and Wei. His wife was née Ou. He placed second in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and seventy-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

程旦〔貫直隸徽州府歙縣民籍，國子生，治禮記，字孟明，行八，年三十七，十二月十七日生〕。曾祖文生，祖福仁〔義官〕，父正春，母王氏。永感下，弟旭、暕、朏、曙，娶鄭氏。應天府鄉試第一百五名，會試第二百三十二名。

高叔嗣〔貫河南開封府祥符縣民籍，國子生，治易經，字子業，行三，年二十三，十二月十四日生〕。曾祖清，祖謹，父珣〔知縣〕，母甄氏。具慶下，兄伯嗣、仲嗣，娶袁氏。河南鄉試第二十二名，會試第一百九十九名。

丘民範〔貫江西廣信府貴溪縣民籍，縣學生，治書經，字汝中，行二十六，年二十六，十一月二十二日生〕。曾祖祺〔知府〕，祖珮，父鉅，母畢氏。慈侍下，兄文浩〔聽選官〕、民望〔監生〕、民仰〔貢士〕，弟民食〔貢士〕、民樂、民節、民符，娶張氏。江西鄉試第四十三名，會試第七名。

林文華〔貫福建興化府莆田縣匠籍，府學生，治詩經，字質夫，行二，年三十五，正月初一日生〕。曾祖堯真〔壽官〕，祖朝弼，父舜中〔壽官〕，前母羅氏，母羅氏。具慶下，兄文英，弟文腆，娶鄭氏。福建鄉試第四十一名，會試第三百二十三名。
translation_en:
Cheng Dan, registered in She County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Mengming; he ranked eighth in family birth order and was aged thirty-seven, born on the seventeenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wensheng; his grandfather, Furen, held the honorary title of Official for Righteous Conduct; his father was Zhengchun, and his mother was née Wang. His parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Xu, Jian, Fei, and Shu, and his wife was née Zheng. He placed 105th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 232nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gao Shusi, registered in Xiangfu County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Ziye; he ranked third in family birth order and was aged twenty-three, born on the fourteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qing; his grandfather was Jin; his father, Xun, was a District Magistrate; and his mother was née Zhen. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Bosi and Zhongsi, and his wife was née Yuan. He placed twenty-second in the Henan Provincial Examination and 199th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qiu Minfan, registered in Guixi County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Ruzhong; he ranked twenty-sixth in family birth order and was aged twenty-six, born on the twenty-second day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather, Qi, was a Prefect; his grandfather was Pei; his father was Ju; and his mother was née Bi. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Wenhao, an official awaiting selection for appointment; Minwang, an Imperial University student; and Minyang, a tribute scholar. His younger brothers were Minshi, a tribute scholar, Minle, Minjie, and Minfu. His wife was née Zhang. He placed forty-third in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Wenhua, registered in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to an artisan household and was a prefectural government school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zhifu; he ranked second in family birth order and was aged thirty-five, born on the first day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather, Yaozhen, held an honorary official title granted for longevity; his grandfather was Chaobi; and his father, Shunzhong, likewise held an honorary official title granted for longevity. His father's former wife was née Luo, and his mother was also née Luo. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Wenying, his younger brother was Wentian, and his wife was née Zheng. He placed forty-first in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 323rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

馮冠〔貫直隸蘇州府常熟縣，軍籍，國子生，治春秋，字正伯，行一，年四十五，九月二十三日生〕。曾祖達，祖順〔封監察御史〕，父玘〔按察司副使，進階亞中大夫〕，母李氏〔封孺人〕。具慶下，弟憲、寀，娶金氏。應天府鄉試第一百二十三名，會試第二百四十五名。

屠大山〔貫浙江寧波府鄞縣，民籍，府學附學生，治易經，字國望，行二十三，年二十四，五月初一日生〕。曾祖瑜〔封榮祿大夫、太子太保、吏部尚書〕，祖渭〔義官〕，父偁，母王氏，繼母陳氏。慈侍下，弟大嶽、大年、大巖、大文、大受、大熬、大美、大亮、大亨、大貞、大音，娶陸氏。浙江鄉試第四十一名，會試第二百五十六名。
translation_en:
Song Gui, courtesy name Yuanxi, was registered in Xincheng County, Baoding Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty [?; the transcription is corrupt], and born on the twentieth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather Gui was officially commended as a righteous commoner; his grandfather was Wen; his father Lin was a County Magistrate; and his mother was née Zhang. His parents and grandparents were deceased. His elder brother was Kui, and his wife was née Xu. He placed eighth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 111th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Runi, courtesy name Yida, was registered in Anfu County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a military household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-nine, and born on the twenty-fourth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather Gongzheng was granted the title of Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice; his grandfather Kun was posthumously granted the title of Left Case Reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review; his father Ang held the honorary designation of Righteous Official; and his mother was née Yan. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Rulun, Ruyuan, and Ruxuan, and his wife was née Peng. He placed seventy-ninth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 300th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Feng Guan, courtesy name Zhengbo, was registered in Changshu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a military household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was first in birth order, aged forty-five, and born on the twenty-third day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Da; his grandfather Shun was granted the title of Investigating Censor; his father Qi was a Surveillance Vice Commissioner, advanced to the prestige rank of Yazhong dafu; and his mother, née Li, was granted the title of Lady (ruren). Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Xian and Cai, and his wife was née Jin. He placed 123rd in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 245th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tu Dashan, courtesy name Guowang, was registered in Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household. An additional student at the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Changes, he was twenty-third in birth order, aged twenty-four, and born on the first day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather Yu was granted the titles of Grand Master for Glorious Emolument, Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and Minister of Personnel; his grandfather Wei held the honorary designation of Righteous Official; his father was Cheng; his mother was née Wang; and his stepmother was née Chen. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brothers were Dayue, Danian, Dayan, Dawen, Dashou, Da’ao, Damei, Daliang, Daheng, Dazhen, and Dayin, and his wife was née Lu. He placed forty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 256th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Pan En 潘恩, courtesy name Ziren, was registered in a civilian household in Shanghai County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A county school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the twenty-sixth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Lin, an Office Commissioner; his grandfather was Qing; and his father was Kui, a County Clerk. His father’s former wife was née Zhao, and his mother was née Qian. He had surviving grandparents and both parents living. His younger brothers were Hui, Zhong, and Shu. He married a woman née Bao and subsequently a woman née Cao. He ranked ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventy-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fang Yilan 方一蘭, courtesy name Shipei, was registered in a military household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian. An attached student of the prefectural school specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-four, and born on the fifth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Xin, a Prefectural Vice Prefect promoted to the prestige title Grand Master of Central Compliance; his grandfather was Bian; and his father was Yixian, a District Magistrate. His mother was née Wu. Both parents were living. His elder brother Yigui became a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) in the same examination cohort; his younger brother was Yiwu. He married a woman née Chen. He ranked eighth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and twenty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Ru 陳儒, courtesy name Ruzong, was registered in an officer household of the Embroidered-uniform Guard. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was fourth in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the fifth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Shi, a Company Commander in the Embroidered-uniform Guard, posthumously granted the title General of Military Strategy; his grandfather was Baozong, a Vice Battalion Commander in the same guard; and his father was Xian, an Admonisher. His father’s former wives were née Huang and née Tian; his mother was née Tian, and his stepmother was née Yin. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Jun and Wei, both Vice Battalion Commanders, and Jie; his younger brothers were Ren, Zuo, and Yi. He married a woman née Hou and subsequently a woman née Yang. He ranked twenty-first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ruan Chaodong 阮朝東, courtesy name Zixi, was registered in a civilian household in Macheng County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-four, and born on the twelfth day of the intercalary ninth month. His great-grandfather was Gang, a Vice Magistrate; his grandfather was Dayong; and his father was Gui. His father’s former wife was née He, and his mother was née Cai. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Chaoyang, a tribute scholar (gongshi); his younger brothers were Chaonan, Chaoduan, Chaosui (a tribute scholar), Chaoshi, Chaoce (a tribute scholar), and Chaoyi. He married a woman née Yin. He ranked first in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 174th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wan Xiang 萬象, courtesy name Gongchen, was registered in a civilian household in Yugan County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi. A county government student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was twelfth in birth order, aged forty-four, and born on the sixth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yanbin; his grandfather, Fu’an; his father, Zhang; and his mother, née Zhang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Guan, Xian, Gai, Chong, and Cai; his younger brother was Shourong. He married a woman née Wu. He ranked twelfth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 275th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Bi 鄭弼, courtesy name Xiefu, was registered in a military household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian. A Directorate of Education student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the seventeenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qi, a Grand Coordinator; his grandfather, Qian, an Assistant Instructor; his father, Hui; and his mother, née Ye. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Lu and Huan; his younger brothers were Yu, Jun, Cheng, Bin, Zhan, Xiang, Xiu, Xi, Shu, and Kui. He married a woman née Yu. He ranked third in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 160th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lü Zhuan 呂顓, courtesy name Youtong, was registered in a civilian household in Ningzhou, Qingyang Prefecture, Shaanxi. A subprefectural government student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-six, and born on the twenty-seventh day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ying, a Subprefectural Judge; his grandfather, Sheng, posthumously granted the civil prestige title Zhengshi lang and the office of Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Rites; and his father, Lun, an honorary official for public benefaction. His mother was née Yang, and his stepmother was née Xing. Parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Xian, Xu, and Qi. He married a woman née Ge. He ranked first in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 293rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Feng Fang 豐坊, courtesy name Cunli, was registered in a civilian household in Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang. A prefectural government student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was third in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the fifth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qing, a Right Provincial Administration Commissioner. His grandfather, Yun, was an Instructor, additionally granted the titles Grand Master for Upright Service and Right Mentor of the Right Secretariat of the Heir Apparent. His father, Xi, held the title Grand Master for Upright Service, the designation ‘assisting in rectifying the various officials’ [?], and the office of Right Mentor of the Right Secretariat of the Heir Apparent. His mother, née Shi, was additionally granted the title Lady of Suitability. Parents and grandparents were living. His elder brothers were Zhi and Yuan; his younger brother was Chi. He married a woman née Zhou. He ranked first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 215th in the Metropolitan Examination.

陸銓〔貫浙江寧波府鄞縣軍籍，國子生，治易經，字選之，行五七，年三十二，十二月二十七日生〕。曾祖琦，祖垸〔贈監察御史〕，父偁〔按察司副使，封中順大夫〕，母楊氏〔封恭人〕。具慶下，兄鎬、鉞〔監生〕、鈇、鉝、鈳〔南京兵部郎中〕、鐄，弟釴〔翰林院編修〕，娶陳氏。浙江鄉試第十四名，會試第三名。

陳九成〔貫江西廣信府玉山縣民籍，國子生，治書經，字大韶，行二十一，年四十二，正月十九日生〕。曾祖俊民，祖景榮，父龍〔訓導〕，母汪氏。具慶下，兄端陽、白陽，弟三陽、畎、九經，娶王氏。江西鄉試第三十六名，會試第六十九名。
translation_en:
Lu Xiang 盧襄 was registered in a civilian household in Wu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Changes, he had the courtesy name Shichen and ranked second in his family; he was forty-three years old, born on the seventeenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Li; his grandfather was Shicheng; his father was Gang, granted the title of Investigating Censor. His mother, née Chen, was posthumously granted the title of Lady (ruren), and his stepmother was née Wu. Both parents were living. His elder brother Yong was a Surveillance Vice Commissioner serving as Education Intendant. His wife was née Chen. He placed tenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 295th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Hang 黃杭 was registered in a military household of Pinghai Guard, Fujian, and was a native of Longxi County. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Documents, he had the courtesy name Bozhou and ranked sixth in his family; he was thirty years old, born on the tenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Yimin; his grandfather was Bangzheng, an honorary official recognized for longevity; his father was Qing, an Assistant Prefect of a subprefecture. His father's principal wife was née Ye, and his birth mother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Kui, Yan (an Imperial University student), Qing, and Xun; his younger brothers were Qin and Shi. His wife was née Dai. He placed twenty-eighth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and seventy-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Quan 陸銓 was registered in a military household in Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Changes, he had the courtesy name Xuanzhi and ranked fifty-seven [?] in his family; he was thirty-two years old, born on the twenty-seventh day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Qi; his grandfather was Yuan, posthumously granted the title of Investigating Censor; his father was Cheng, a Surveillance Vice Commissioner granted the title of Grand Master of Central Accord. His mother, née Yang, was granted the title of Lady of Respect (gongren). Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Gao, Yue (an Imperial University student), Fu, Li, Ke (a Bureau Director in the Nanjing Ministry of War), and Huang; his younger brother Yi was a Hanlin Academy Compiler. His wife was née Chen. He placed fourteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Jiucheng 陳九成 was registered in a civilian household in Yushan County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Documents, he had the courtesy name Dashao and ranked twenty-first in his family; he was forty-two years old, born on the nineteenth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Junmin; his grandfather was Jingrong; his father was Long, an Assistant Instructor; his mother was née Wang 汪. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Duanyang and Baiyang; his younger brothers were Sanyang, Quan, and Jiujing. His wife was née Wang 王. He placed thirty-sixth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and sixty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
胡有恒〔貫直隸淮安府山陽縣，民籍，國子生，治禮記，字貞甫，行一，年三十四，三月初一日生〕。曾祖銘，祖祐，父淮，母鄒氏。慈侍下，弟有容、有執、有為，聘倪氏，娶張氏。應天府鄉試第九十五名，會試第二百十一名。

周祖堯〔貫山東兗州府東平州，民籍，州學生，治書經，字宗道，行一，年三十，十二月二十一日生〕。曾祖監〔府檢校〕，祖愷，父瑀，母李氏。具慶下，弟祖舜，娶張氏。山東鄉試第三名，會試第二百八十六名。

甘為霖〔貫四川敘州府富順縣，軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字公望，行二，年三十六，十二月二十一日生〕。曾祖雨〔封布政司參議、資治少尹〕，祖敬修〔亞中大夫、布政司左參政〕，父澤〔訓科〕，母凃氏，繼母趙氏。慈侍下，兄汝霖，弟嘉霖、化霖、春霖、傳霖，娶周氏，繼娶徐氏。四川鄉試第四十六名，會試第十五名。

程煌〔貫直隸徽州府婺源縣，民籍，國子生，治書經，字子明，行二十二，年三十八，正月二十日生〕。曾祖孟通，祖士英，父枋，母汪氏。永感下，弟燦，娶俞氏。應天府鄉試第八十一名，會試第一百八十一名。
translation_en:
Hu Youheng, registered in Shanyang County, Huai’an Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Zhenfu. First in birth order, he was thirty-four years old and was born on the first day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ming, his grandfather You, his father Huai, and his mother née Zou. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Yourong, Youzhi, and Youwei. He was betrothed to a woman née Ni and married a woman née Zhang. He placed ninety-fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 211th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Zuyao, registered in Dongping Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the subprefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Zongdao. First in birth order, he was thirty years old and was born on the twenty-first day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jian, a prefectural examiner; his grandfather was Kai, his father Yu, and his mother née Li. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Zushun, and he married a woman née Zhang. He placed third in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 286th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gan Weilin, registered in Fushun County, Xuzhou Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Gongwang. Second in birth order, he was thirty-six years old and was born on the twenty-first day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yu, honorarily invested as Assistant Administration Commissioner and with the prestige title Zizhi shaoyin; his grandfather was Jingxiu, who held the prestige title Yazhong dafu and served as Left Administration Vice Commissioner; his father was Ze, a medical instructor. His mother was née Tu, and his stepmother née Zhao. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Rulin, and his younger brothers were Jialin, Hualin, Chunlin, and Chuanlin. He married a woman née Zhou and subsequently a woman née Xu. He placed forty-sixth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and fifteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cheng Huang, registered in Wuyuan County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Ziming. Twenty-second in birth order, he was thirty-eight years old and was born on the twentieth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Mengtong, his grandfather Shiying, his father Fang, and his mother née Wang. Both parents were deceased. His younger brother was Can, and he married a woman née Yu. He placed eighty-first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 181st in the Metropolitan Examination.

董漢策〔貫湖廣辰州衛，官籍，浙江鄞縣人，國子生，治書經，字道夫，行一，年四十，七月二十三日生〕。曾祖良，祖昱〔百戶〕，父俊〔兵部員外郎〕，母芮氏〔封安人〕。慈侍下，弟漢醇、漢儒〔副千戶〕，娶蕭氏、彭氏、濮氏，繼娶龔氏。湖廣鄉試第四十三名，會試第八十九名。

劉炯〔貫直隸蘇州府長洲縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字文韜，行三，年三十九，九月初一日生〕。曾祖宗韶，祖淳〔贈工部主事〕，父杲〔都察院右副都御史〕，母張氏〔封安人〕，繼母唐氏。慈侍下，兄恢、燦，弟熈〔陰陽正術〕、禜〔典膳〕，娶楊氏。應天府鄉試第一百三名，會試第一百二名。

鄭曉〔貫浙江嘉興府海鹽縣，軍匠籍，縣學生，治書經，字窒甫，行五，年二十五，正月十二日生〕。曾祖讓，祖延〔市舶提舉司副提舉〕，父儒泰〔訓導〕，母費氏。具慶下，兄暲、昕、時、暘，弟曦、啓、職、曐，娶劉氏。浙江鄉試第一名，會試第十四名。
translation_en:
Zhao Tingsong, registered in Yueqing County, Wenzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a county government student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zihou; he ranked ninth in his family and was twenty-nine years old, born on the nineteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shoujian, his grandfather Lai, his father Zao, and his mother née Zeng. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Ruisong (an Imperial University student), Yansong, Chisong, and Shengsong; his younger brother was Jiasong. He married a woman née Yu. He placed sixty-ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 254th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dong Hance, registered in an official household of the Chenzhou Guard, Huguang, was originally from Yin County, Zhejiang. He was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Daofu; he ranked first in his family and was forty years old, born on the twenty-third day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Liang, his grandfather Yu (a Company Commander), and his father Jun (a Vice Director in the Ministry of War); his mother, née Rui, was granted the title Lady of Peace. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brothers were Hanchun and Hanru (a Deputy Battalion Commander). He married women née Xiao, Peng, and Pu, and subsequently a woman née Gong. He placed forty-third in the Huguang Provincial Examination and eighty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Jiong, registered in Changzhou County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Wentao; he ranked third in his family and was thirty-nine years old, born on the first day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zongshao, his grandfather Chun (posthumously appointed a Secretary in the Ministry of Works), and his father Gao (Right Vice Censor-in-chief of the Censorate). His mother, née Zhang, was granted the title Lady of Peace; his stepmother was née Tang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Hui and Can; his younger brothers were Xi (Director of a School of Yin and Yang) and Yong (a Provisioner). He married a woman née Yang. He placed 103rd in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 102nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Xiao, registered in Haiyan County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a military artisan household and was a county government student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zhifu; he ranked fifth in his family and was twenty-five years old, born on the twelfth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rang, his grandfather Yan (Deputy Superintendent of a Maritime Trade Superintendency), his father Rutai (an Assistant Instructor), and his mother née Fei. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zhang, Xin, Shi, and Yang; his younger brothers were Xi, Qi, Zhi, and Xing [division of the brothers’ names uncertain]. He married a woman née Liu. He placed first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fourteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Chen Wenyu 陳文譽, courtesy name Deqing, was registered in a civilian household in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked eighty-seventh in his family and was aged thirty-two, born on the seventeenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was He; his grandfather, Ming, was an assistant subprefect; his father was Guan; his mother was née Wang, and his birth mother was née Peng. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Wenjiang, and his wife was née Feng. He placed seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 240th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Wei 胡偉, courtesy name Shiqi, was registered in an artisan household attached to the Wugong Central Guard and was a native of Wutai County, Shanxi. An additional student at the Shuntian prefectural school specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked second in his family and was aged twenty-five, born on the seventeenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather, Yu, was a company commander; his grandfather, Jin, was a disciplinary officer; his father was Zhong, and his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Jun, and his younger brothers were Ru and Qiao. He married a woman née Dong and subsequently became betrothed to a woman née Chen. He placed seventy-sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 260th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Ting 王庭, courtesy name Zhifu, was registered in a civilian household in Changzhou County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Changes, he ranked third in his family and was aged thirty-six, born on the twenty-eighth day of the intercalary first month. His great-grandfather was Kexing; his grandfather was Min; his father, Yi, was an assistant instructor. His father's former wife was née Xue, and his mother was née Yu. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were En, Lu, and Wen. He married a woman née Chen and subsequently married a woman née Yu 郁. He placed sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 178th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yi Luan 易鸞, courtesy name Minghe, was registered in a civilian household in Fenyi County, Yuanzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi. A county-school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked first in his family and was aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-third day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Qing; his grandfather was Zhen; his father was Juren, and his mother was née Huang. Both parents were living. His wife was née Yuan. He placed seventy-seventh in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 135th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhu Zhe 朱淛, registered in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a salt-producing household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Bidong; he ranked fifteenth among his brothers and male cousins and was aged twenty-eight, born on the fourth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kai, his grandfather Zhong, his father Tong, and his mother née Wu. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Chenxing, and his wife was née Lin. He placed first in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 129th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Peng An 彭黯, registered in Anfu County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Daoxian; he ranked fifth among his brothers and male cousins and was aged thirty-seven, born on the fifth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yiyuan, his grandfather Yu, his father Ruxiang, and his mother née Liu. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brother was Dian, and his wife was née Wang. He placed sixteenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 150th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Gun 章袞, registered in Linchuan County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to an artisan household and was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Ruming; he ranked sixth among his brothers and male cousins and was aged thirty-five, born on the twentieth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Guiyan, his grandfather Dakai, his father Xiaoying, and his mother née Shu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Fu 甫, his younger brother Fu 芾, and his wife was née Huang. He placed second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 371st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhong Wang 鍾汪, registered in Nanhai County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, belonged to a military household and served as Instructor at the Wuning County school in Jiangxi, specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Jishen; he ranked fifth among his brothers and male cousins and was aged forty-three, born on the sixteenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jinyang, his grandfather Xuanling, his father Luan, and his mother née Zhou. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Shi (an Instructor), Yan, and Xiang; his wife was née Zeng. He placed twenty-fourth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 128th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Gu Menggui 顧夢圭 was registered in Kunshan County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Wuxiang, ranked third in family order, and was aged twenty-four, born on the twenty-seventh day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Xun, posthumously granted the titles of Left Admonisher of the Left Secretariat and concurrently Reader-in-Waiting of the Hanlin Academy; his grandfather was Yizhi, granted the title of Investigating Censor; and his father was Qian, a Prefect and formerly an Education Intendant serving as a censor. His mother, née Gong, was granted the title of Lady (ruren), and his stepmother was née Yang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Wenzheng, a Registrar; his younger brothers were Wentong, Mengchuan, Mengxiong, Qianheng, Mengyu, and Menggu. He married a woman née Huangfu. He ranked eighty-seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 234th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ying Tingyu 應廷育 was registered in Yongkang County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household. A county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Renqing, ranked eighty-second in family order, and was aged twenty-seven, born on the thirteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Sijing, his grandfather Shangzhi, his father Shu, and his mother née Lou. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brother was Tingzhi. He married a woman née Chi. He ranked thirty-sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and sixty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xia Mi 夏謐 was registered in Jinxian County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a military household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he had the courtesy name Tingyi, ranked twenty-fourth in family order, and was aged twenty-eight, born on the fifth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Zhongji; his grandfather was Qiyin, who held a prestige title of the upper seventh rank; and his father was Ming, a prefectural Prison Warden. His mother was née Wen, and his stepmother née Hu. His father alone was living. His elder brothers were Zhao, Hui, Liang, Nan, Gai, Gao, Yi, Rang, and Zi; his younger brother was Liang. He married a woman née Xue. He ranked forty-first in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 384th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ma Kun 馬坤 was registered in Tongzhou, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a military household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Shunqing, ranked sixth in family order, and was aged thirty, born on the thirteenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Yongyu; his grandfather was Wenshen, who held an honorary official title conferred for longevity; his father was Hui; and his mother was née Hu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jian, Xun, Jie, Xun, Che, and Zhuang. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née Li. He ranked fourteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 191st in the Metropolitan Examination.

潘壯，貫浙江紹興府山陰縣，民籍，府學生，治易經，字直卿，行一，年三十三，六月初三日生。曾祖玉〔壽官〕，祖鵬，父俊，母沈氏。重慶下，弟基、臺、望、𡌨、厓，娶王氏。浙江鄉試第十二名，會試第二百十九名。

陳褒，貫福建福寧州寧德縣，軍籍，國子生，治禮記，字邦進，行六，年三十六，十月十二日生。曾祖畊，祖和〔學正，贈刑部郎中〕，父宇，母鄭氏。具慶下，兄文、方、卞〔典膳〕、襃〔甲戌進士〕、雍〔監生〕，弟衮、充、言，娶黃氏，繼娶方氏。福建鄉試第三十七名，會試第二十五名。

陳讚，貫福建福州府長樂縣，民籍，直隸嘉定縣學教諭，治詩經，字允揚，行二，年三十四，十二月初三日生。曾祖植，祖宏煒，父德隆〔教諭，贈刑部主事〕，前母林氏，母丁氏〔贈安人〕，繼母郭氏。慈侍下，兄讓〔知縣〕、諤、謹〔府同知〕、謨、談〔知府〕、鑾〔署教諭，舉人〕，弟諧，娶卓氏。福建鄉試第十五名，會試第一百八十三名。

段續，貫陝西臨洮府蘭州，軍籍，山西陽曲縣人，國子生，治書經，字紹先，行一，年三十一，八月初五日生。曾祖椿，祖曠，父增，母于氏。慈侍下，弟繼、綬，娶陳氏，繼娶陳氏。陝西鄉試第六十三名，會試第一百七十七名。
translation_en:
Pan Zhuang, registered in Shanyin County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a prefectural school student. He specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zhiqing; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-three years old, born on the third day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yu [holder of an honorary longevity title], his grandfather Peng, his father Jun, and his mother née Shen. His grandfather and both parents were living. His younger brothers were Ji, Tai, Wang, Pi (𡌨) [?], and Ya. He married a woman née Wang. He placed twelfth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 219th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Bao, registered in Ningde County, Funing Subprefecture, Fujian, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Bangjin; he ranked sixth among his brothers and was thirty-six years old, born on the twelfth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Geng; his grandfather He [School Instructor, posthumously granted the title of Director in the Ministry of Justice]; his father Yu; and his mother née Zheng. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Wen, Fang, Bian [Steward], Bao (襃) [metropolitan graduate of the jiaxu year, 1514], and Yong [student of the Directorate of Education]; his younger brothers were Gun, Chong, and Yan. He married a woman née Huang and subsequently a woman née Fang. He placed thirty-seventh in the Fujian Provincial Examination and twenty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Zan, registered in Changle County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was Instructor at the county school of Jiading in the Metropolitan Region. He specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yunyang; he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-four years old, born on the third day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhi, his grandfather Hongwei, and his father Delong [Instructor, posthumously granted the title of Secretary in the Ministry of Justice]. His father's former wife was née Lin, his mother née Ding [posthumously granted the title of Lady of Repose], and his stepmother née Guo. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Rang [District Magistrate], E, Jin [Prefectural Vice Prefect], Mo, Tan [Prefect], and Luan [acting Instructor, provincial graduate]; his younger brother was Xie. He married a woman née Zhuo. He placed fifteenth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 183rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Duan Xu, registered in Lanzhou, Lintao Prefecture, Shaanxi, belonged to a military household and was originally from Yangqu County, Shanxi. He was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Shaoxian; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-one years old, born on the fifth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chun, his grandfather Kuang, his father Zeng, and his mother née Yu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Ji and Shou. He married a woman née Chen and subsequently another woman née Chen. He placed sixty-third in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 177th in the Metropolitan Examination.

藍田〔貫山東萊州府膠州即墨縣，軍籍，國子生，治易經，字玉甫，行一，年四十七，二月初六日生。〕曾祖福盛〔贈通議大夫、南京刑部右侍郎〕，祖銅〔贈通議大夫、南京刑部右侍郎〕，父章〔南京刑部右侍郎兼都察院左僉都御史，進階資善大夫〕，母徐氏〔封淑人〕。具慶下，弟囦、因〔官生〕，娶范氏，繼娶劉氏。山東鄉試第七十四名，會試第八名。

translation_en:
Wu Huiqi 吳會期 was registered in Qiongshan County, Qiongzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, in a civilian household. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Rites, he had the courtesy name Xingke and ranked second in family birth order. He was thirty-one years old, born on the eighth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jun; his grandfather, Kang, held an honorary office for longevity; his father was Xiao, and his mother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Jingqi, and his younger brothers were Yuanqi and Maoqi. He married a woman née Wang. He placed sixty-first in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and seventy-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lan Tian 藍田 was registered in Jimo County, Jiaozhou Subprefecture, Laizhou Prefecture, Shandong, in a military household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Yufu and ranked first in family birth order. He was forty-seven years old, born on the sixth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather, Fusheng, and grandfather, Tong, were each posthumously granted the titles Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Right Vice Minister of Justice at Nanjing. His father, Zhang, was Right Vice Minister of Justice at Nanjing, concurrently Left Assistant Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate, and had been advanced to the rank of Grand Master for Fostering Goodness. His mother, née Xu, was granted the title Lady of Kindness. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yuan and Yin; Yin was a student admitted by virtue of his father's office. He married a woman née Fan and subsequently a woman née Liu. He placed seventy-fourth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ye Fen 葉份 was registered in Wuyuan County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a civilian household. An attached student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Rites, he had the courtesy name Yuanxue and ranked fourth in family birth order. He was twenty-two years old, born on the eighteenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Guanwu; his grandfather, Zhaoyun, was granted the titles Gentleman for Service in the Literary Community and County Magistrate; his father, Tianqiu, was a Prefect; and his mother, née Wang, was granted the title Lady of Peace. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Tan, and his younger brothers were Qiao, Shi, Zhuo, Zong, Zuo, and Ren. He married a woman née Zhan. He placed seventy-fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 257th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Shiche 張時徹 was registered in Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Weijing and ranked twenty-sixth in family birth order. He was twenty-four years old, born on the twenty-fourth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gongye; his grandfather was Xu; his father was Bian, and his mother was née Sun. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Shiyu and Shixi. He married a woman née Chen. He placed forty-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and seventy-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

余承業〔貫四川眉州青神縣軍籍，縣學生，治詩經，字懋賢，行六，年三十四，四月二十六日生〕。曾祖祥〔戶部郎中，贈都察院右都御史〕，祖子偉〔文林郎，贈戶部主事〕，父寰〔戶部員外郎，進階奉直大夫〕，母程氏〔封太宜人〕。慈侍下，兄承芳〔監生〕、承恩〔官生，南京錦衣衛指揮僉事〕、承勛〔翰林院編修〕、承禮，娶趙氏。四川鄉試第七名，會試第三百四十八名。

茹鳴金〔貫太醫院醫籍，直隸無錫縣人，國子生，治詩經，字聲父，行四，年三十四，十二月十八日生〕。曾祖文中〔壽官〕，祖吉，父海〔封南京戶部主事〕，前母謝氏，母吳氏〔贈安人〕。永感下，兄鳴玉〔知州〕、鳴鸞、鳴鳳〔知縣，前光祿寺寺丞〕，娶陳氏，繼娶徐氏。順天府鄉試第三名，會試第四十四名。

徐廷傑〔貫浙江溫州府永嘉縣民籍，縣學生，治詩經，字獻忠，行三，年三十一，正月初七日生〕。曾祖承祖，祖端，父銳〔訓導〕，母王氏。具慶下，兄廷濬、廷宣，娶張氏。浙江鄉試第二十三名，會試第一百十三名。

崔允〔貫山西太原府代州民籍，大同府懷仁縣人，國子生，治書經，字懋信，行二，年三十八，四月初十日生〕。曾祖環〔贈京山侯〕，祖震〔封京山侯〕，父儒〔兵馬副指揮，贈都事，再加贈京山侯〕，母劉氏〔封孺人，贈太夫人〕。永感下，兄元〔奉天翊衛推誠宣力武臣、特進榮祿大夫、柱國、駙馬都尉、京山侯〕，弟充貢、充光、充寬、充況、充晃、充覺，娶王氏，繼娶郭氏、侯氏。山西鄉試第七十五名，會試第六十二名。
translation_en:
Yu Chengye was registered in a military household in Qingshen County, Meizhou, Sichuan. A county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Maoxian and ranked sixth in family order. He was aged thirty-four, born on the twenty-sixth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather Xiang was a Bureau Director in the Ministry of Revenue, posthumously granted the title of Right Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate; his grandfather Ziwei held the prestige title Gentleman for Rendering Service (wenlin lang) and was posthumously granted the title of Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue. His father Huan was a Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue, advanced to the prestige title Grand Master for Upright Service (fengzhi dafu). His mother, née Cheng, was granted the title Grand Lady of Suitability (tai yiren). His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Chengfang, an Imperial University student; Chengen, a student admitted by virtue of official privilege and an Assistant Commander of the Nanjing Embroidered-Uniform Guard; Chengxun, a Hanlin Academy Compiler; and Chengli. He married a woman née Zhao. He placed seventh in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 348th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ru Mingjin was registered in a medical household under the Imperial Medical Office and was a native of Wuxi County in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Shengfu and ranked fourth in family order. He was aged thirty-four, born on the eighteenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather Wenzhong held an honorary office conferred for longevity; his grandfather was Ji. His father Hai was granted the title of Secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue. His father's former wife was née Xie; his mother, née Wu, was posthumously granted the title Lady of Tranquility (anren). Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Mingyu, a Department Magistrate; Mingluan; and Mingfeng, a County Magistrate and formerly Assistant Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments. He married a woman née Chen and subsequently a woman née Xu. He placed third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and forty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Tingjie was registered in a civilian household in Yongjia County, Wenzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. A county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Xianzhong and ranked third in family order. He was aged thirty-one, born on the seventh day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Chengzu; his grandfather was Duan; his father Rui was an Assistant Instructor; and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Tingjun and Tingxuan. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed twenty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 113th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cui Yun was registered in a civilian household in Daizhou, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, and was a native of Huairen County, Datong Prefecture. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he had the courtesy name Maoxin and ranked second in family order. He was aged thirty-eight, born on the tenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather Huan was posthumously granted the title Marquis of Jingshan; his grandfather Zhen was granted the title Marquis of Jingshan. His father Ru was a Vice Commander of a Wardens' Office, posthumously granted the title of Office Manager and subsequently the additional title Marquis of Jingshan. His mother, née Liu, was granted the title Lady (ruren) and posthumously the title Grand Lady (tai furen). Both parents were deceased. His elder brother Yuan held the titles Military Servitor Who Upholds Heaven, Assists in Defense, Extends Sincerity, and Exerts His Strength; Grand Master for Glorious Happiness with Special Advancement; Pillar of State; Chief Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law; and Marquis of Jingshan. His younger brothers were Chonggong, Chongguang, Chongkuan, Chongkuang, Chonghuang, and Chongjue. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently women née Guo and née Hou. He placed seventy-fifth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and sixty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Ting, courtesy name Zijia, was registered in a military household in Jiajiang County, Jiading Subprefecture, Sichuan. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the ninth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather Wenqing was a county-school Instructor; his grandfather Lan received the honorary title of Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue; and his father Fengzhu was an Assistant Subprefect. His father's former wife was née Jiang, his mother née Li, and his stepmother née Jiang. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Shu, an Instructor in the yin-yang school, and Lin, a holder of a seventh-rank prestige title; his younger brothers were Xiang, Xu, and Lian. He was betrothed to a woman née Li and married a woman née Luo. He ranked fourth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 245th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Feng Chengfang, courtesy name Shili, was registered in an officer household of the Guilin Central Guard, Guangxi. A Confucian scholar specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the thirteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather Xing was an Assistant Commander; his grandfather was Ning and his father Gao. His mother was née Zhang and his stepmother née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Chengyin, and his wife was née Xie. He ranked fourteenth in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and 146th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Han, courtesy name Shide, was registered in a civilian household in Changshu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged forty-two, and born on the second day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fu; his grandfather Da was posthumously granted the title of Secretary in the Ministry of Justice; and his father Hai was a Prefect, advanced in prestige rank to Grand Master of the Second Rank (yazhong dafu). His legal mother was née Zhu, who received the title of Lady of Peace, and his birth mother was née Zhou. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers Fan and Yu were students of the Directorate of Education. He married a woman née Qian and subsequently a woman née Shi. He ranked sixty-sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and ninety-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Feng'ao, courtesy name Borui, was registered in a civilian household in Chengdu County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the eleventh day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather Desheng held an honorary official title granted for longevity; his grandfather was Gao and his father Shixin. His mother was née Ruan. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brother was Fengyang, and his wife was née Mo. He ranked ninth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 295th in the Metropolitan Examination.

陸冕〔貫直隸蘇州府崑山縣民籍，國子生，治易經，字子端，行二，年三十六，正月十六日生〕。曾祖春，祖實，父士達〔承事郎〕，母吳氏，繼母顧氏。永感下。兄冠，弟旒、弁，娶劉氏。應天府鄉試第一百二十一名，會試第六十三名。

屠應坤〔貫浙江嘉興府平湖縣人，營州衛軍籍，國子生，治書經，字文厚，行二，年三十一，正月二十日生〕。曾祖湘〔贈刑部尚書〕，祖機〔贈刑部尚書〕，父勲〔刑部尚書，贈太保，謚康僖〕，嫡母陳氏〔贈夫人〕、林氏、畢氏〔封夫人〕，生母楊氏。慈侍下。兄應奎〔布政司叅議〕、應壁〔主事〕、應垕〔監察御史〕、應堂、應塤〔前禮部郎中〕，弟應埲、應壇、應坼、應坊、應埈、應埏，娶陸氏。順天府鄉試第二十四名，會試第一百七十六名。

曾存仁〔貫江西吉安府吉水縣民籍，縣學附學生，治書經，字懋遠，行一，年三十四，三月二十五日生〕。曾祖光偉，祖克紹，父伯崇，母周氏。具慶下。弟侃、价、傅，娶羅氏。江西鄉試第五十七名，會試第二百四十八名。

張文憲〔貫武功右衛軍籍，浙江崇德縣人，國子生，治詩經，字廷鑒，行五，年三十三，三月初九日生〕。曾祖如成，祖善〔壽官〕，父溥，前母薛氏，母李氏。永感下。兄文英、文睿、文奇、文華，弟文奎，娶隨氏，繼娶陳氏。順天府鄉試第四十二名，會試第一百十名。
translation_en:
Lu Mian 陸冕, courtesy name Ziduan, was registered in the civilian category in Kunshan County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in birth order and aged thirty-six, born on the sixteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chun; his grandfather, Shi; and his father, Shida, a Gentleman for Rendering Service. His mother was née Wu and his stepmother née Gu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Guan, and his younger brothers were Liu and Bian. He married a woman née Liu. He placed 121st in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 63rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tu Yingkun 屠應坤, courtesy name Wenhou, was a native of Pinghu County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, registered in the military category under Yingzhou Guard. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was second in birth order and aged thirty-one, born on the twentieth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather, Xiang, and grandfather, Ji, were both posthumously appointed Minister of Justice. His father, Xun, was Minister of Justice, posthumously appointed Grand Guardian and given the posthumous name Kangxi. His legal mothers were née Chen, posthumously granted the title Lady; née Lin; and née Bi, granted the title Lady. His birth mother was née Yang. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Yingkui, an Administrative Assistant in a Provincial Administration Commission; Yingbi, a Secretary; Yinghou, an Investigating Censor; Yingtang; and Yingxun, formerly a Bureau Director in the Ministry of Rites. His younger brothers were Yingbeng, Yingtan, Yingche, Yingfang, Yingjun, and Yingshan. He married a woman née Lu. He placed 24th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 176th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zeng Cunren 曾存仁, courtesy name Maoyuan, was registered in the civilian category in Jishui County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi. An additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order and aged thirty-four, born on the twenty-fifth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Guangwei; his grandfather, Keshao; his father, Bochong; and his mother, née Zhou. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Kan, Jie, and Fu. He married a woman née Luo. He placed 57th in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 248th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Wenxian 張文憲, courtesy name Tingjian, was registered in the military category under Wugong Right Guard and was a native of Chongde County, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was fifth in birth order and aged thirty-three, born on the ninth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rucheng; his grandfather, Shan, held an honorary official title for longevity; and his father was Pu. His father’s former wife was née Xue, and his mother was née Li. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Wenying, Wenrui, Wenqi, and Wenhua, and his younger brother was Wenkui. He married a woman née Sui and subsequently a woman née Chen. He placed 42nd in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 110th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Qiao Qi, courtesy name Jingfu, was registered in a civilian household in Zhuozhou, Shuntian Prefecture. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked thirteenth in family birth order and was thirty-five years old, born on the twenty-ninth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Li, his grandfather Xing, his father Jiang, and his mother née Zhao; both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Gong, Deputy Battalion Commander in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard; Lu; Feng; Peng; Yun; Tian; Chuan; Shen; Defu; and Delu. His younger brother was Hu, and his wife was née Zhang. He placed 132nd in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 285th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wei Yingzhao, courtesy name Weihan, was registered in a civilian household in Wu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked fourth in family birth order and was thirty-nine years old, born on the twelfth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qin, his grandfather Wensheng, his father Zhining, a Judge, and his mother née Yuan. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Yingkui, Yinglong, and Yingzhou; his younger brothers were Yingqi and Yingzeng. His wife was née Jiang. He placed 106th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 251st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu An, courtesy name Zhenwen, was registered in a civilian household in Chongren County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi. A county government school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked second in family birth order and was thirty-six years old, born on the twenty-sixth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ziyi; his grandfather Sui, an Assistant Prefect; and his father Chong, a Director of a county government school, posthumously appointed Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Rites. His legal mothers were née Xiong, née Lu, and née Yang, the last granted the title Grand Lady (Tai Ruren); his birth mother was née Chen. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Zui, Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Rites, and Jun, a Bureau Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice. His younger brother was Yan. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née Chen. He placed thirty-eighth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and eighty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jin Xian, courtesy name Bangyi, was registered in a civilian household in Kunshan County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked third in family birth order and was thirty-eight years old, born on the sixteenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Mao, who held an honorary official title for longevity; his grandfather was Shen; his father was Yan, an Assistant Instructor; and his mother was née Yang. His father was living, and his mother was deceased. His elder brothers were Zhong and En; his younger brothers were Que and Wei. His wife was née Chen. He placed fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 231st in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Chen Guan, courtesy name Duanqing, was registered in a military household in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-six, born on the twenty-second day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Ming; his grandfather, Cong, was a County Registrar posthumously appointed Investigating Censor; his father, Kui, was Left Provincial Administration Commissioner; and his mother, née Peng, held the title Lady (Ruren) by imperial grant. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed thirty-second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 247th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ji Biao, courtesy name Minghe, was registered in a military household attached to the Raozhou Guard Chiliad in Jiangxi and was a native of Shanyang County in the directly administered region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked fifteenth among his brothers and was aged twenty-six, born on the sixteenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Xin'an; his grandfather, Tianjue; his father, Fengxiang; and his mother, née Jiang. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brothers were Zong, Yue, and Quan, and his younger brother was Fang. He married a woman née Li. He placed twenty-ninth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 101st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Tang, courtesy name Kentang, was registered in a civilian household in Changshu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region. A county school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged twenty-two, born on the twenty-sixth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Sheng; his grandfather, Nan; his father, Kun; and his mother, née Yu. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Bo. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed eighty-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 214th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Ge, courtesy name Shiyan, was registered in a civilian household in Xindu County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Changes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged forty-one, born on the eleventh day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather, Qing, was a County Magistrate; his grandfather was Jing; his father, Yuwen, held the honorary title Official for Righteousness (yiguan); and his mother was née Zhou. His parents and grandparents were deceased. His younger brother was Gui. He married a woman née Xu. He placed second in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 230th in the Metropolitan Examination.
