translation_en:
Sima Tai, courtesy name Luzhan, was registered in a military household of the Embroidered-uniform Guard in Nanjing and was a native of Xianning County, Shaanxi. An supplementary student at the Yingtian Prefectural School specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-two, born on the seventeenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xun, his grandfather Zhen, his father Long, and his mother née Zhang. His mother alone was still living. His younger brothers were Heng, Song, and Hua, and his wife was née Shen. He placed eighty-seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 337th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Ren, courtesy name Shiyuan, was registered in a civilian household in Quzhou County, Guangping Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-two, born on the seventh day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhi, his grandfather Biao, and his father Mei, an official awaiting selection for appointment. His father's former wife was née Zhang, and his mother was née Lü. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Yi, his younger brothers Fang and Xiao, and his wife was née Fang. He placed 116th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 321st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Zonggu, courtesy name Benchun, was registered in a military household in Shishou County, Jingzhou Prefecture, Huguang. A county school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked seventh among his brothers and was aged thirty-two, born on the seventh day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Angong, his grandfather Lun, an Assistant Instructor, his father Daoqi, and his mother née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brother Zongzai was a Department Magistrate; his younger brothers were Zongshi, Zongzheng, Zongdun, and Zonghui, and his wife was née Zeng. He placed ninth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 287th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Liangce, courtesy name Yuting, was registered in a military household in Suizhou, De'an Prefecture, Huguang. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-nine, born on the twenty-second day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chun, his grandfather Qing, his father Jin, who held an honorary official title for longevity, and his mother née Ma. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Liangfan, and his wife was née Zhang. He placed second in the Huguang Provincial Examination and twenty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Han 汪漢 was registered in Huaining County, Anqing Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a civilian household. A county school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Yuanzhi, ranked first among his brothers, and was aged forty-one, born on the thirteenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Yanheng; his grandfather, Xiaoqi; and his father, Rong. His father's former wife was née Qian, and his mother was née Zhan. Both parents were deceased. His wife was née Chen. He placed twenty-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twelfth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Deyou 趙得祐 was registered in Lulong County, Yongping Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a civilian household. A county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Yuanji, ranked second among his brothers, and was aged thirty-three, born on the twenty-third day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather, Zhong, was an Investigating Censor, advanced in prestige rank to Grand Master of Central Compliance; his grandfather, Ding, was a District Magistrate; and his father was Zhang. His mother was née Hu, and his stepmother was née Xu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Deshou; his younger brothers were Dehui, Defu, Delu, Dezhen, Dexiang, Dehu, Deqi, Dezuo, Deyu, Dexi, Deli, Deyou [?], and Deli [repeated in the transcription]. His wife was née Yu. He placed forty-fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 296th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ke Weiqi 柯維騏 was registered in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he had the courtesy name Qichun, ranked fourth among his brothers, and was aged twenty-seven, born on the second day of the second month. His great-grandfather, Jun, held an honorary official title for longevity; his grandfather, Xuan, was posthumously appointed Case Reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review; and his father, Ying, was a Prefect. His mother, née Jiang, was invested with the title of Lady (ruren). His mother alone was living. His elder brothers were Weixiong, a Messenger in the Office of Transmission; Weipi, a tribute scholar (gongshi); and Weiyu. His younger brothers were Weifan and Weihan. His wife was née Gu. He placed twenty-fourth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and forty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Yi 王億 was registered in Xian County, Hejian Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he had the courtesy name Wancheng, ranked first among his brothers, and was aged thirty-four, born on the fifteenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Shou; his grandfather, Yu; and his father, Ming. His mother was née Liu, and his stepmother was née Dong. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Zhong, and his wife was née Sun. He placed forty-eighth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 263rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wu Yunlu, registered in Nanhai County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Tianshen. Third in family order, he was thirty-two years old and was born on the twenty-sixth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Jiaxun; his grandfather was Xin; and his father, Lian, was a magistrate, honorifically invested as acting vice director in the Ministry of Revenue and granted the right to wear fourth-rank official attire. His mother, née He, was invested as Lady of Peace (anren). His father alone survived. His elder brothers were Yunzhen, a prefect, and Yunli; his younger brothers were Yunyu, a tribute scholar (gongshi), and Yunzhi. He married a woman née Ma. He placed seventh in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 204th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Huai, registered in Dantu County, Zhenjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Zonghai. Third in family order, he was thirty-four years old and was born on the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Jing; his grandfather, Yi, held the honorary designation of Official for Righteousness (yiguan); his father was Zhen; and his mother was née Zhou. His father alone survived. His elder brother was Lan; his younger brothers were Shu, Yue, and Lian. He married a woman née Yang and subsequently a woman née Yu. He placed second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 259th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Gan, registered in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Liangfu. Thirty-ninth in family order, he was forty-one years old and was born on the thirteenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Keheng; his grandfather, Youzhi, was honorifically invested as investigating censor; and his father, Yuan, was administration vice commissioner of the left in a Provincial Administration Commission, promoted to the prestige rank of Grand Master of the Palace (dazhong dafu). His mother, née Ying, was invested as Lady of Virtue (shuren). Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Xiang, a prefect; Dong, a prefect; and Song. His younger brothers were Pan, an official awaiting selection for appointment, and Gai. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née Zhu. He placed fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 139th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Huai was registered in a civilian household in Shangyuan County, Yingtian Prefecture, and was originally from Huai’an County, Fujian. He was a prefectural government student specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Weidong. Fourth in family order, he was twenty-nine years old and was born on the thirteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Gong; his grandfather was Siren; and his father was Ming. His father’s former wife was née Gu, and his mother was née Yu. His mother alone survived. His elder brothers were Pu, Hong, and Hao; his younger brothers were Chun, Lian, Jun, and Chao. He married a woman née Ni. He placed seventy-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 206th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Dayong 張大用 was registered in a civilian household in Yuechi County, Shunqing Prefecture, Sichuan. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Rites, he had the courtesy name Xingzhi, ranked first among his brothers, and was aged twenty-four, born on the fourth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenlin, an honorary official for public benefaction; his grandfather was Rui, a county vice magistrate; his father was Shouren; and his mother was née Ma. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brother was Dafu, and his wife was née Chen. He placed forty-eighth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 189th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shi Chen 史臣 was registered in a civilian household in Wujiang County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Bangzhi, ranked first among his brothers, and was aged fifty, born on the twenty-eighth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Heng, an honorary official for public benefaction; his grandfather was Jian; his father was Yongxi, an Imperial University student; and his mother was née Wu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Xiang, a ceremonial usher, and Kui. His wife was née Tao. He placed twenty-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 267th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Guowei 張國維 was registered in a civilian household in Dingyuan County, Fengyang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and was a native of Shanghai County. A county school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he had the courtesy name Chongsi [?], ranked second among his brothers, and was aged thirty-five, born on the eighteenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yu; his grandfather was Jin, a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the jiashen year; his father was Yongtai, a metropolitan graduate of the wuchen year; and his mother was née Yuan. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Guoji, a tribute scholar (gongshi), and his younger brother was Guozheng. His wife was née Qian. He placed sixty-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and tenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Du 王度 was registered in a civilian household in Linhai County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was a native of Ninghai County. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Lüsheng, ranked second among his brothers, and was aged thirty-three, born on the twenty-third day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zong, a prefect posthumously awarded the titles Grand Master for Central Deliberation and Governance-Assisting Governor (zanzhi yin); his grandfather was Wen, a right administration vice commissioner in a Provincial Administration Commission; his father was Yuan; his mother was née Chen; and his stepmother was née Fan. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Yong, and his younger brothers were Fu, Luan, Yue, Jin, Rui, and Kai. His wife was née Lü. He placed twenty-sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and sixty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Li Rizhang, registered in a civilian household in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was an supplementary student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Shangjiong. He ranked fourth among his brothers and was twenty-seven years old, born on the twelfth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Sheng; his grandfather was Ping, an honorary official recognized for longevity; his father was Ting, an Assistant Instructor; and his mother was née Xu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Chen, an official awaiting appointment, Xun, and Rixuan; his younger brothers were Rijiu, Riji, and Rijin. His wife was née Dong. He placed ninety-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 194th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Chen, registered in a civilian household in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a county-school student. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Gongbi. He ranked fourth among his brothers and was thirty-one years old, born on the second day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Zhongxuan; his grandfather was Biao; his father was Dawu; and his mother was née Zhang. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brother was Chao, and his wife was née Wei. He placed 171st in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 142nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Yi, registered in a military household in Wuhu County, Taiping Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Shibo. He ranked first among his brothers and was twenty-eight years old, born on the second day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Lian; his grandfather was Wenzuo; his father was Ji; and his mother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Shu and Li. His wife was née Ding; his subsequent wife was née Qin. He placed 106th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 274th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Pin, registered in a military household in Baling County, Yuezhou Prefecture, Huguang, was a county-school student. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Guoxin. He ranked fourth among his brothers and was thirty years old, born on the third day of the intercalary fifth month. His great-grandfather was Kai; his grandfather was Zhili, a Chief Clerk; his father was Kui; his mother was née Liu; and his stepmother was née Lei. His father and stepmother were living. His younger brothers were Yao and Po, and his wife was née Li. He placed seventh in the Huguang Provincial Examination and seventy-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Yu Zhou, registered in an artisan household of the Yulin Front Guard and originally from Putian County, Fujian, was an added-quota student of the Shuntian Prefectural School specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Ziju; he ranked third among his brothers and was aged twenty-five, born on the thirteenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Yanzhi; his grandfather was Daoyao, an honorary official recognized for public benefactions; and his father was Yizheng, a County Magistrate. His father's former wife was née Lin, and his mother was née Li. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Zhun and Ju, and his younger brother was Ting. He married a woman née Xie. He placed twelfth in the Shuntian Prefectural Provincial Examination and 299th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Li, registered in a civilian household in Nanchong County, Shunqing Prefecture, Sichuan, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Yifu; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-four, born on the second day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Hai, a County Vice Magistrate; his grandfather was Li, a County Magistrate; and his father was Chun. His mother and stepmother were both née Yu. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Lu, Jian, Du, Xu, Wu, Qianheng, Mengheng, Jinming, and Geng. He married a woman née Wang. He placed twenty-third in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 159th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Tingmei, registered in a military household in Huanggang County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Record of Rites. His courtesy name was Zhihe; he ranked fourth among his brothers and was aged thirty-eight, born on the nineteenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Simin, a Subprefectural Vice Magistrate; his grandfather was Wenkai, granted the honorary title of County Magistrate; and his father was Lin, a County Magistrate. His mother, née Hu, had been granted the title of Lady of the Ninth Rank. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Tinglu, a tribute student, and Tingji; his younger brothers were Tingzhao, Tingru, a tribute student, Tingchen, a former Subprefectural Magistrate, Tinghuai, Tingwu, and Tingnan. He married a woman née Zhou and subsequently a woman née He. He placed sixteenth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 223rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fu Jiong, registered in a civilian household in Jinxian County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Chaojin; he ranked twelfth among his brothers and was aged thirty-one, born on the eleventh day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Shiyan; his grandfather was Yuchuan; his father was Song; and his mother was née Ji. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brother was Can, a tribute student. He married a woman née Wan. He placed ninety-first in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 106th in the Metropolitan Examination.

曹曙〔貫山東兖州府濟寧州民籍，國子生，治詩經，字明之，行四，年三十八，十一月初一日生〕。曾祖遵，祖信，父清〔壽官〕，前母徐氏，母葉氏，繼母羅氏。具慶下，兄旺〔七品散官〕、晢，弟曦、昛，娶劉氏。山東鄉試第十四名，會試第三百八十三名。

林應標〔貫福建興化府莆田縣民籍，府學附學生，治書經，字君表，行一，年二十五，正月二十六日生〕。曾祖叔孟〔義官〕，祖與飾，父師頤，母俞氏，繼母余氏。具慶下，娶陳氏。福建鄉試第二十八名，會試第六十五名。

黃瓚〔貫福建泉州府南安縣民籍，國子生，治易經，字宗獻，行一，年三十四，八月初十日生〕。曾祖孟銘，祖復祖，父邦胤〔義官〕，母何氏。慈侍下，弟瑀、綸、統，娶丘氏。福建鄉試第八十二名，會試第一百四十五名。

李騰霄〔貫山西太原府盂縣民籍，國子生，治書經，字子冲，行三，年三十三，九月二十日生〕。曾祖諫，祖璧〔州判官〕，父軾，母郭氏。具慶下，兄騰雲、騰漢，弟騰霖，娶韓氏。山西鄉試第四十九名，會試第二百九十七名。
translation_en:
Cao Shu, courtesy name Mingzhi, was registered in a civilian household in Jining Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes, he was fourth in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the first day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zun; his grandfather was Xin; and his father was Qing, who held an honorary title for longevity. His father’s former wife was née Xu, his mother was née Ye, and his stepmother was née Luo. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Wang, a prestige official of the seventh rank, and Zhe; his younger brothers were Xi and Ju. His wife was née Liu. He placed fourteenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 383rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Yingbiao, courtesy name Junbiao, was registered in a civilian household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian. An additional student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-five, and born on the twenty-sixth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shumeng, who held the honorary title of Official for Righteousness; his grandfather was Yushi; his father was Shiyi; his mother was née Yu 俞; and his stepmother was née Yu 余. Both parents were living. His wife was née Chen. He placed twenty-eighth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and sixty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Zan, courtesy name Zongxian, was registered in a civilian household in Nan’an County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the tenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Mengming; his grandfather was Fuzu; his father was Bangyin, who held the honorary title of Official for Righteousness; and his mother was née He. His father was deceased, and he attended his living mother. His younger brothers were Yu, Lun, and Tong. His wife was née Qiu. He placed eighty-second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 145th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Tengxiao, courtesy name Zichong, was registered in a civilian household in Yu County, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the twentieth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jian; his grandfather was Bi, a Subprefectural Assistant Judge; his father was Shi; and his mother was née Guo. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Tengyun and Tenghan; his younger brother was Tenglin. His wife was née Han. He placed forty-ninth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 297th in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
馬蓿〔貫山西振武衛官籍，直隸當塗縣人，國子生，治易經，字敏卿，行四，年三十五，八月二十七日生〕。曾祖才〔百戶〕，祖翱〔副千戶〕，父銘〔副千戶〕，嫡母費氏〔封宜人〕，繼母張氏，生母李氏。慈侍下，兄英〔副千戶〕、芹、芠，弟萬、蕃、茂，娶李氏。山西鄉試第二十名，會試第一百五十六名。

黃禎〔貫山東青州府安丘縣民籍，縣學生，治春秋，字德兆，行三，年三十四，正月二十四日生〕。曾祖英，祖泰〔知縣〕，父錦，母高氏。重慶下，兄祐、祚，弟祥、禕、祿，娶周氏，繼娶周氏。山東鄉試第二名，會試第十八名。

駱顒〔貫四川叙州府富順縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字君孚，行一，年二十八，二月十七日生〕。曾祖思全，祖本政〔主簿〕，父清高，前母宋氏、戴氏，母羅氏。慈侍下，弟頌，娶王氏。四川鄉試第五十五名，會試第四十八名。

蕭璆〔貫湖廣辰州衛軍籍，江西廬陵縣人，國子生，治詩經，字子鳴，行七，年二十八，七月二十八日生〕。曾祖鑰，祖致中，父佐〔府照磨〕，前母沈氏，母張氏。具慶下，兄瑞、琰、玨、璋、琨、珂，娶施氏，繼娶賈氏。湖廣鄉試第十九名，會試第二百三十七名。
translation_en:
Ma Xu 馬蓿, courtesy name Minqing, was registered in an officer household in Zhenwu Guard, Shanxi, and was a native of Dangtu County in Zhili. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was fourth in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the twenty-seventh day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cai, a Company Commander; his grandfather was Ao, a Vice Battalion Commander; and his father was Ming, also a Vice Battalion Commander. His father's principal wife, Lady Fei, was granted the title Lady of Suitability; his stepmother was Lady Zhang, and his birth mother was Lady Li. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Ying, a Vice Battalion Commander, Qin, and Wen; his younger brothers were Wan, Fan, and Mao. He married Lady Li. He placed twentieth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 156th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Zhen 黃禎, courtesy name Dezhao, was registered in a civilian household in Anqiu County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong. A county school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the twenty-fourth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ying; his grandfather was Tai, a County Magistrate; his father was Jin, and his mother was Lady Gao. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brothers were You and Zuo; his younger brothers were Xiang, Yi, and Lu. He married Lady Zhou and subsequently another Lady Zhou. He placed second in the Shandong Provincial Examination and eighteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Luo Yong 駱顒, courtesy name Junfu, was registered in a civilian household in Fushun County, Xuzhou Prefecture, Sichuan. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the seventeenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Siquan; his grandfather was Benzheng, a Registrar; and his father was Qinggao. His father's former wives were Lady Song and Lady Dai; his mother was Lady Luo. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brother was Song. He married Lady Wang. He placed fifty-fifth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and forty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiao Qiu 蕭璆, courtesy name Ziming, was registered in a military household in Chenzhou Guard, Huguang, and was a native of Luling County, Jiangxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was seventh in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the twenty-eighth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yue; his grandfather was Zhizhong; and his father was Zuo, a Prefectural Records Examiner. His father's former wife was Lady Shen; his mother was Lady Zhang. Both his parents were living. His elder brothers were Rui, Yan, Jue, Zhang, Kun, and Ke. He married Lady Shi and subsequently Lady Jia. He placed nineteenth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 237th in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
劉珂〔貫直隸大名府開州，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字伯璿，行一，年四十二，正月初六日生〕。曾祖聚，祖整，父浩，母傅氏。慈侍下，弟玦、璐、瑁，娶孫氏，繼娶董氏。順天府鄉試第三名，會試第一百五十五名。

李清〔貫湖廣常德府龍陽縣，軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字介卿，行一，年三十二，四月十四日生〕。曾祖仁玉，祖聸〔壽官〕，父思文〔教授〕，母高氏，繼母林氏。具慶下，弟淑，娶袁氏。湖廣鄉試第六十名，會試第三百九十名。

陳之良〔貫湖廣德安府隨州，民籍，應山縣人，國子生，治詩經，字伯善，行一，年三十一，閏五月十七日生〕。曾祖間，祖璣〔壽官〕，父儼〔訓導〕，母劉氏。永感下，弟之輔〔貢士〕、之弼、之維、之佑，娶米氏。湖廣鄉試第五十二名，會試第二百八十二名。

王松〔貫順天府固安縣，民籍，國子生，治書經，字汝節，行十，年三十，十月初八日生〕。曾祖徽，祖皷〔知縣〕，父鸞〔主簿〕，前母辛氏，母董氏，繼母史氏。具慶下，兄檠、幹、棟〔主簿〕、桂、楫〔大使〕、栻、朴、桓、權、機、祝，弟梯，娶曹氏，繼娶賈氏。順天府鄉試第一百二十七名，會試第九十六名。
translation_en:
Liu Ke 劉珂, registered in a civilian household in Kaizhou, Daming Prefecture, Zhili, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Boxuan; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged forty-two, born on the sixth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ju, his grandfather Zheng, and his father Hao; his mother was née Fu. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brothers were Jue, Lu, and Mao. He married a woman née Sun and subsequently a woman née Dong. He placed third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 155th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Qing 李清, registered in a military household in Longyang County, Changde Prefecture, Huguang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Jieqing; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-two, born on the fourteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Renyu, his grandfather Dan (holder of an honorary rank for longevity), and his father Siwen (a Prefectural School Instructor); his mother was née Gao and his stepmother née Lin. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Shu. He married a woman née Yuan. He placed sixtieth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 390th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Zhiliang 陳之良, registered in a civilian household in Suizhou, De'an Prefecture, Huguang, and originally from Yingshan County, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Boshan; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-one, born on the seventeenth day of the intercalary fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jian, his grandfather Ji (holder of an honorary rank for longevity), and his father Yan (an Assistant Instructor); his mother was née Liu. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Zhifu (a tribute scholar), Zhibi, Zhiwei, and Zhiyou. He married a woman née Mi. He placed fifty-second in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 282nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Song 王松, registered in a civilian household in Gu'an County, Shuntian Prefecture, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Rujie; he ranked tenth among his brothers and was aged thirty, born on the eighth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hui, his grandfather Gu (a District Magistrate), and his father Luan (a Registrar). His father's former wife was née Xin, his mother née Dong, and his stepmother née Shi. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Qing, Gan, Dong (a Registrar), Gui, Ji (a Commissioner), Shi, Pu, Huan, Quan, Ji, and Zhu; his younger brother was Ti. He married a woman née Cao and subsequently a woman née Jia. He placed 127th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and ninety-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Hu Wenkui, registered in an artisan household in Leiyang County, Hengzhou Prefecture, Huguang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Ruzhang; he ranked sixth in his family and was forty years old, born on the twenty-sixth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zirong; his grandfather, Zheng; and his father, Lian, posthumously appointed Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue. His mother, née Chen, was granted the title Lady of Tranquility. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Wenyu, Wenbi (Provincial Surveillance Commissioner), and Wendan (an honorary official recognized for public benefactions). He married a woman née Xu and subsequently a woman née Li. He placed fifteenth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 209th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dai Jingfu, registered in a civilian household in Xiuning County, Huizhou Prefecture, Zhili, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Yingshan; he ranked seventeenth in his family and was forty-five years old, born on the third day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was He; his grandfather, Jinglin; his father, Qingchun; and his mother, née Cheng. His mother alone survived. His elder brothers were Ying'ang, Yingxuan, Yingchuan, Yingwan, and Yingwang. He married a woman née Wu. He placed eighty-first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 281st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Gengqi, registered in a military household in Leting County, Luanzhou, Yongping Prefecture, Zhili, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Renshu; he ranked first in his family and was twenty-four years old, born on the twenty-seventh day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bin (holder of an honorary rank for longevity); his grandfather, Jing (Office Manager); his father, Liang; his mother, née Wang; and his stepmother, née Lin. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Jiuchou, Genglin 耿麟, Gengpeng, Gengkun, Genglin 耿麐, Gengfeng, and Gengguang. He married a woman née Yu. He placed fiftieth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 233rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Fang, registered in a civilian household in Fenghua County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zixuan; he ranked fourth in his family and was thirty-two years old, born on the eleventh day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuanjiao; his grandfather, Pu; his father, Xun; and his mother, née Qian. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zhen and Quan; his younger brothers were Qin, Feng, Zhao, and Bin. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed sixty-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 148th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wu Peng was registered in a civilian household in Xiushui County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was a native of Haining County. A prefectural government school student, he specialized in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Wanli; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged twenty-four, born on the twenty-first day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yi; his grandfather, Zhao, was an unranked clerk; his father was Fang, and his mother was née Huang. Both parents were living. His younger brother was He, and his wife was née Dai. He placed fifty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 168th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Qiao was registered in a civilian household in Guangchang County, Jianchang Prefecture, Jiangxi. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Ziqian; he ranked twenty-second among his brothers and was aged thirty-nine, born on the twenty-eighth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ziyu; his grandfather, Sheng, was a county vice magistrate; his father was Qing, and his mother was née Fu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Shi, Xin, Xiang, Fang, Shun, Gui, Zhi (a registrar), Bang, Shu, and Xi [? name divisions uncertain]; his younger brothers were Mao, Shou, and Qi. He married a woman née He and subsequently a woman née Zeng. He placed twenty-second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 373rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lü Zhang was registered in an officer household of the Embroidered-uniform Guard and was a native of Jingmen Subprefecture, Huguang. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Shangde; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-nine, born on the tenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jian; his grandfather, Tong, was posthumously granted the title of battalion commander; his father, Hai, was a full battalion commander. His mother, née Sun, was posthumously granted the title Lady of Suitability; his stepmother, née Zhang, was granted the same title. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His younger brother was Jie, and his wife was née Wang. He placed eleventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Ji was registered in a civilian household in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian. An additional student of the prefectural government school, he specialized in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Shiyong; he ranked fifth among his brothers and was aged twenty-four, born on the seventeenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Weichu; his grandfather, Jingyang, was posthumously granted the title of secretary in the Ministry of Revenue; his father, Tan, was a prefect. His father's former wife, née Lin, was granted the title Lady of Peace; his mother was née Tao. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Lun, who had been granted the right to wear official cap and girdle under applicable regulations; Yi, a tribute scholar; Shou, a station master; and Zuan. His wife was née Lin. He placed seventieth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and forty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

周鰲〔貫直隸常州府江陰縣民籍，國子生，治書經，字巨夫，行二，年三十六，八月初九日生〕。曾祖鑑，祖繹，父庭芝，嫡母楊氏，生母孫氏。慈侍下，兄鯨，弟鯤、鮪、鯢、鱸、魴、鯁、鱅。娶呉氏。應天府鄉試第二十四名，會試第二百六十一名。

屠倬〔貫浙江寧波府鄞縣民籍，國子生，治易經，字文卿，行三十二，年三十七，十二月二十四日生〕。曾祖子良，祖琛〔教諭〕，父湖〔贈監察御史〕，母方氏〔贈孺人〕。永感下，兄傭、俁、佑、佺、僑〔監察御史〕，弟儼、佶。娶姚氏。浙江鄉試第二十五名，會試第二百六十四名。

李枝〔貫河南開封府扶溝縣軍籍，府學生，治詩經，字伯材，行三，年三十三，九月二十七日生〕。曾祖忠，祖正〔贈戶部員外郎〕，父夢陽〔提學副使〕，母左氏。嚴侍下，兄根〔義官〕、木〔貢士〕，弟友竹〔驛丞〕、樹、楚、梁、柱。娶冀氏。河南鄉試第六十八名，會試第一百三十三名。
translation_en:
Wang Ping 王評, registered in a civilian household in Changshu County, Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shenyan; he ranked second in his family and was aged thirty-six, born on the twenty-seventh day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Yan, his grandfather Xi, his father Zongbiao, and his mother née Yao. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Huai (Assistant Prefect of Shuntian Prefecture), Gui, Qi, Song, Liu 留 (a tribute scholar), Zhao, Liu 柳, and Fang; his younger brothers were Quan, Lun, Qiao, Mo, Yu, Dong, Fu, and Zan. He married a woman née Ji and subsequently a woman née Liu. He placed seventy-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 138th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Ao 周鰲, registered in a civilian household in Jiangyin County, Changzhou Prefecture, Zhili, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Jufu; he ranked second in his family and was aged thirty-six, born on the ninth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Jian, his grandfather Yi, and his father Tingzhi; his father's principal wife was née Yang, and his birth mother was née Sun. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brother was Jing; his younger brothers were Kun, Wei, Ni, Lu, Fang, Geng, and Yong. He married a woman née Wu. He placed twenty-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 261st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tu Zhuo 屠倬, registered in a civilian household in Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Wenqing; he ranked thirty-second in his family and was aged thirty-seven, born on the twenty-fourth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Ziliang; his grandfather Chen was an Instructor; his father Hu was posthumously granted the title of Investigating Censor; and his mother, née Fang, was posthumously granted the title of Lady (Ruren). Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Yong, Yu, You, Quan, and Qiao (an Investigating Censor); his younger brothers were Yan and Ji. He married a woman née Yao. He placed twenty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 264th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Zhi 李枝, registered in a military household in Fugou County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Bocai; he ranked third in his family and was aged thirty-three, born on the twenty-seventh day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Zhong; his grandfather Zheng was posthumously granted the title of Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue; his father Mengyang was a Surveillance Vice Commissioner in charge of education; and his mother was née Zuo. His mother was deceased, and he attended his surviving father. His elder brothers were Gen (an honorary official for public benefaction) and Mu (a tribute scholar); his younger brothers were Youzhu (a Station Master), Shu, Chu, Liang, and Zhu. He married a woman née Ji. He placed sixty-eighth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 133rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

陳遷〔貫四川成都府漢州什邡縣軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字維喬，行七，年四十二，十二月二十七日生〕。曾祖宗顯，祖忠，父濟，前母廖氏、李氏，母鄧氏。慈侍下，兄運、選、導、通、述、迪，娶周氏，繼娶王氏。四川鄉試第三十四名，會試第三百三十二名。
translation_en:
Chen Dashan, registered in a military household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Ruobao, he ranked ninth among his brothers and male cousins, and he was twenty-six, born on the twenty-eighth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hong; his grandfather was Yao, an honorary official distinguished for longevity; his father was Xiangsi; his father's former wife was née Lin, and his mother was née Zhu. His parents and a grandparent were living. His elder brother was Daliang, and his younger brothers were Dabei and Daji. He married a woman née Fang. He placed sixteenth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 166th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jiao Yu, registered in a civilian household in Taiping County, Ningguo Prefecture, Zhili, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Bosheng, he ranked first among his brothers and male cousins, and he was thirty-two, born on the twenty-fourth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yaokan [?], his grandfather was Huirong, his father was Zhigang, and his mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Ran, Tong, Wei, Xi, Jiong, Lie, Ju, Can, and Huang. He married a woman née Liu. He placed ninety-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and forty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liao Yunlong, registered in an artisan household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Congzhi, he ranked fifth among his brothers and male cousins, and he was twenty-nine, born on the tenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Song, honorarily appointed Case Reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review; his grandfather was Lin; his father was Chengfu; his legal mother was née Chen, and his birth mother was née Gong. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brothers were Yunjing, Yunhong, Yunpeng, and Yun'e. He married a woman née Zhu. He placed second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 359th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Qian, registered in a military household in Shifang County, Hanzhou, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Weiqiao, he ranked seventh among his brothers and male cousins, and he was forty-two, born on the twenty-seventh day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zongxian, his grandfather was Zhong, and his father was Ji; his father's former wives were née Liao and née Li, and his mother was née Deng. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Yun, Xuan, Dao, Tong, Shu, and Di. He married a woman née Zhou and subsequently a woman née Wang. He placed thirty-fourth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 332nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Gong Yuan, registered in Taicang Subprefecture, Suzhou, in the directly administered territory, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the subprefectural school. He specialized in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Wenfu, and he ranked sixteenth among his male siblings and cousins. He was thirty-eight, born on the twenty-second day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Qian, his grandfather Jin, and his father Cai; his mother was née Hu and his stepmother née Qian. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Lu, Yi (a tribute scholar, gongshi), Xuan, Zhi, Nian, and Zhe; his younger brothers were Ni, Quan, and You. His wife was née Yao. He placed thirtieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sheng Yingyang, registered in Wujiang County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered territory, belonged to a military household and was a native of Wu County. He was a student of the Imperial University and specialized in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Sixian, and he ranked sixth among his male siblings and cousins. He was thirty-one, born on the eighteenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather Yan and grandfather Tang were both physicians in the Imperial Medical Service; his father Kun held honorary official status, and his mother was née Liu. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brothers were Yingqi (Right Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate), Yingbi (a physician awarded the official cap and sash), Yingkui, and Yinglong; his younger brothers were Yingfu (a physician awarded the official cap and sash), Yingshi, Yingling, and Yingbin. His wife was née Lu; he subsequently married a woman née Chen. He placed eighty-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 351st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Jie, registered in Renqiu County, Hejian Prefecture, in the directly administered territory, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Guoxin, and he ranked third among his male siblings and cousins. He was forty, born on the sixth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Bin, his grandfather Jie, and his father Li; his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jue and Xiu; his younger brothers were Yao, Pei, Heng, Ke, Cong, Rui, Zongwen, and Zongwu. His wife was née Li; he subsequently married women née Duan and née Pan. He placed 109th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 193rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Chong, registered in a guardsman household of the Sichuan Ceremonial Guard Office, was a native of Pi County, Chengdu Prefecture. He was a student of the Imperial University and specialized in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Shuyu, and he ranked second among his male siblings and cousins. He was thirty-two, born on the twentieth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Jian, his grandfather Hao, and his father Shiying; his mother was née Cai and his stepmother née Peng. His father was deceased, and he served his surviving mother. His elder brother was Hong and his younger brother Ang. His wife was née Zhu. He placed ninth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 381st in the Metropolitan Examination.

王允修〔貫直隸保定府容城縣，民籍，縣學增廣生，治易經，字克成，行四，年二十四，正月初九日生〕。曾祖能〔贈工部右侍郎〕，祖志廣〔封工部右侍郎〕，父賓〔刑部右侍郎〕，前母李氏〔贈淑人〕，母崔氏〔封淑人〕。慈侍下，兄允中、允塞、允言，娶韓氏。順天府鄉試第一百十一名，會試第二百二十八名。

解冠〔貫湖廣永州府道州，軍籍，國子生，治易經，字季玄，行九，年三十五，五月初二日生〕。曾祖興仲，祖晚成，父德良，母蔣氏。慈侍下，兄魁，弟勉，娶蔣氏。湖廣鄉試第八十四名，會試第一百五十三名。
translation_en:
Song Jin 宋錦, courtesy name Zhifu, was registered in Hezhou, Zhili, in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged forty-five, and born on the fifth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Boyuan; his grandfather, Xiang; his father, Jin 縉; and his mother, née Wang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Duo, and he married a woman née Zhang. He placed sixty-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 269th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Yunxiu 王允修, courtesy name Kecheng, was registered in Rongcheng County, Baoding Prefecture, Zhili, in a civilian household. An added student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Book of Changes, he was fourth in birth order, aged twenty-four, and born on the ninth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather, Neng, was posthumously granted the title of Right Vice Minister of Works; his grandfather, Zhiguang, was granted the same title; and his father, Bin, was Right Vice Minister of Justice. His father's former wife, née Li, was posthumously granted the title of Lady (shuren); his mother, née Cui, was granted that title. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Yunzhong, Yunsai, and Yunyan, and he married a woman née Han. He placed 111th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 228th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xie Guan 解冠, courtesy name Jixuan, was registered in Daozhou, Yongzhou Prefecture, Huguang, in a military household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he was ninth in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the second day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xingzhong; his grandfather, Wancheng; his father, Deliang; and his mother, née Jiang. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His elder brother was Kui, his younger brother was Mian, and he married a woman née Jiang. He placed eighty-fourth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 153rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

第三甲二百六十五名，賜同進士出身。

麥春芳〔貫廣東廣州府南海縣，民籍，順德縣人，府學生，治詩經，字元實，行一，年二十五，正月二十四日生〕。曾祖讓，祖壅〔義官〕，父俊，母鍾氏。具慶下，弟仲芳、承芳、廷芳，娶李氏。廣東鄉試第二名，會試第一百八名。

陳守愚〔貫山東兖州府東平州壽張縣，民籍，縣學生，治春秋，字如愚，行一，年三十三，四月初十日生〕。曾祖杲，祖忠〔縣丞〕，父璉，母任氏。慈侍下，兄子仁、子義、子信、子雄、子强、子恭、子言、子隆，娶周氏。山東鄉試第三十二名，會試第二百二十七名。
translation_en:
Third Class: 265 men, granted the status of graduates equivalent to metropolitan graduates (jinshi).

Feng Shiyong 馮世雍 was registered in Jiangxia County, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang, in a military household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Zihe and ranked third in family order. He was thirty years old, born on the twenty-seventh day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yue; his grandfather, Qian, held an honorary official title for longevity; his father, Fei, was an Imperial University student; and his mother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Shijun and Shining, and his younger brothers were Shixi, Shimei, Shihui, and Shixian. His wife was née Li. He placed eighth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 131st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Mai Chunfang 麥春芳 was registered in Nanhai County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, in a civilian household, and was a native of Shunde County. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Yuanshi and ranked first in family order. He was twenty-five years old, born on the twenty-fourth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rang; his grandfather, Yong, held an honorary official title for charitable contributions; his father was Jun; and his mother was née Zhong. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zhongfang, Chengfang, and Tingfang. His wife was née Li. He placed second in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 108th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Shouyu 陳守愚 was registered in Shouzhang County, Dongping Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, in a civilian household. A county school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he had the courtesy name Ruyu and ranked first in family order. He was thirty-three years old, born on the tenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gao; his grandfather, Zhong, was a County Vice Magistrate; his father was Lian; and his mother was née Ren. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his living mother. His elder brothers were Ziren, Ziyi, Zixin, Zixiong, Ziqiang, Zigong, Ziyan, and Zilong. His wife was née Zhou. He placed thirty-second in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 227th in the Metropolitan Examination.

石瓘〔貫燕山左衛軍籍，直隸威縣人，國子生，治易經，字廷陳，行三，年四十，三月十二日生〕。曾祖全，祖政，父洪，母唐氏。慈侍下，兄環、珍，娶倪氏，繼娶郄氏。順天府鄉試第一百三名，會試第一百六十七名。

translation_en:
Wang Xiu 王琇 was registered with Xuanwu Guard in Henan and was a student of the Kaifeng Prefectural School. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Wanyu. Sixth in birth order, he was aged thirty-four and was born on the twenty-fifth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shun, his grandfather Tong, and his father Zhen; his mother was née Qi. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Huan, Pei, Jie, Yu, and Cong; his younger brothers were Jin, Kun, and Ju. He married a woman née He and subsequently a woman née Li. He ranked sixth in the Henan Provincial Examination and twenty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Yan 吳彥 held artisan registration in Shanyin County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Shimei. First in birth order, he was aged thirty and was born on the third day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xuan. His grandfather Yuan was granted the honorary title of Secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice and the additional privilege of wearing fourth-rank official attire. His father Bian was a Surveillance Vice Commissioner. His mother, née Ru, was posthumously granted the title Lady of Peace; his stepmother, née Du, was granted the same title. His family status was recorded as having living elders in both the grandparental and parental generations. His younger brothers were Yin, Yi, Qi, Jing, Yi, Chan, Yi, Xin, Zhu, Shao, and Huo. He married a woman née Jin. He ranked twenty-ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and seventy-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shi Guan 石瓘 held military registration with Yanshan Left Guard and was a native of Wei County in the directly administered metropolitan region. He was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Tingchen. Third in birth order, he was aged forty and was born on the twelfth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Quan, his grandfather Zheng, and his father Hong; his mother was née Tang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Huan and Zhen. He married a woman née Ni and subsequently a woman née Qie. He ranked 103rd in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 167th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Xian 周憲 held salt-producing household registration in Xiaoshan County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Shaoji. First in birth order, he was aged thirty-eight and was born on the tenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bin, his grandfather Yongqing, and his father Fu; his mother was née Yu. Both parents were deceased. He married a woman née Xu, and subsequently women née Shi 施 and Shi 史. He ranked fifty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 239th in the Metropolitan Examination.

治春秋字和韶行二年二十七四月十八日生
曾祖子雲 祖謙寧 父宜泰〔贈兵部主事〕 母許氏〔封安人〕
慈侍下 兄簧〔布政司參議〕 娶俞氏

俞振强〔貫浙江紹興府新昌縣民籍，國子生，治書經，字德强，行九，年四十一，十一月二十七日生〕。曾祖尚純〔監生〕，祖用信〔壽官〕，父廷佐〔壽官〕，母章氏，繼母鄭氏。具慶下，弟振洪、振懷、振臺、振豪。娶王氏，繼娶石氏。浙江鄉試第三名，會試第三百三十八名。

王選〔貫河南開封府尉氏縣軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字士魁，行一，年四十四，六月十八日生〕。曾祖昇，祖拳，父欽〔經歷〕，母陸氏。具慶下，弟迥〔知州〕。娶劉氏。河南鄉試第二十七名，會試第二百九十名。

張珩〔貫直隸保定府安州民籍，州學生，治詩經，字汝節，行五，年二十八，十二月初七日生〕。曾祖清，祖敏，父學，母郝氏。嚴侍下，兄琮、琛、瑜、玠，弟珎、瑶、琳、琚、玕、璠。娶馬氏。順天府鄉試第二名，會試第十一名。

陳篪〔貫福建興化府莆田縣軍籍，府學附學生，治春秋，字和韶，行二，年二十七，四月十八日生〕。曾祖子雲，祖謙寧，父宜泰〔贈兵部主事〕，母許氏〔封安人〕。慈侍下，兄簧〔布政司參議〕。娶俞氏。福建鄉試第二十四名，會試第一百五十一名。
translation_en:
Yu Zhenqiang, registered in a civilian household in Xinchang County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Deqiang; he ranked ninth among his brothers and was aged forty-one, born on the twenty-seventh day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Shangchun, a student of the Imperial University; his grandfather, Yongxin, and his father, Tingzuo, both held honorary longevity titles. His mother was née Zhang, and his stepmother née Zheng. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zhenhong, Zhenhuai, Zhentai, and Zhenhao. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née Shi. He placed third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 338th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Xuan, registered in a military household in Weishi County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shikui; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged forty-four, born on the eighteenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Sheng; his grandfather, Quan; his father, Qin, a Registrar; and his mother, née Lu. Both parents were living. His younger brother Jiong was a Department Magistrate. He married a woman née Liu. He placed twenty-seventh in the Henan Provincial Examination and 290th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Heng, registered in a civilian household in Anzhou, Baoding Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the departmental school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Rujie; he ranked fifth among his brothers and was aged twenty-eight, born on the seventh day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Qing; his grandfather, Min; his father, Xue; and his mother, née Hao. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Cong, Chen, Yu, and Jie; his younger brothers were Zhen, Yao, Lin, Ju, Gan, and Fan. He married a woman née Ma. He placed second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eleventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Chi, registered in a military household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, was an additional student of the prefectural school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Heshao; he ranked second among his brothers and was aged twenty-seven, born on the eighteenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Ziyun; his grandfather, Qianning; and his father, Yitai, posthumously granted the title of Secretary in the Ministry of War. His mother, née Xu, was granted the title of Lady of Peace. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother Huang was an Assistant Administration Commissioner in a Provincial Administration Commission. He married a woman née Yu. He placed twenty-fourth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 151st in the Metropolitan Examination.

胡九功〔貫河南開化府尉氏縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字允治，行一，年三十八，十一月二十四日生〕。曾祖顯〔主簿〕，祖海，父璋，母于氏。慈侍下，弟九思，娶王氏。河南鄉試第二十三名，會試第二百二十四名。

崔應極〔貫河南開封府通許縣民籍，縣學生，治詩經，字建之，行二，年二十八，八月十九日生〕。曾祖浩，祖珽〔知縣，贈文林郎〕，父敖〔兵馬指揮，封文林郎〕，前母于氏〔贈孺人〕，母張氏〔封孺人〕。具慶下，兄應辰〔典膳〕，弟應昌、應聘、應怡、應恪，娶張氏。河南鄉試第十六名，會試第一百六十一名。

喻希禮〔貫湖廣黃州府麻城縣軍籍，國子生，治春秋，字節之，行四，年三十二，二月二十四日生〕。曾祖哲〔學正，贈員外郎〕，祖宗府〔知府〕，父瀹〔州判官〕，母江氏。具慶下，兄希仁、希義〔監生〕、希畢，弟希召、希智、希傅、希恭、希寬，娶萬氏。湖廣鄉試第二十七名，會試第二百三名。

朱觀〔貫直隸蘇州府崑山縣民籍，國子生，治易經，字顯伯，行五，年四十，六月十六日生〕。曾祖顯，祖珍，父苓〔壽官〕，母馮氏，繼母陳氏。具慶下，兄韶、鼎、臯、謙，弟頤、節、艮、蒙、益、震，娶周氏，繼娶楊氏。應天府鄉試第一百九名，會試第二百十一名。
translation_en:
Hu Jiugong 胡九功 was registered in a civilian household in Weishi County, Kaihua Prefecture [?], Henan. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Yunzhi and ranked first among his brothers; he was thirty-eight, born on the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather Xian was a Registrar; his grandfather was Hai, his father was Zhang, and his mother was née Yu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brother was Jiusi, and his wife was née Wang. He placed twenty-third in the Henan Provincial Examination and two hundred twenty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cui Yingji 崔應極 was registered in a civilian household in Tongxu County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan. A county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Jianzhi and ranked second among his brothers; he was twenty-eight, born on the nineteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hao; his grandfather Ting was a District Magistrate, posthumously granted the title Gentleman for Attending the Forest of Letters; and his father Ao was a Commander of a Police Office, granted the same title. His father's former wife, née Yu, was posthumously granted the title Lady, and his mother, née Zhang, was granted that title. Both parents were living. His elder brother Yingchen was a Director of Foodstuffs; his younger brothers were Yingchang, Yingpin, Yingyi, and Yingke. His wife was née Zhang. He placed sixteenth in the Henan Provincial Examination and one hundred sixty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Xili 喻希禮 was registered in a military household in Macheng County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he had the courtesy name Jiezhi and ranked fourth among his brothers; he was thirty-two, born on the twenty-fourth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather Zhe was a Schoolmaster, posthumously granted the title Vice Director; his grandfather Zongfu was a Prefect; his father Yue was a Subprefectural Assistant Magistrate; and his mother was née Jiang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xiren, Xiyi (a student of the Directorate of Education), and Xibi; his younger brothers were Xizhao, Xizhi, Xifu, Xigong, and Xikuan. His wife was née Wan. He placed twenty-seventh in the Huguang Provincial Examination and two hundred third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Guan 朱觀 was registered in a civilian household in Kunshan County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Xianbo and ranked fifth among his brothers; he was forty, born on the sixteenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xian, his grandfather was Zhen, and his father Ling held an honorary official title conferred for longevity. His mother was née Feng and his stepmother née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Shao, Ding, Gao, and Qian; his younger brothers were Yi, Jie, Gen, Meng, Yi, and Zhen. He married a woman née Zhou and subsequently a woman née Yang. He placed one hundred ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and two hundred eleventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

張心〔貫浙江紹興府餘姚縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字存良，行七，年三十五，二月初九日生〕。曾祖燁〔壽官〕，祖縉，父廷玘，母楊氏。永感下，娶徐氏。浙江鄉試第八十三名，會試第二百八十三名。

季鎬〔貫山西瀋陽中護衛，軍籍，浙江龍泉縣人，河南汲縣學教諭，治禮記，字與周，行一，年三十四，閏九月初四日生〕。曾祖彥德，祖敬宗，父政，嫡母閔氏，生母陳氏。具慶下，娶包氏。山西鄉試第四名，會試第十六名。

李涵〔貫直隸永平府遷安縣，民籍，府學生，治易經，字容之，行五，年二十六，三月二十六日生〕。曾祖林，祖友〔教諭〕，父金〔按察司副使〕，母徐氏〔封宜人〕。慈侍下，兄洪、濡、霑、潤，弟泳、治、沐、淶、洲、憲，娶廖氏。順天府鄉試第八十五名，會試第一百七名。

高凌漢〔貫山東兗州府東平州，軍匠籍，州學生，治詩經，字伯羽，行二，年三十六，十一月十八日生〕。曾祖昇，祖迪，父瓛，母劉氏。具慶下，兄凌霄，娶侯氏。山東鄉試第十四名，會試第二百二十九名。
translation_en:
Zhang Xin 張心 was registered in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Cunliang and ranked seventh in birth order; he was thirty-five years old, born on the ninth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Ye, an honorary official for longevity; his grandfather was Jin; his father was Tingqi; and his mother was née Yang. His parents and grandparents were deceased. He married a woman née Xu. He ranked eighty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 283rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ji Gao 季鎬 was registered in the Shenyang Central Escort Guard in Shanxi, in a military household, and was a native of Longquan County, Zhejiang. He served as Instructor at the county school of Ji County, Henan, and specialized in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Yuzhou, and he ranked first in birth order; he was thirty-four years old, born on the fourth day of the intercalary ninth month. His great-grandfather was Yande; his grandfather was Jingzong; his father was Zheng; his father's principal wife was née Min; and his birth mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Bao. He ranked fourth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and sixteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Han 李涵 was registered in Qian'an County, Yongping Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a civilian household. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Rongzhi and ranked fifth in birth order; he was twenty-six years old, born on the twenty-sixth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Lin; his grandfather was You, an Instructor; his father was Jin, a Surveillance Vice Commissioner; and his mother was née Xu, invested with the title Lady of Suitability. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Hong, Ru, Zhan, and Run; his younger brothers were Yong, Zhi, Mu, Lai, Zhou, and Xian. He married a woman née Liao. He ranked eighty-fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 107th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gao Linghan 高凌漢 was registered in Dongping Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, in a military artisan household. A subprefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Boyu and ranked second in birth order; he was thirty-six years old, born on the eighteenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Sheng; his grandfather was Di; his father was Huan; and his mother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Lingxiao. He married a woman née Hou. He ranked fourteenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 229th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Liu Qinshun 劉欽順 was registered in an official household in Shishou County, Jingzhou Prefecture, Huguang. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Tiqian; he ranked second in birth order and was forty years old, born on the seventeenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Donggeng, granted the title of Secretary in the Ministry of Justice; his grandfather was Xi, designated by imperial command as Secretary in the Ministry of Justice [?]; his father was Zengzhe, his mother née Wei, and his stepmother née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Qincheng; his younger brothers were Qin’en, a tribute scholar (gongshi), Qinmeng, Qinshou, Qinshan, Qinzhong, Qinquan, and Qinfu. He married a woman née Zhou and subsequently a woman née Wan. He placed twenty-fourth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and twenty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ji Chun 紀純 was registered in a civilian household in Cizhou, Zhangde Prefecture, Henan. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yizhi; he ranked first in birth order and was forty-five years old, born on the fourth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lin; his grandfather was Can, posthumously granted the title of Investigating Censor; and his father was Jie, an Investigating Censor. His mother, née Li, was granted the title of Lady (Ruren); his stepmother was also née Li. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Jue, Xiang, Yue, Zongren, and Long; his younger brothers were Kui, Zi, Shou, a Director of Foodstuffs, Yue, Chen, and Rang. He married a woman née Wu and subsequently a woman née Chen. He placed tenth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 249th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ji Zi 紀資 was registered in a civilian household in Renqiu County, Hejian Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region (Zhili). A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Tingyan; he ranked first in birth order and was forty-seven years old, born on the twenty-fifth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xin, his grandfather You, his father Lun, his mother née Lin, and his stepmother née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Jin; his younger brothers were Zan and Bin. He married a woman née Bian. He placed 129th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 278th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Yi 王儀 was registered in a civilian household in Wen’an County, Bazhou, Shuntian Prefecture. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Kejing; he ranked third in birth order and was forty years old, born on the thirtieth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Biao; his grandfather was Neng, a Registrar; and his father was Xian, an Honorary Official. His mother was née Feng. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Jie (价), an Honorary Official, and Jie (傑); his younger brothers were Xiang, Lun, Zongyao, Zongshun, and Ji. He married a woman née Xing and subsequently a woman née Song. He placed ninety-eighth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 118th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Dai Jing 戴鯨 was registered in a military household in Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Shilin; he ranked sixth in birth order and was aged thirty-eight, born on the twentieth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather Zhong received the honorary rank Chengde lang and title of Assistant Prefect; his grandfather Hao was a Prefect, advanced to the honorary rank Yazhong dafu. His father Jia was a County School Instructor, granted the honorary rank Fengzhi dafu and title of Bureau Vice Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice, with permission to wear fourth-rank official dress. His mother, née Du, was granted the title Lady of Suitability. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ao 鰲, a Prefect, and Huan, an honorary official recognized for public benefactions; his younger brothers were Ji 鱀, a Bureau Vice Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice, and Ao 鼇. He married a woman née Wang. He placed fifty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 241st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Bingyi 李秉彛 was registered in a civilian household in Shizhou, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Tianchang; he ranked sixth in birth order and was aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-fourth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Rong, his grandfather Daliang, and his father Jing; his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Bingzhong, Bingxiao, Bingxian, Bingliang, and Bingxin. He married a woman née Ren. He placed sixth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 326th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiang Xi 項錫 was registered in an official household in Jiaxing County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was a native of Jiashan County and a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Bingren; he ranked third in birth order and was aged thirty-four, born on the twenty-eighth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather Heng was posthumously granted the honorary rank Zizheng dafu and title of Left Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate. His grandfather Zhong was Minister of War, posthumously granted the title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and the name Xiangyi. His father Jing was Right Administration Vice Commissioner in a Provincial Administration Commission, advanced to the honorary rank Jiayi dafu. His father's principal wife, née Zhao, was posthumously granted the title Lady; the entry also lists mothers née Tian and née Wang, and identifies his birth mother as née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yong and Tang, both Battalion Commanders; Kai, a student admitted by virtue of hereditary official privilege; and Zhen, a student of the Directorate of Education. His younger brothers were Hua and Jin. He married a woman née Zhu. He placed 107th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 114th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Gui 劉桂 was registered in a military household in Huanggang County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang, and was a prefectural government school student. He specialized in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Zifang; he ranked second in birth order and was aged thirty-seven, born on the fifth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Quan; his grandfather Yue held honorary official rank without a substantive appointment. His father Bozhou held an honorary title granted for longevity. His mother was née Wang and his stepmother née Cai. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Tang; his younger brothers were Dong, Pu, Liang, Qiao, Xing, Cai, and Guo. He married a woman née Wang 汪. He placed fifth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and sixty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

汪琯〔貫直隸徽州府婺源縣民籍，國子生，治春秋，字諧甫，行十六，年四十六，六月十三日生〕。曾祖潯，祖掄，父炯，母江氏。慈侍下，娶詹氏，繼娶韓氏。應天府鄉試第三十七名，會試三百十三名。

杜朝紳〔貫四川成都府崇慶州民籍，國子生，治書經，字叔縉，行二，年三十二，五月初八日生〕。曾祖啓初，祖泰和，父山〔教諭〕，母鍾氏。慈侍下，兄朝東，弟朝憲、朝冕、朝儀，娶王氏。四川鄉試第二十二名，會試第二百三十六名。

方潤〔貫直隸徽州府歙縣民籍，國子生，治禮記，字時雨，行三十七，年三十九，六月二十七日生〕。曾祖以高，祖叔玉，父宗萬，前母張氏，母徐氏，繼母嚴氏。慈侍下，兄津，弟海，娶王氏。應天府鄉試第四十一名，會試第四名。
translation_en:
Cai Rui 蔡銳, courtesy name Jinbo, was registered in an official household of Yongqing Right Guard and was a native of Luanzhou, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first in family seniority and was aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-ninth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather Gui was posthumously appointed Commander; his grandfather Xuan was a Commander; and his father was Tong. His mother was née Liu, and his stepmother née Hu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Qi, Xi, and Ming, and his wife was née Zhang. He placed thirty-fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and one hundred forty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Guan 汪琯, courtesy name Xiefu, was registered in a civilian household in Wuyuan County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked sixteenth in family seniority and was aged forty-six, born on the thirteenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Xun, his grandfather Lun, and his father Jiong; his mother was née Jiang. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His wife was née Zhan; he subsequently married a woman née Han. He placed thirty-seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and three hundred thirteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Du Chaoshen 杜朝紳, courtesy name Shujin, was registered in a civilian household in Chongqing Subprefecture, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked second in family seniority and was aged thirty-two, born on the eighth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Qichu, his grandfather Taihe, and his father Shan, a School Instructor; his mother was née Zhong. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother was Chaodong, and his younger brothers were Chaoxian, Chaomian, and Chaoyi. His wife was née Wang. He placed twenty-second in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and two hundred thirty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fang Run 方潤, courtesy name Shiyu, was registered in a civilian household in She County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked thirty-seventh in family seniority and was aged thirty-nine, born on the twenty-seventh day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Yigao, his grandfather Shuyu, and his father Zongwan. His father's former wife was née Zhang, his mother née Xu, and his stepmother née Yan. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother was Jin, his younger brother Hai, and his wife née Wang. He placed forty-first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zeng Zhongkui, registered in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Sida; he ranked second in his family and was thirty-nine years old, born on the twenty-seventh day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yangwen, his grandfather Dehou, and his father Jingrui; his mother was née Ke. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Yuankui, and his wife was née Cai. He placed seventy-seventh in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 386th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qin Jin, registered in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Maonan; he ranked tenth in his family and was thirty-eight years old, born on the seventh day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tang, his grandfather Xi, and his father Kui; his mother was née Zhao. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brothers were Jin, Ao, Ying, Yue (Investigating Censor), and Hong (an official awaiting selection for appointment); his younger brothers were Luan, Qiao, Quan, Kai, Fu, Bo, and Long. His wife was née Dong. He placed twenty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 322nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gu Wenlong, registered in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zhifu; he ranked first in his family and was thirty-eight years old, born on the twentieth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ziliang, his grandfather Ding, and his father Yan (an honorary official). His father's former wife was née Zhang, and his mother was née Ma. His mother was living and his father deceased. His wife was née Shen. He placed 112th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and forty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Dan, registered in Yueqing County, Wenzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zongshi; he ranked fifth in his family and was thirty-three years old, born on the sixteenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chun (a Bureau Director in the Ministry of Personnel), his grandfather Fu, and his father Yuan; his mother was née Zhou. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zhang (Vice Commissioner of a Provincial Surveillance Commission), Xu, Hao, Bing, and Fei; his younger brother was Xi. His wife was née Zhang. He placed eightieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 395th in the Metropolitan Examination.
