translation_en:
Kong Xi, registered in a civilian household in Anlu County, De’an Prefecture, Huguang, was a native of Yongchang Prefecture, Yunnan, and a county school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Yanhe; he ranked sixth among his brothers and was aged forty-five, born on the twenty-eighth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhi, his grandfather Xiang, and his father Kai (Admonisher, granted an increased salary at rank 5a); his mother was née Wang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Chuan. He married a woman née Liu and subsequently a woman née Du. He placed eighty-first in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 357th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Xing, registered in a civilian household in Changle County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was an attached student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zhongfu; he ranked ninth among his brothers and was aged twenty-seven, born on the ninth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Boda, his grandfather Shuqi, and his father Yongfeng; his mother was née Lin. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brother was Ti, and his younger brothers were Ke and Heng. He married a woman née Chen. He placed seventy-fifth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 165th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chu Shu, registered in a military household of the Ningxia Left Guard, Shaanxi, was a native of Jiangdu County, Zhili, and a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Guobao; he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-three, born on the first day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Daoheng, his grandfather Fang, and his father Bijing (holder of an honorary official title conferred for longevity); his father’s former wife was née Yu, and his mother was née Wang. His mother was living and his father deceased. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed tenth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 370th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cai Wenkui, registered in a military household in Dehua County, Jiujiang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Guohua; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty, born on the twenty-ninth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Deyi (District Magistrate), his grandfather Cong (District Vice Magistrate), and his father Xian; his mother was née Liu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Wenhua and Wenguang. He married a woman née Hu. He placed forty-third in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 175th in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
梁廷振〔貫廣東廣州府南海縣民籍，國子生，治易經，字伯綱，行二，年三十八，五月初七日生〕。曾祖康善，祖道森，父英〔壽官〕，母周氏。具慶下，兄健，弟廷掄，娶李氏。廣東鄉試第五十名，會試第三百二名。

盧紳〔貫陝西西安府咸寧縣民籍，縣學生，治易經，字汝佩，行三，年三十三，十二月十二日生〕。曾祖椿，祖興，父旺〔壽官〕，母周氏，繼母王氏。具慶下，兄縉、經，娶林氏。陝西鄉試第二十九名，會試第一百四十一名。

方雲鶴〔貫浙江杭州府餘杭縣軍籍，國子生，治易經，字鳴皐，行四，年四十五，十月二十三日生〕。曾祖禎，祖琳，父傑〔義官〕，母金氏，繼母楊氏。永感下，兄雲鴻、雲鵬、雲鳳，弟雲龍、雲鸞、雲新，娶金氏。應天府鄉試第二十六名，會試第二百十三名。

吳世澤〔貫福建福州府連江縣民籍，國子生，治易經，字宗仁，行一，年三十七，十一月初二日生〕。曾祖衡，祖寅〔訓導〕，父瑲，母趙氏，繼母陳氏、宗氏。慈侍下，弟世治、世淵，娶陳氏。福建鄉試第四十名，會試第十三名。
translation_en:
Liang Tingzhen, registered in a civilian household in Nanhai County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Bogang, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-eight, born on the seventh day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kangshan, his grandfather Daosen, and his father Ying (holder of an honorary title for longevity); his mother was née Zhou, both parents were living, his elder brother was Jian and his younger brother Tinglun, and his wife was née Li; he placed fiftieth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 302nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Shen, registered in a civilian household in Xianning County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Rupei, he ranked third among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-three, born on the twelfth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chun, his grandfather Xing, and his father Wang (holder of an honorary title for longevity); his mother was née Zhou and his stepmother née Wang, both parents were living, his elder brothers were Jin and Jing, and his wife was née Lin; he placed twenty-ninth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 141st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fang Yunhe, registered in a military household in Yuhang County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Minggao, he ranked fourth among his brothers, and he was aged forty-five, born on the twenty-third day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhen, his grandfather Lin, and his father Jie (holder of an honorary title for public benefaction); his mother was née Jin and his stepmother née Yang, both parents were deceased, his elder brothers were Yunhong, Yunpeng, and Yunfeng, his younger brothers were Yunlong, Yunluan, and Yunxin, and his wife was née Jin; he placed twenty-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 213th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Shize, registered in a civilian household in Lianjiang County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Zongren, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-seven, born on the second day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Heng, his grandfather Yin (an Assistant Instructor), and his father Qiang; his mother was née Zhao and his successive stepmothers were née Chen and née Zong, his father was deceased and his mother living, his younger brothers were Shizhi and Shiyuan, and his wife was née Chen; he placed fortieth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and thirteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

姜梁〔貫浙江衢州府江山縣，民籍，國子生，治書經，字子方，行二百三，年三十二，正月十八日生〕。曾祖達〔贈南京禮部郎中〕，祖德璇，父潤，母毛氏。永感下，兄棟、椿，弟桂，娶詹氏。浙江鄉試第十九名，會試第二十八名。

李邦直〔貫廣東高州府茂名縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字汝司，行二，年二十八，四月初三日生〕。曾祖唐，祖璘，父執中，母歐氏。慈侍下，兄邦柱，弟邦翰、邦光、邦基，娶楊氏。廣東鄉試第四十七名，會試第九十名。

劉錄〔貫江西饒州府鄱陽縣，軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字世臣，行三十，年三十二，八月初五日生〕。曾祖經〔贈監察御史〕，祖烈〔左參政，贈太中大夫、資治少尹〕，父城〔都察院右副都御史〕，嫡母董氏〔封孺人〕，生母范氏。永感下，兄鎮〔義官〕、庸、填、釗、鏓〔遇例千戶〕，弟鑄，娶趙氏。江西鄉試第八十四名，會試第三十六名。

郭寶〔貫河南衛輝府獲嘉縣，民籍，府學生，治詩經，字惟善，行四，年二十七，十二月十五日生〕。曾祖讓〔驛丞〕，祖暹〔縣丞〕，父惠〔縣丞〕，嫡母周氏，生母張氏。具慶下，兄完、富、定〔訓科〕，弟寧，娶張氏。河南鄉試第九名，會試第三百六十五名。
translation_en:
Jiang Liang 姜梁 was registered in Jiangshan County, Quzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zifang, and he ranked 203rd in his family’s birth order. He was thirty-two years old, born on the eighteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Da, posthumously appointed Director of a bureau in the Nanjing Ministry of Rites; his grandfather was Dexuan; his father was Run; and his mother was née Mao. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Dong and Chun, and his younger brother was Gui. His wife was née Zhan. He placed nineteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and twenty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Bangzhi 李邦直 was registered in Maoming County, Gaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong, in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Rusi, and he ranked second in his family’s birth order. He was twenty-eight years old, born on the third day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tang; his grandfather was Lin; his father was Zhizhong; and his mother was née Ou. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother was Bangzhu, and his younger brothers were Banghan, Bangguang, and Bangji. His wife was née Yang. He placed forty-seventh in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and ninetieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Lu 劉錄 was registered in Poyang County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a military household. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shichen, and he ranked thirtieth in his family’s birth order. He was thirty-two years old, born on the fifth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jing, posthumously appointed Investigating Censor; his grandfather was Lie, Left Administration Vice Commissioner, posthumously awarded the titles Grand Master of Palace and Assistant Director for Aid in Governance; and his father was Cheng, Right Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate. His legal mother was née Dong, awarded the title Lady, and his birth mother was née Fan. His parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Zhen, an Honorary Official; Yong; Tian; Zhao; and Cong, appointed Battalion Commander under an applicable regulation. His younger brother was Zhu. His wife was née Zhao. He placed eighty-fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and thirty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Bao 郭寶 was registered in Huojia County, Weihui Prefecture, Henan, in a civilian household. A prefectural school student, he specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Weishan, and he ranked fourth in his family’s birth order. He was twenty-seven years old, born on the fifteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rang, a Station Master; his grandfather was Xian, a County Vice Magistrate; and his father was Hui, also a County Vice Magistrate. His legal mother was née Zhou, and his birth mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Wan, Fu, and Ding, a Medical Instructor; his younger brother was Ning. His wife was née Zhang. He placed ninth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 365th in the Metropolitan Examination.

陳洪範〔貫浙江紹興府餘姚縣，民籍，縣學附學生，治書經，字于周，行七，年三十，六月十三日生〕。曾祖紀，祖污，父璧，母孫氏。具慶下，兄洪金，弟洪寶、洪謨、洪誥，娶范氏。浙江鄉試第八十七名，會試第三十二名。

方策〔貫廣西桂林右衛，軍籍，臨桂縣人，國子生，治易經，字載道，行一，年三十，五月二十九日生〕。曾祖友政，祖洪，父玉，前母沈氏，母周氏。具慶下，弟憲，娶劉氏。廣西鄉試第三名，會試第一百九十七名。
translation_en:
Li Zhou 李輈, courtesy name Wenyu, was registered in a military household in Panyu County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked fourth in his family and was thirty-four years old, born on the eleventh day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather Xiaolian and father Run held honorary official status for longevity; his grandfather was Can, and his mother was née Zheng. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Lu, Nian, and Shi, and his wife was née Lin. He placed thirtieth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and fortieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Jujing 孫巨鯨, courtesy name Ziyu, was registered in a civilian household in Huizhou, Gongchang Prefecture, Shaanxi, and was a native of Chaoyi County. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked second in his family and was thirty years old, born on the twenty-fifth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xiu, his grandfather Jian, his father Ke, and his mother née Zhao. Both parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brother was Jukun, and his younger brothers were Juli and Ju’ao. His wife was née Deng; he subsequently married a woman née Yan. He placed fifth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 352nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Hongfan 陳洪範, courtesy name Yuzhou, was registered in a civilian household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. An additional student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked seventh in his family and was thirty years old, born on the thirteenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ji, his grandfather Wu 污 [?], his father Bi, and his mother née Sun. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Hongjin, and his younger brothers were Hongbao, Hongmo, and Honggao. His wife was née Fan. He placed eighty-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and thirty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fang Ce 方策, courtesy name Zaidao, was registered in a military household of the Guilin Right Guard, Guangxi, and was a native of Lingui County. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first in his family and was thirty years old, born on the twenty-ninth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Youzheng, his grandfather Hong, and his father Yu; his father's former wife was née Shen, and his mother was née Zhou. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Xian, and his wife was née Liu. He placed third in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and 197th in the Metropolitan Examination.

祝繼皐〔貫浙江杭州府海寧縣匠籍，國子生，治春秋，字師謨，行二，年三十八，九月二十六日生〕。曾祖銀，祖淇〔封刑部主事〕，父萃〔布政司左參政，進階嘉議大夫〕，母褚氏〔封安人〕。慈侍下，兄繼賢〔上林苑監左監丞〕、繼英〔貢士〕，弟繼華〔監生〕、繼昭〔監生〕、繼夏、繼夔〔監生〕、繼善，娶劉氏。浙江鄉試第四名，會試第一百五十七名。

商大節〔貫湖廣安陸州軍籍，河南洛陽縣學教諭，治春秋，字孟堅，行二，年三十五，九月十二日生〕。曾祖義〔貢士〕，祖汝霖，父盈，母姜氏。具慶下，兄大全，弟大鑾，娶彭氏。湖廣鄉試第五十九名，會試第一百三十二名。

王欽〔貫福建福州中衛前所官籍，候官縣學附學生，治易經，字公寅，行六，年二十九，七月初五日生〕。曾祖智〔贈通議大夫、都察院右副都御史〕，祖佐〔教諭，封監察御史，累贈都察院右副都御史〕，父鼎，母李氏。嚴侍下，兄鍾、鎧，弟鉞、鍵、鑰、鎮，娶林氏，繼娶林氏。福建鄉試第八十名，會試第二百七十六名。

袁載〔貫浙江寧波府慈谿縣民籍，縣學附學生，治詩經，字安道，行二十五，年三十六，九月初十日生〕。曾祖智，祖糖，父煦，母王氏。慈侍下，兄吉、坤、圭、耇、里，弟基、圻、孝、彀，娶章氏。浙江鄉試第二十九名，會試第二百八十五名。
translation_en:
Zhu Jigao 祝繼皐 was registered in an artisan household in Haining County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Shimo; he ranked second in his family and was thirty-eight, born on the twenty-sixth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yin; his grandfather, Qi, received the honorary appointment of Secretary in the Ministry of Justice; his father, Cui, was Left Administration Vice Commissioner in a Provincial Administration Commission, advanced to the rank of Grand Master for Excellent Counsel; and his mother, née Chu, received the title Lady of Peace. His mother was still living, and his father was deceased. His elder brothers were Jixian, Left Assistant Director of the Directorate of Imperial Parks, and Jiying, a tribute student; his younger brothers were Jihua and Jizhao, both students of the Directorate of Education, Jixia, Jikui, also a student of the Directorate of Education, and Jishan. He married a woman née Liu. He placed fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 157th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shang Dajie 商大節 was registered in a military household in Anlu Subprefecture, Huguang, and served as Instructor at the Luoyang County School in Henan. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Mengjian; he ranked second in his family and was thirty-five, born on the twelfth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yi, a tribute student; his grandfather was Rulin; his father was Ying; and his mother was née Jiang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Daquan, and his younger brother was Daluan. He married a woman née Peng. He placed fifty-ninth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 132nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Qin 王欽 was registered in an officer household of the Front Battalion of Fuzhou Central Guard, Fujian, and was an supplementary student at the Houguan County School specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Gongyin; he ranked sixth in his family and was twenty-nine, born on the fifth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather, Zhi, was posthumously awarded the rank of Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and the appointment of Right Vice Censor-in-Chief in the Censorate. His grandfather, Zuo, was an Instructor, received the honorary appointment of Investigating Censor, and subsequently received posthumous appointments culminating in Right Vice Censor-in-Chief in the Censorate. His father was Ding, and his mother was née Li. His father was still living, and his mother was deceased. His elder brothers were Zhong and Kai; his younger brothers were Yue, Jian, Yue, and Zhen. He married a woman née Lin and subsequently another woman née Lin. He placed eightieth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 276th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yuan Zai 袁載 was registered in a civilian household in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was a supplementary student at the county school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Andao; he ranked twenty-fifth in his family and was thirty-six, born on the tenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhi; his grandfather was Tang; his father was Xu; and his mother was née Wang. His mother was still living, and his father was deceased. His elder brothers were Ji, Kun, Gui, Gou, and Li; his younger brothers were Ji, Qi, Xiao, and Gou. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed twenty-ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 285th in the Metropolitan Examination.

俞稷〔貫浙江嚴州府建德縣軍籍，國子生，治易經，字舜牧，行三，年三十四，八月初十日生〕。曾祖炫，祖灝，父廷貴〔審理正〕，母魯氏。嚴侍下，兄夔〔知縣〕、龍，弟貢、凱，娶馬氏。浙江鄉試第八十三名，會試第一百七十三名。

薛宗鎧〔貫廣東潮州府揭陽縣民籍，府學生，治書經，字子脩，行一，年二十六，三月初一日生〕。曾祖志安，祖驥，父俊〔國子監學正〕，母莊氏。重慶下，弟宗鑑、宗銓、宗鏗、宗鐺、宗鐸、宗鑰、宗釜、宗鎬，娶丁氏。廣東鄉試第四十九名，會試第二百十七名。

王庚〔貫直隸永平府灤州民籍，國子生，治易經，字文祥，行二，年三十九，十月十六日生〕。曾祖通，祖益，父得春〔壽官〕，母衛氏。具慶下，兄奎，娶李氏。順天府鄉試第三十五名，會試第三百七十九名。
translation_en:
Shi Jian 石簡, registered in a military household in Ninghai County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Lianbo; he ranked tenth in his family and was aged thirty-seven, born on the seventh day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jing; his grandfather, Tian, was an Instructor; his father, Bin, was an Assistant Instructor; and his mother was née Pan. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Liang, and his younger brothers were Yun, Lu, Jie, Pian, and Ju. He married a woman née Lü. He placed fifteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 353rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Ji 俞稷, registered in a military household in Jiande County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Shunmu; he ranked third in his family and was aged thirty-four, born on the tenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xuan; his grandfather was Hao; his father, Tinggui, was a Judicial Director; and his mother was née Lu. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Kui, a District Magistrate, and Long; his younger brothers were Gong and Kai. He married a woman née Ma. He placed eighty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 173rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xue Zongkai 薛宗鎧, registered in a civilian household in Jieyang County, Chaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was a prefectural government school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zixiu; he ranked first in his family and was aged twenty-six, born on the first day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhian; his grandfather was Ji; his father, Jun, was an Instructor in the Directorate of Education; and his mother was née Zhuang. Both parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Zongjian, Zongquan, Zongkeng, Zongdang, Zongduo, Zongyao, Zongfu, and Zonggao. He married a woman née Ding. He placed forty-ninth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 217th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Geng 王庚, registered in a civilian household in Luanzhou, Yongping Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Wenxiang; he ranked second in his family and was aged thirty-nine, born on the sixteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tong; his grandfather was Yi; his father, Dechun, held an honorary official title granted for longevity; and his mother was née Wei. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Kui. He married a woman née Li. He placed thirty-fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 379th in the Metropolitan Examination.

李宗樞〔貫陝西西安府耀州富平縣，軍籍，國子生，治禮記，字子西，行三，年二十七，十二月二十四日生〕。曾祖讓，祖文政〔贈府同知〕，父恕〔布政司左參議〕，母宋氏〔封宜人〕。慈侍下，兄宗橋〔義官〕、宗桂〔醫學訓科〕，娶王氏。陝西鄉試第十五名，會試第三百四十九名。

translation_en:
Jiang En, courtesy name Junxi, was registered in Guang’an Subprefecture, Shunqing Prefecture, Sichuan, in a military household. A student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the eighth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Yao, a County Assistant Magistrate; his grandfather was Yonghe; and his father was Congjian, an honorary official for public benefaction. His mother and stepmother were both née He. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Qian. He married a woman née Li and subsequently a woman née Deng. He placed sixty-first in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 270th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Mo, courtesy name Yizheng, was registered in Anfu County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the fourth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Liwen; his grandfather was Benhui; and his father was Bangzhao, an annual tribute student. His mother was née Yin. His mother alone was living. His elder brother was Dong, and his younger brothers were Zhu, Bing, Shi, Quan, Xiang, Qi, Bai, Jian, and Ji. He married a woman née Wang. He placed thirty-seventh in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 320th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Zongshu, courtesy name Zixi, was registered in Fuping County, Yao Subprefecture, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, in a military household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Rites, he was third in birth order, aged twenty-seven, and born on the twenty-fourth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Rang; his grandfather was Wenzheng, posthumously appointed Vice Prefect; and his father was Shu, Left Assistant Administration Commissioner. His mother, née Song, held the title Lady of Suitability. His mother alone was living. His elder brothers were Zongqiao, an honorary official for public benefaction, and Zonggui, a Medical Instructor. He married a woman née Wang. He placed fifteenth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 349th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Long Dazhi, courtesy name Rudeng, was registered in an officer household of the Front Yulin Guard and was a native of Tangyi County, Shandong. An additional student of the Shuntian prefectural school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the eleventh day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Jun, a Guard Commander posthumously awarded the title General of Manifest Valor; his grandfather was Shun, an Assistant Regional Military Commissioner awarded the title General of Manifest Valor; and his father was Duo, a Guard Commander awarded the same title. His mother, née Liu, held the title Lady of Chastity. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Jun and Han. He married a woman née Chen. He placed ninety-fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 366th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhou Xiang, registered in a military household in Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes (Yijing); his courtesy name was Daqing, he ranked second in his family, and he was twenty-seven, born on the twenty-eighth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Yu, his grandfather Xing, his father Qin, and his mother née Yu; both parents were living, his elder brother was Mo, his younger brothers were Zhi and Huai, and his wife was née Zang; he placed fifteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and sixty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zuo Sizhong, registered in a civilian household in Yaozhou, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes (Shijing); his courtesy name was Changchen, he ranked first in his family, and he was thirty-two, born on the twenty-fifth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Chun, his grandfather Jin (honorarily appointed Right Assistant Judge in the Court of Judicial Review), his father Jing (Assistant Surveillance Commissioner), and his mother née Song (granted the title Lady of Peace); both parents were living, his younger brother was Sijing, and he married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née Hu; he placed sixteenth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and seventy-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fang Sheng, registered in a civilian household in Wuyuan County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region (Zhili), was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents (Shujing); his courtesy name was Shiyou, he ranked seventieth in his family, and he was forty-six, born on the twenty-second day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Shixi, his grandfather Sida, his father Wenbao, and his mother née Wang; both parents were deceased, his elder brothers were Qin (an honorary official for charitable contributions) and Jian, and his wife was née Cheng; he placed sixty-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 279th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shang Zhi, registered in a military household of the Left Jinwu Guard and a native of Gaoping County, Shanxi, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents (Shujing); his courtesy name was Shixian, he ranked twelfth in his family, and he was forty-eight, born on the eleventh day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Zheng, his grandfather He, his father Kuan, and his mother née Liu; both parents were deceased, his elder brothers were Shou, Fu, and Lu, and he married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née Xiao; he placed sixty-seventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 169th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Chen Mo, courtesy name Shiyu, was registered in a civilian household in Ba County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked third in his family and was aged forty-two, born on the sixteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenhui; his grandfather, Xi; his father, Renshi; and his mother, née Liu. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were En and Zhao, and his younger brother was Shun. He married a woman née Wang. He placed forty-second in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 126th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Fu, courtesy name Kongxiu, was registered in a civilian household in Shangyuan County, Yingtian Prefecture, and was a native of Lishui County, Zhejiang. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first in his family and was aged forty-two, born on the eleventh day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zongkui; his grandfather, Zishi; his father, Rong, a magistrate; and his mother, née Zhang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brother was Ting. He married a woman née Li. He placed sixty-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 136th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Huai, courtesy name Zhongchuan, was registered as a bannerman of the Embroidered-uniform Guard and was a native of Wuding Subprefecture, Shandong. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked second in his family and was aged forty, born on the twenty-sixth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenshan; his grandfather, Guang; his father, Zheng; his mother, née Fang; and his stepmother, née Dong. His parents were deceased. His elder brother was Jiang, and his younger brother was Ji. He married a woman née Gu and subsequently a woman née Fan. He placed twenty-third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 341st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Di Chong, courtesy name Zhongxu, was registered in a military household in Liyang County, Yingtian Prefecture. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked ninth in his family and was aged forty-two, born on the twenty-ninth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zongyi; his grandfather, Jie; his father, Qin; and his mother, née Peng. His parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Xiang, Jin, Pan, and Zhu, and his younger brother was Han. He married a woman née Yang. He placed thirty-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fifty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Sanxing, courtesy name Chengfu, was registered in a military household in Chaoyi County, Tongzhou, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. He ranked first among his brothers and was twenty-five sui, born on the eighteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather, Bin, was a Clerk, posthumously awarded the title of Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue; his grandfather, Jin, was a former Director in the Ministry of Revenue; and his father, Chaoyong, was a Judge. His mother was née Ma, and his stepmother was née Li. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Sanjun, Sanli, Sanjie, Sanzhi, Sance, Sanyi, and Sanyou. He married a woman née Hao. He placed 54th in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 329th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Hu, courtesy name Ruqi, was registered in an officer household of the Nanyang Central Escort Guard, Henan. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Documents. He ranked fifth among his brothers and was thirty-six sui, born on the twenty-sixth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wang; his grandfather, Xin, was a Vice Battalion Commander, granted the honorary title General of Military Strategy; and his father, Sheng, held an honorary title for longevity. His father’s former wife was née Zhang, his mother was née Xiong, and his stepmother was née Lu. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Lian, Pin, Xuan, and Ji. He married a woman née Liu and subsequently a woman née Pang. He placed 57th in the Henan Provincial Examination and 307th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Yi, courtesy name Boshi, was registered in a salt-producing household in Hengshui County, Shenzhou, Zhending Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the county Confucian school, he specialized in the Book of Changes. He ranked sixth among his brothers and was twenty-nine sui, born on the thirteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenli; his grandfather, Qing; and his father, Hui. His father’s former wife was née Liu, his mother was née Zhang, and his stepmother was also née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Chong, Yu, and Su, and his younger brothers were Huan, Jun, and Cai. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 88th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Guan Yingchun, courtesy name Dongyang, was registered in Zhending County, Zhending Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a military household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-five, and born on the twenty-fifth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fu, who held an honorary title for longevity; his grandfather was Xuan; his father was Long; and his mother was née Li. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Yingkui, Yingbi, Yingyi, and Yingzhen, and his wife was née Wu. He ranked one hundredth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 358th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Ming, courtesy name Jiqing, was registered in Licheng County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, in a salt-producing household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged forty, and born on the sixth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ao; his grandfather was Zhen; and his father was Qian, who held an honorary title for longevity. His father's former wife was née Jia, and his mother was née Zhao. His father alone was still living. His elder brother was Cong and his younger brother was Hui. His wife was née Meng, and he subsequently married a woman née Ren. He ranked sixty-ninth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and fifty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yan Fu, courtesy name Jieqing, was registered in Caozhou, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, in a military household. A student of the department school specializing in the Book of Odes, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-nine, and born on the twenty-eighth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhongkuan; his grandfather was Yi; his father was Hao; and his mother was née Wu. His mother alone was still living. His elder brother was Lun, and his younger brothers were Tang, Pu, and Fen. His wife was née Chen. He ranked tenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 235th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Mao Qu, courtesy name Daheng, was registered in Wujiang County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a civilian household. A student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes, he was third in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the twenty-seventh day of the intercalary third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fengyi; his grandfather was Youliang; his father was Yuan; and his mother was née Chen. His mother alone was still living. His elder brothers were Lü and Shu, and his wife was née Gu. He ranked fifty-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 134th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Rong, registered in Lishui County, Chuzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a prefectural school student. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zongren. First in birth order, he was forty-four and was born on the eighteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhong, his grandfather Yangzheng, and his father He; his mother was née Zhou. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brothers were Li and Tang, and his wife was née Xiang. He ranked sixty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fifty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xia Guoxiao, registered in Fuzhou, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a subprefectural school student. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Renfu. Second in birth order, he was thirty-five and was born on the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yanbi, his grandfather Bangben, and his father Zheng; his mother was née Yi. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Guozhong, and his younger brothers were Guoxian, Guobin, and Guozhu. His wife was née Zhao. He ranked sixty-fifth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and three hundred fiftieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yin Shangxian, registered in Ye County, Laizhou Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to an artisan household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Binqing. Third in birth order, he was thirty-three and was born on the third day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sheng, his grandfather Ying, and his father Tong, a county school instructor; his mother was née Wang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Wen, Heng, and Zuo, and his wife was née Xu. He ranked nineteenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and two hundred eighty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Peng, registered in Yangshuo County, Guilin Prefecture, Guangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Tengxiao. Second in birth order, he was thirty-two and was born on the twenty-fourth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Longguang. His grandfather Sheng was a prefectural registrar, posthumously granted the title of Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice. His father Liu was a Surveillance Vice Commissioner; his mother, née Zhou, was invested with the title Lady of Suitability. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother Luan was a student of the Directorate of Education, and his younger brothers were E, Ou, and Zhi. His wife was née Zhang. He ranked seventh in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and three hundred sixty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Jingfu and ranked second among his brothers. He was aged twenty-nine, born on the twenty-sixth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rong, his grandfather Xue, and his father Lian, a District Magistrate; his mother was née Cao and his stepmother née Zhang. He had living grandparents and parents. His elder brother was Chong, his younger brothers Bao and Ding, and his wife was née Shi. He placed seventy-sixth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 315th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ye Liangpei 葉良佩 was registered in Taiping County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a military household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Jingzhi and ranked first among his brothers. He was aged twenty-three, born on the fourteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xu, his grandfather Yong, and his father Zhao; his mother was née Fu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Liang’ou and Liangchu, and his wife was née Zhao. He placed thirty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and thirty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Zongren 劉宗仁 was registered in Daming County, Daming Prefecture, Zhili, in a civilian household. A county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Rongfu and ranked first among his brothers. He was aged forty, born on the twenty-fourth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Si, his grandfather Fu, and his father Yun; his mother was née Lai. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Zongli, Zongzhi, Zongdao, Zongshun, Zongyu, Zongtang, Zongwen, and Zongwu, and his wife was née Guo. He placed 120th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 304th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Yang Zuo, courtesy name Yidao, was registered in a civilian household in Changshou County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the sixteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sheng, a student of the Directorate of Education; his grandfather was Ding; his father was Dexiu, an Assistant Instructor; and his mother was née Wang. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother was Ru and his younger brother Ji. He married a woman née Li and subsequently a woman née Zhang. He ranked seventy-fifth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 393rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fan Ji, courtesy name Dounan, was registered in an artisan household in Daxing County, Shuntian Prefecture, and was a native of Wujiang County in the directly administered region. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he was third in birth order, aged forty-one, and born on the thirteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shichang, his grandfather Jin, and his father Lin; his father's former wife was née Xiao, and his mother was née Feng. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Wen, Zhang, Kui, and Bi, and his younger brother was Yi. He married a woman née Mu and subsequently women née Dong and née Zhang. He ranked 114th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 221st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Shixu, courtesy name Yukui, was registered in a military household in Jiyang County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged forty-one, and born on the third day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather's name is transcribed as 𤇍 [reading uncertain]; his grandfather was Tai, his father Yong, and his mother née Huang. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brother was Shizhi. He married a woman née Bai and subsequently a woman née Liu. He ranked ninth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 210th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Tingli, courtesy name Zili, was registered in a civilian household in Tongshan County, Xingguo Subprefecture, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Rites, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the twenty-fourth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xin, an Examiner in the Provincial Surveillance Commission; his grandfather was Yuancong; his father was Boji, a Prefectural Judge; and his mother was née Wu. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Tingwen and Tingfu. He married a woman née Han. He ranked sixty-fourth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 164th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Shiyong 陸時雍 was registered in Gui’an County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a military household; he was a county school student specializing in the Book of Changes, with the courtesy name Youchun, ranked third among his brothers, and was aged twenty-seven, born on the nineteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yi〔Gentleman for Attending to Affairs (chengshi lang)〕, his grandfather Yu, his father Lian, and his mother née Shen; both parents were deceased; his elder brothers were Shizhong〔tribute student (gongshi)〕and Shihe; his wife was née Yang; he placed forty-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 347th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Daofang 胡道芳 was registered in She County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region, in a military household; he was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, with the courtesy name Weizhong, ranked fifth among his brothers, and was aged thirty-eight, born on the twenty-third day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wu, his grandfather Gui, his father Xuan, his father’s former wife née Wang 汪, and his mother née Wu; both parents were living; his elder brothers were Suifang and Kuifang, and his younger brother Yunfang; his wife was née Wu; he placed thirty-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qin Shixian 秦世顯 was registered in Jingyang County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, in an artisan household; he was an attached student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes, with the courtesy name Zixiu, ranked third among his brothers, and was aged eighteen, born on the second day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Si, his grandfather You〔holder of an honorary official title for longevity〕, his father Ju, his mother née Dan, and his stepmother née Wang 王; his parents and at least one grandparent were living; his elder brothers were Shiheng and Shiguang, and his younger brothers Shimei and Shiguan; he was betrothed to a woman née Wang; he placed thirty-first in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and ninety-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qin Hao 秦鎬 was registered in Sanyuan County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, in a civilian household; he was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, with the courtesy name Zijing, ranked second among his brothers, and was aged twenty-seven, born on the nineteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kerang, his grandfather Bing, his father Zhongxue, and his mother née Ma; both parents were deceased; his elder brother was Zhen; his wife was née Chao; he placed twenty-first in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 246th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Xuan 郭鉉, courtesy name Rujie, was registered in Dai Subprefecture, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, in a military household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked third among his brothers and was aged forty-four, born on the twentieth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fengxian, his grandfather Hui, and his father Tingbi; his mother was née Li. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Qin and Kai, and his wife was née Liu. He placed thirty-sixth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 188th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Shen 鄔紳, courtesy name Peizhi, was registered in Dantu County, Zhenjiang Prefecture, Zhili, in a military household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Changes, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-seven, born on the twenty-fifth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ming, his grandfather Jian, and his father Rong; his mother was née Gao. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Lun, and his wife was née Chen. He placed fifty-fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fifty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Diaoyuan 李調元, courtesy name Huaqing, was registered in Xi County, Guang Subprefecture, Runing Prefecture, Henan, in a military household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-first day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhongliang; his grandfather Hong was a student of the Directorate of Education, and his father Yao held an honorary official title conferred for longevity. His mother was née Qiang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Diaogeng and Diaohu, and his wife was née Shi. He placed forty-sixth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 292nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Kai 楊愷, courtesy name Yuliang, was registered in Qiongshan County, Qiongzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, in a military household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-two, born on the second day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zicheng, his grandfather Xiong, and his father Ding; his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His wife was née Hai. He placed twenty-third in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 172nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

左季賢〔貫山東東昌府臨清州丘縣，民籍，縣學生，治禮記，字晉卿，行三，年三十二，十二月初十日生〕。曾祖希庸，祖翼，父文舉〔州判官〕，母吳氏。具慶下，兄孟賢、仲賢，弟相，娶劉氏。山東鄉試第五名，會試第三百三十九名。

汪居安〔貫直隸安慶府桐城縣，軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字行可，行三，年三十五，十二月二十七日生〕。曾祖文達，祖冬，父潜，嫡母丁氏，生母胡氏。慈侍下，兄居仁、居正，娶李氏。應天府鄉試第一百六名，會試第二百三十八名。
translation_en:
Liu Rusong, registered in Licheng County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a civilian household and was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zhenwu; he ranked first in birth order and was aged thirty-two, born on the fifteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Shun, his grandfather Zhe, and his father Cheng; his mother was née Li. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Rulin and his younger brother Ruji; his wife was née Jin. He placed sixth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 361st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xia Yulin, registered in Changshu County, Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to a military household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Guofu; he ranked first in birth order and was aged thirty-eight, born on the twenty-second day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Sheng, his grandfather Chen, and his father Jian; his mother was née Xu and his stepmother née Qian. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Tielin, Jiaolin, and Shilin; his wife was née Fan. He placed 111th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 318th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zuo Jixian, registered in Qiu County, Linqing Subprefecture, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Jinqing; he ranked third in birth order and was aged thirty-two, born on the tenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Xiyong, his grandfather Yi, and his father Wenju, a subprefectural judge; his mother was née Wu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Mengxian and Zhongxian, and his younger brother Xiang; his wife was née Liu. He placed fifth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 339th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Ju’an, registered in Tongcheng County, Anqing Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to a military household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Xingke; he ranked third in birth order and was aged thirty-five, born on the twenty-seventh day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Wenda, his grandfather Dong, and his father Qian; his legal mother was née Ding and his birth mother née Hu. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Juren and Juzheng; his wife was née Li. He placed 106th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 238th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Lu Yingzhen, registered in a civilian household in Feicheng County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Ruifu; he ranked first in birth order and was thirty years old, born on the ninth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhen; his grandfather, Xuan, was an Assistant Instructor; his father was Lan, and his mother was née Liu. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brother was Yingxiang, and his wife was née Zhai. He placed fifty-first in the Shandong Provincial Examination and three hundred fifty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Heng, registered in a civilian household in Yugan County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zongde; he ranked twenty-fifth in birth order and was forty-four years old, born on the twenty-eighth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tongzu; his grandfather, Zimu, was posthumously granted the title of Prefectural Vice Prefect; his father, Zhe, was Associate Commissioner of the Salt Distribution Commission, advanced to the prestige title of Grand Master of Central Rectitude. His mother, née Luo, was granted the title of Lady of Suitability. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Yu, an Instructor; Hu, an Instructor; Huang, a Professor; Jin; Qi; Sui; and Yao. His wife was née Gao. He placed twenty-seventh in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and one hundred twentieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ye Rui, registered in an official household in Lin'an Guard, Yunnan, and originally from Fengyang County in the directly administered metropolitan region, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Yingqi; he ranked first in birth order and was thirty-five years old, born on the twelfth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rong; his grandfather was Cheng; his father, Cong, was a provincial graduate (juren) serving as Acting School Instructor; and his mother was née Feng. His father was deceased and his mother living. His wife was née Zeng. He placed eighteenth in the Yunnan–Guizhou Provincial Examination and two hundred eighty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Luo Pu, registered in a military household in Raoping County, Chaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Shouyue; he ranked first in birth order and was thirty-seven years old, born on the twelfth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was De; his grandfather was Huan; his father's name is transcribed as 𪉀 [?]; and his mother was née Lin. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brother was Shan, and his wife was née Xu. He placed nineteenth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and one hundred nineteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Fang Riqian, registered in a salt-producing household in Fuqing County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Tidao; he ranked eighth in family birth order and was thirty-five years old, born on the seventh day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yin, his grandfather Ji, his father Wei, and his mother née Shi. His mother was still living, and his father was deceased. His younger brothers were Riyue and Bingyang; his wife was née Shi. He placed forty-fourth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and one hundred forty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Ti, registered in an official household of Dingliao Right Guard, Liaodong, was originally from Zhijiang County, Huguang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he had the courtesy name Zhongyi, ranked first in family birth order, and was thirty-nine years old, born on the tenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sheng, his grandfather Kuan, his father Hong, his mother née Guo, and his stepmother née Huang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jian, a Company Commander, and Kai; his younger brothers were Dong, Xing, Huai, and Ke. His wife was née Yao. He placed twenty-second in the Shandong Provincial Examination and two hundred forty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Jun, registered in a civilian household in Nanhai County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zhaiqing; he ranked first in family birth order and was fifty-one years old, born on the twenty-ninth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shengbao, his grandfather Yuan, and his father Neng. His legal mother was née Liao, and his birth mother was née Yan. Both parents were deceased. His younger brother was Zhong, and his wife was née Yu. He placed sixty-third in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and two hundred twelfth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Zhun, registered in a bannerman household of the Shaanxi Ceremonial Guard Office, was originally from Qingtian County, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Rites, he had the courtesy name Zitui, ranked sixth in family birth order, and was thirty years old, born on the ninth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Li, Chief of the Ceremonial Guard; his grandfather was Xuan, a prestige official of the seventh rank; and his father was Yue. His father's former wife was née Li, his mother was née Qiao, and his stepmother was née Zhang. His mother was still living, and his father was deceased. His elder brothers were Pu, a Ceremonial Guard Officer; Run, a Chief of a Hundred entitled to wear official cap and girdle; Qia, a provincial graduate serving as acting Instructor; Zhao; and Fa. His younger brother was Shu, and his wife was née Zhu. He placed fifth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and two hundred fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fu Feng'ao 傅鳳翺, registered in a civilian household in Yingshan County, Sui Subprefecture, De'an Prefecture, Huguang, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Dehui; he ranked second among his brothers, was aged thirty-seven, and was born on the fifteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jing, his grandfather Xianquan, and his father Ji, a Judicial Officer; his mother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Fengxiang, and his younger brothers were Fengyi and Fengchong. His wife was née Wang. He placed forty-fourth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and ninety-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Ji 王激, registered in a military salt-producing household in Yongjia County, Wenzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Ziyang; he ranked second among his brothers, was aged forty-eight, and was born on the seventh day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gong, his grandfather Feng, and his father Zheng; his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brother Che was a tribute scholar (gongshi), and his younger brother was Pei. His wife was née Shao. He placed second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 262nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Pan Ying 潘穎, registered in a civilian household in Ninghai County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shuyu; he ranked fourth among his brothers, was aged forty-one, and was born on the sixth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Pu, his grandfather Ci, and his father Jun; his father's former wife was née Wang, and his mother was née Yang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Xu. His wife was née Ye. He placed thirty-sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 258th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fu Mengbi 傅夢弼, registered in a civilian household in Tangyin County, Zhangde Prefecture, Henan, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Qiyan; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty-six, and was born on the twenty-seventh day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Liang, his grandfather Jie, and his father Ting, a Station Master; his father's former wives were née Han and née Fan, and his mother was née Li. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Mengxian and Mengxiang. His wife was née Chen. He placed sixteenth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 109th in the Metropolitan Examination.

His courtesy name was Jingyang; he ranked third among his brothers and was aged twenty-eight, born on the sixth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ming, his grandfather Gang, his father Lin, and his mother née Zhang. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Xu, Yu, Xiong, Yan, and Dian [?]. He married a woman née Hua. He placed eighty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 394th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Danan 沈大楠, registered in a civilian household in Kunshan County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Tingcai; he ranked third among his brothers and was aged thirty-six, born on the twenty-fifth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lu, his grandfather Cun, a District Magistrate, his father Xu 湏 [?], and his mother née Wang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Dachun and Datong; his younger brothers were Dadong, Daliang, Dachuan, Dazhong, Daqi, and Dazong. He married a woman née Sheng. He placed 112th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 187th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Wanbi 徐萬璧, registered in a civilian household in Dazhu County, Guang’an Subprefecture, Shunqing Prefecture, Sichuan, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Chaozhong; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-six, born on the eleventh day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Youzhong, his grandfather Sigao, his father Liang, who held an honorary official title for longevity, and his mother née Zhuo. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Wanqiong, Wanyu, Wanyao, and Wanxiu. He married a woman née Lan. He placed fifteenth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and forty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fan Jinglin 樊景麟, registered in a military household in Xinfan County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, and originally from Puzhou, Shanxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Jiren; he ranked fourth among his brothers and was aged thirty-nine, born on the fifteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was En, his grandfather Qing, his father Boqi, and his mother née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jinglu and Jingfeng. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed sixty-eighth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 268th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Li Mengzhou, registered in a civilian household in Haimen County, Tongzhou Subprefecture, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Xidao; he ranked third among his brothers, was thirty-six years old, and was born on the first day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Chengzu, Assistant Gentleman for Achieving Merit (digong zuolang); his grandfather was Jie, an official awaiting selection for appointment; and his father was Shi, an assistant prefect. His mother was née Sun, his stepmother née Zhang, and his birth mother née Zhu. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Xinsong, an assistant instructor, and Mengshou; his younger brother was Mengchen. He married a woman née Zhang and subsequently a woman née Jiang. He placed ninetieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 114th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Shifu, registered in a military household in Dingyuan County, Fengyang Prefecture, in the directly administered region, was a native of Fengyang Central Guard and a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Rulin; he ranked first among his brothers, was thirty-seven years old, and was born on the tenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Yuan, his grandfather Fei, and his father Xian, an honorary official recognized for public benefaction; his mother was née Chai. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brothers were Shibi, Shilian, Shiju, Shifang, and Shixian. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed thirty-fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventy-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Bian, registered in a military household of Zhenwu Guard in Shanxi, was a native of Daizhou and an added-quota student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shangyi; he ranked second among his brothers, was twenty-seven years old, and was born on the first day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Xian, his grandfather Zhihong, and his father Zheng; his mother was née Gao. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Jing. He married a woman née Yu. He placed thirty-third in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 330th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Kun, registered in a civilian household in Chongde County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Mengdeng; he ranked second among his brothers, was thirty-nine years old, and was born on the tenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Wenzhong, an honorary official recognized for longevity; his grandfather was Yu; and his father was Xun, an honorary official recognized for public benefaction. His mother was née Xu. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Min. He married a woman née Lü. He placed sixty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 121st in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhou Yuan, courtesy name Weiyi, was registered in a civilian household in Daxing County, Shuntian Prefecture, and was a native of Yin County, Zhejiang. A Confucian scholar, he specialized in the Book of Changes. He was fifth in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the twenty-first day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xiaohe; his grandfather, Rui; his father, Shuo; and his mother, née Zhang. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brother was Kui, and his younger brothers were Zhe, Xun, and Nan. He married a woman née Guan. He placed thirty-seventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 130th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dong Hong, courtesy name Zhongxuan, was registered in a military household in Jing County, Ningguo Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He was twenty-seventh in birth order, aged forty-one, and born on the fourteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuanliang; his grandfather, Zhidao, posthumously appointed Prefect; his father, Zhuo, an honorary official; and his mother, née Chen. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Jin, Rui, and Zuan, all honorary officials; Lian, an official holding prestige rank; and Yin, a tribute scholar. His younger brothers were Guan, Luan, Rong, Yue, and Yi. He married a woman née Wen. He placed 118th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 363rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Tingxiang, courtesy name Zizhong, was registered in a civilian household in Pingliang County, Pingliang Prefecture, Shaanxi. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Changes. He was first in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the twenty-fifth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gao; his grandfather, Quan; his father, Jian, a County Registrar; his mother, née Jin; and his stepmother, née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Shifu, and his younger brothers were Bangru, Tingdong, Tingji, Tingzhen, Tingji, and Tingmei. He married a woman née Hu and subsequently a woman née Jia. He placed thirty-fourth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and thirtieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Shaofang, courtesy name Bochuan, was registered in an official household in Yingcheng County, De’an Prefecture, Huguang. A county school student, he specialized in the Book of Changes. He was first in birth order, aged twenty-seven, and born on the twenty-fourth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Min, a Vice Prefect; his grandfather, Yu; his father, Lan; and his mother, née Chen. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brother was Jifang. He married a woman née Zhou and subsequently a woman née Tian. He placed forty-sixth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 298th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Yang Quan 楊銓, courtesy name Bingheng, was registered in an officer household of the Wugong Right Guard and was a native of Pizhou in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the twentieth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather Rong, grandfather Ying, and father Mao were all Battalion Commanders. His father's former wife was née Wang; his mother, also née Wang, was invested as Lady of Suitability. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Jin and his younger brother Jun. He married a woman née Ren and subsequently women née Wang and née Li. He placed seventy-eighth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 266th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang You 王侑, courtesy name Tingxian, was registered in a guardsman's household of the Embroidered-uniform Guard and was a native of Wanzhou, Guangdong. An attached student of the Shuntian Prefectural School specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-six, and born on the eighth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Xianzheng, his grandfather Zhikui, and his father Jinghe, Vice Commissioner of the Institute of Imperial Handicrafts; his mother was née Sheng. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother Zuo was Vice Commissioner of the Leather Workshop. He married a woman née Peng and subsequently a woman née Yan. He placed 103rd in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 396th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Haogu 張好古, courtesy name Shangyou, was registered in a civilian household in Yangcheng County, Zezhou, Shanxi. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged forty-five, and born on the nineteenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Guang, his grandfather Che, and his father Heng, posthumously appointed Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue. His mother, née Chang, was posthumously honored as Lady of Peace; his stepmother, née Liu, was invested as Lady of Peace. His father was deceased and his surviving mother was living. His younger brothers were Haoren, Haoque, Haojue (Director in the Ministry of Revenue), Haowen, Haocha, Haoli, and Haohui. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née Li. He placed fortieth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 224th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qiao Qian 喬遷, courtesy name Yumu, was registered in a civilian household in Dingtao County, Caozhou, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the fourth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Tong, his grandfather Zhongyou, an honorary official recognized for public beneficence, and his father Xi, a student of the Imperial University; his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Xuan. He married a woman née Fei. He placed thirty-sixth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 399th in the Metropolitan Examination.

李欽昊〔貫順天府東安縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字子翼，行二，年三十八，四月初五日生〕。曾祖東〔行人司司副，贈太僕寺少卿〕，祖侃〔都察院右僉都御史〕，父德恢〔布政司右參政，贈中大夫〕，母延氏〔封恭人，贈淑人〕。永感下，兄暐，弟光霽〔南京大理寺寺副〕、光需，娶孟氏。順天府鄉試第八十六名，會試第三百四十三名。
translation_en:
Gan Xun, registered in a civilian household in Fengcheng County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Xizhou; he ranked second in birth order and was thirty-one, born on the twelfth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Nanrong; his grandfather, Hao, and father, Jie, were sacrificial officials (shengjiguan). His mother was née Yang, and his stepmother née Feng. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Dian, and his wife was née Fan. He placed 109th in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 340th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Zhuo, registered in a civilian household in Guixi County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Chengfu; he ranked eighteenth in birth order and was thirty-eight, born on the twenty-third day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Guichen; his grandfather, Shilong; and his father, Shangzhen, who held an honorary title for longevity. His mother was née Liang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Huan, Huang, Ying, Huan, Xuan, Daonan, Yuan, and Li; his younger brothers were Xizu and Xizong. His wife was née Ye; he subsequently married women née Jiang and née Yu. He placed fifteenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 149th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Tong, registered in an official household in Wujin County, Changzhou Prefecture, Zhili, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Weiyi; he ranked first in birth order and was thirty-seven, born on the twenty-first day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather, Ying, held the prestige title of Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Special Advancement and served as Junior Mentor, concurrently Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, and Minister of Rites; he was posthumously awarded the title of Grand Guardian and the name Zhong’an. His grandfather, Gong, was a Discipline Officer in the Embroidered-uniform Guard. His father, Qian, was appointed Commander of the Zhenjiang Guard under the applicable regulations. His mother was née Duan. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Kai and Ke, the latter a Discipline Officer; his younger brothers were Lun, Shen, Huai, Zheng, Yi, En, De, Zong, and Zhi. His wife was née Shao; he subsequently married a woman née Gu and was betrothed to a woman née Bian. He placed thirteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Qinhao, registered in a civilian household in Dong’an County, Shuntian Prefecture, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Ziyi; he ranked second in birth order and was thirty-eight, born on the fifth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather, Dong, was Vice Director of the Office of Transmission and was posthumously awarded the title of Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud. His grandfather, Kan, was Right Assistant Censor-in-chief in the Censorate. His father, Dehui, was Right Administration Vice Commissioner in a Provincial Administration Commission and was posthumously awarded the prestige title of Grand Master of the Palace. His mother, née Yan, was granted the title of Lady of Respect and posthumously awarded that of Lady of Chastity. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Wei; his younger brothers were Guangji, Assistant Judge of the Court of Judicial Review in Nanjing, and Guangxu. His wife was née Meng. He placed eighty-sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 343rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

顏容端〔貫廣東惠州府長樂縣民籍，國子生，治書經，字體嚴，行一，年三十三，八月初八日生〕。曾祖璿，祖光〔訓科〕，父珙，母鄒氏。具慶下，弟容正、容重，娶魏氏。廣東鄉試第四十九名，會試第三十九名。

王傅〔貫河南河南衛官籍，陝西高陵縣人，洛陽縣學生，治易經，字道宗，行二，年三十一，五月二十八日生〕。曾祖忠，祖從善〔百戶〕，父昭〔百戶〕，前母孫氏，母孫氏。慈侍下，兄俊〔百戶〕，弟佶，娶吳氏，繼娶孫氏。河南鄉試第五十名，會試第三百十四名。
translation_en:
Zhang Su 張素 was registered in a military household of the Anning Defense Thousand-household Office in Yunnan and was a native of Pucheng County, Fujian. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Jiwen, ranked first among his brothers, and was thirty-five years old, born on the twenty-ninth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Feng, his grandfather Ying, and his father Wei; his mother was née Dai and his stepmother née Bian. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Zhang and subsequently a woman née Dai. He placed seventh in the Yunnan–Guizhou Provincial Examination and 376th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Guan 許琯 was registered in a civilian household in Dangtu County, Taiping Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and was a native of She County. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Bohe, ranked second among his brothers, and was thirty-one years old, born on the fifteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zizhen, his grandfather Yongren, and his father Jiqing; his father's former wife was née Luo, his mother née Wu, and his stepmother née Song. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brother was Guang; his younger brothers were Yao, Cheng, Jin, Wei, Yuan, Yue, and Fu. He married a woman née Cheng. He placed twelfth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 124th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yan Rongduan 顏容端 was registered in a civilian household in Changle County, Huizhou Prefecture, Guangdong. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he had the courtesy name Tiyan, ranked first among his brothers, and was thirty-three years old, born on the eighth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xuan, his grandfather Guang, a Medical Instructor, and his father Gong; his mother was née Zou. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Rongzheng and Rongzhong. He married a woman née Wei. He placed forty-ninth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and thirty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Fu 王傅 was registered in an official household of the Henan Guard in Henan and was a native of Gaoling County, Shaanxi. A Luoyang county school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Daozong, ranked second among his brothers, and was thirty-one years old, born on the twenty-eighth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhong, his grandfather Congshan, a Company Commander, and his father Zhao, also a Company Commander; his father's former wife and his mother were both née Sun. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother Jun was a Company Commander; his younger brother was Ji. He married a woman née Wu and subsequently a woman née Sun. He placed fiftieth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 314th in the Metropolitan Examination.

阿其麟〔貫山西振武衛官籍，代州人，州學增廣生，治詩經，字仁夫，行一，年二十八，四月二十五日生〕。曾祖勝〔副千戶〕，祖顥〔副千戶〕，父衡，母李氏。慈侍下，娶張氏。山西鄉試第三十九名，會試第九十九名。
