translation_en:
A Qilin 阿其麟 was registered in an official household of Zhenwu Guard, Shanxi, and was a native of Daizhou. He was an added-quota student of the subprefectural school and specialized in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Renfu; he was first in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the twenty-fifth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather Sheng and grandfather Hao were both Vice Commanders of a Battalion; his father was Heng, and his mother was née Li. His father was deceased and his mother living. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed thirty-ninth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and ninety-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Bai Yi 白鎰 was registered in a military household in Pingding Subprefecture, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi. He was a student of the subprefectural school and specialized in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Yingheng; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-nine, and born on the fourth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather Qi was honorifically granted the title of Investigating Censor; his grandfather Jie was honorifically granted the title of Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel. His father Sicong held a seventh-rank prestige title, and his mother was née Lü. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Yong, a dianke [?]; Zhong, a prefectural Examiner; and Jin, a tribute scholar. His younger brothers were Zhen, a Registrar; Quan, a tribute scholar; Jian and Fu, both Imperial University students; and Chun. He married a woman née Sun. He placed sixty-fourth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and one hundred fifty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Shiyong 周世雍 was registered in a civilian household in Shunde County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong. He was an attached student of the county school and specialized in the Record of Rites. His courtesy name was Yucheng; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the first day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Guang, his grandfather Lian, his father Zhi, and his mother née Fang. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Shigao, Shiming, Shixiao, Shiliang, Shizhe, and Shishu. He married a woman née Huang. He placed thirty-sixth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and three hundred sixty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhong Ying 鍾英 was registered in a military household of Wuxiang Right Guard and was a native of Ziyang County, Shandong. He was an Imperial University student and specialized in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Ruji; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the eleventh day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Sheng, his grandfather Gang, his father Zan, and his mother née Chen. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Mei. He married a woman née Liu. He placed thirty-fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

text:

punctuated:
王良卿〔貫江西吉安府安福縣民籍，縣學增廣生，治易經，字汝忠，行八，年二十九，九月十六日生〕。曾祖俊英，祖萬章〔封主事〕，父爵〔運使，進階嘉議大夫〕，前母鄧氏〔贈安人〕，母謝氏〔封安人〕。具慶下，兄鈺，娶李氏。江西鄉試第一百八十二名，會試第三百七十五名。

陳表〔貫雲南前衛軍籍，湖廣安鄉縣人，四川南溪縣學教諭，治書經，字獻忠，行二，年三十四，十一月十七日生〕。曾祖讓，祖德昇，父孔易，母謝氏。具慶下，兄襲，弟製、扆、衮，娶黃氏。雲貴鄉試第二十三名，會試第三百二十五名。

孫昺〔貫直隸太平府當塗縣軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字子晦，行一，年四十二，正月十四日生〕。曾祖銓，祖璥，父宸〔壽官〕，母陳氏，繼母楊氏。嚴侍下，兄輔、麟、鳳、冕、裕、容、貴、昌、綱，弟紀、方、暹、綉、杲，娶朱氏。應天府鄉試第一百二十五名，會試第三百四十六名。

陸岡〔貫江西撫州府臨川縣儒籍，府學附學生，治詩經，字本坤，行九，年三十三，四月十三日生〕。曾祖懋宗，祖𤇍〔啓官壽〕，父元〔州判〕，母鄒氏，繼母徐氏。具慶下，兄𨦟〔醫官〕、山、阜，弟陵、川，娶朱氏。江西鄉試第一百四名，會試第二百四十四名。
translation_en:
Wang Liangqing 王良卿 was registered in a civilian household in Anfu County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, and was an additional student at the county school. He specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Ruzhong; he ranked eighth in his family and was twenty-nine years old, born on the sixteenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Junying; his grandfather, Wanzhang, received the honorary title of Secretary; and his father, Jue, was a Salt Distribution Commissioner, advanced in prestige rank to Grand Master for Excellent Counsel. His father’s former wife, née Deng, was posthumously granted the title of Lady of Tranquility; his mother, née Xie, was granted the same title. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Yu, and his wife was née Li. He placed 182nd in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 375th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Biao 陳表 was registered in a military household of the Yunnan Front Guard and was a native of Anxiang County, Huguang. He served as Instructor at the county school of Nanxi, Sichuan, and specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Xianzhong; he ranked second in his family and was thirty-four years old, born on the seventeenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Rang, his grandfather Desheng, his father Kongyi, and his mother née Xie. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Xi, and his younger brothers were Zhi, Yi, and Gun. His wife was née Huang. He placed 23rd in the Yunnan–Guizhou Provincial Examination and 325th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Bing 孫昺 was registered in a military household in Dangtu County, Taiping Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zihui; he ranked first in his family and was forty-two years old, born on the fourteenth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Quan, his grandfather Jing, and his father Chen, who held an honorary official title conferred for longevity. His mother was née Chen and his stepmother née Yang. His father alone was living. His elder brothers were Fu, Lin, Feng, Mian, Yu, Rong, Gui, Chang, and Gang; his younger brothers were Ji, Fang, Xian, Xiu, and Gao. His wife was née Zhu. He placed 125th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 346th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Gang 陸岡 was registered in a Confucian scholar household in Linchuan County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, and was an attached student at the prefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Benkun; he ranked ninth in his family and was thirty-three years old, born on the thirteenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Maozong; his grandfather was 𤇍 [pronunciation uncertain], whose annotation reads 啓官壽 [?, possibly referring to an honorary official title conferred for longevity]; and his father, Yuan, was an Assistant Prefect. His mother was née Zou and his stepmother née Xu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were 𨦟 [pronunciation uncertain], a Medical Officer, Shan, and Fu; his younger brothers were Ling and Chuan. His wife was née Zhu. He placed 104th in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 244th in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
葉瑞〔貫江西饒州府樂平縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字君輯，行六，年四十五，九月二十九日生〕。曾祖世春，祖日新，父純標，母鄭氏。永感下，兄珪、璧，弟璁、珮，娶王氏。江西鄉試第三十四名，會試第三百九十二名。

許廷桂〔貫直隸鳳陽府壽州蒙城縣，官籍，國子生，治詩經，字世芳，行一，年四十，十月初三日生〕。曾祖富，祖志〔知縣〕，父譚，母段氏。具慶下，弟廷相，娶鄒氏。應天府鄉試第九十七名，會試第八十名。

龍欽〔貫湖廣長沙府茶陵州，軍籍，國子生，治易經，字則敬，行二，年四十三，三月十六日生〕。曾祖瑜，祖濟高，父振澧，母曾氏。具慶下，兄則忠，弟則仁、則憲、錫、則恪、則宣、鎧，娶易氏，繼娶陳氏。湖廣鄉試第四十七名，會試第二百九十一名。

薛華〔貫山西平陽府蒲州河津縣，民籍，國子生，治書經，字時暉，行二，年三十八，正月初二日生〕。曾祖溥〔贈刑部員外郎〕，祖諶〔刑部員外郎〕，父鸞，母陳氏。具慶下，兄芸，弟芝〔貢士〕、葵〔中書舍人〕、艾、菖、蘭、芥、茂、蔓、萊、蕚、蕃、芬，娶衛氏。山西鄉試第六十七名，會試第一百十五名。
translation_en:
Ye Rui 葉瑞, registered in Leping County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Junji; he ranked sixth among his brothers and was aged forty-five, born on the twenty-ninth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shichun, his grandfather Rixin, and his father Chunbiao; his mother was née Zheng. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Gui and Bi, and his younger brothers Cong and Pei. His wife was née Wang. He placed thirty-fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 392nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Tinggui 許廷桂, registered in Mengcheng County, Shou Subprefecture, Fengyang Prefecture, the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to an official household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Shifang; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged forty, born on the third day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fu, his grandfather Zhi (a county magistrate), and his father Tan; his mother was née Duan. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Tingxiang, and his wife was née Zou. He placed ninety-seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eightieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Long Qin 龍欽, registered in Chaling Subprefecture, Changsha Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Zejing; he ranked second among his brothers and was aged forty-three, born on the sixteenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yu, his grandfather Jigao, and his father Zhenli; his mother was née Zeng. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Zezhong; his younger brothers were Zeren, Zexian, Xi, Zeke, Zexuan, and Kai. His wife was née Yi; he subsequently married a woman née Chen. He placed forty-seventh in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 291st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xue Hua 薛華, registered in Hejin County, Pu Subprefecture, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Shihui; he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-eight, born on the second day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Pu (posthumously appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice), his grandfather Chen (Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice), and his father Luan; his mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Yun; his younger brothers were Zhi (a tribute scholar, gongshi), Kui (a Secretariat Drafter), Ai, Chang, Lan, Jie, Mao, Man, Lai, E, Fan, and Fen. His wife was née Wei. He placed sixty-seventh in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 115th in the Metropolitan Examination.

胡節〔貫山東萊州府濰縣，軍籍，縣學生，治詩經，字介夫，行一，年二十四，九月十七日生〕。曾祖英，祖宣，父洪，母郭氏。具慶下，弟忠，娶劉氏。山東鄉試第十二名，會試第三百十二名。

張景〔貫河南汝寧府汝陽縣，民籍，順天府大興縣人，國子生，治春秋，字光啓，行一，年三十九，八月十一日生〕。曾祖斌，祖喜，父璽〔義官〕，母杜氏。具慶下，弟昺、昱、星，娶强氏。河南鄉試第四名，會試第二百一名。

張集〔貫直隸真定府晉州，民籍，國子生，治書經，字汝思，行二，年二十八，正月二十七日生〕。曾祖信，祖名矩〔封監察御史，贈大理寺左寺丞〕，父璿〔都察院右僉都御史〕，母邵氏〔封宜人〕。具慶下，兄棐，弟渠、檠、築、臬、槃，娶王氏。順天府鄉試第四十八名，會試第三百七十七名。

周延〔貫江西吉安府吉水縣，民籍，儒士，治易經，字南喬，行四，年二十五，十一月初二日生〕。曾祖適〔教授〕，祖温，父良福，母李氏。慈侍下，弟纓，娶熊氏。江西鄉試第四十名，會試第九十八名。
translation_en:
Hu Jie 胡節, courtesy name Jiefu, was registered in a military household in Wei County, Laizhou Prefecture, Shandong. A county government school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-four, and born on the seventeenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ying, his grandfather Xuan, his father Hong, and his mother Lady Guo. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Zhong, and his wife was Lady Liu. He ranked twelfth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 312th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Jing 張景, courtesy name Guangqi, was registered in a civilian household in Ruyang County, Runing Prefecture, Henan, and was a native of Daxing County, Shuntian Prefecture. An Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-nine, and born on the eleventh day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bin, his grandfather Xi, his father Xi 璽 (an honorary official), and his mother Lady Du. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Bing, Yu, and Xing, and his wife was Lady Qiang. He ranked fourth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 201st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Ji 張集, courtesy name Rusi, was registered in a civilian household in Jinzhou, Zhending Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Documents, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the twenty-seventh day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xin. His grandfather, named Ju, had been granted the title of Investigating Censor and posthumously awarded that of Left Assistant Minister of the Court of Judicial Review. His father was Xuan, Right Assistant Censor-in-chief of the Censorate, and his mother was Lady Shao, granted the title of Lady of Suitability. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Fei, and his younger brothers were Qu, Qing, Zhu, Nie, and Pan. His wife was Lady Wang. He ranked forty-eighth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 377th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Yan 周延, courtesy name Nanqiao, was registered in a civilian household in Jishui County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi. A Confucian scholar specializing in the Classic of Changes, he was fourth in birth order, aged twenty-five, and born on the second day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shi, a Prefectural School Professor; his grandfather was Wen, his father Liangfu, and his mother Lady Li. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brother was Ying, and his wife was Lady Xiong. He ranked fortieth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and ninety-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

錢术〔貫浙江嘉興府海鹽縣民籍，縣學生，治書經，字汝沖，行四十二，年三十二，正月二十八日生〕。曾祖顯〔贈監察御史〕，祖璠，父滂，母朱氏，繼母顧氏。具慶下，兄模〔訓導〕、木，弟潾、榦、福、祿、栢、邦、柱、栻，娶鄭氏。浙江鄉試第十四名，會試第五十一名。

虞守愚〔貫浙江金華府義烏縣民籍，國子生，治禮記，字惟明，行一百六十四，年四十一，八月初五日生〕。曾祖潤，祖葬，父尚禮，母何氏。慈侍下，弟守魯、守蒙、守德、守道、守元、守亨，娶黃氏。浙江鄉試第八十五名，會試第三百五十五名。

陳仲〔貫福建泉州府晉江縣匠籍，縣學生，治易經，字時中，行二，年三十八，四月十六日生〕。曾祖賢生，祖玘〔遞運所大使〕，父福〔義官〕，母李氏。具慶下，兄伯，弟伏、价、佐、佑，娶李氏。福建鄉試第七十六名，會試第一百九十二名。

謝應龍〔貫直隸徽州府祁門縣民籍，縣學生，治春秋，字雲卿，行十二，年三十七，十月二十五日生〕。曾祖䫴〔壽官〕，祖恒，父宣，母汪氏。慈侍下，兄應春、應奎，弟應鳳、應麟、應鍾、應禎、應時、應熊、繼輅、箕、斗、昴、璧、應鶉，娶汪氏，繼娶江氏。應天府鄉試第十三名，會試第三百六十名。
translation_en:
Qian Shu 錢术 [?], courtesy name Ruchong, was registered in a civilian household in Haiyan County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A county school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked forty-second in his family and was thirty-two years old, born on the twenty-eighth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Xian, posthumously appointed Investigating Censor; his grandfather was Fan; his father was Pang; his mother was née Zhu, and his stepmother née Gu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Mo, an Assistant Instructor, and Mu; his younger brothers were Lin, Gan, Fu, Lu, Bai, Bang, Zhu, and Shi. He married a woman née Zheng. He placed fourteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fifty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Shouyu 虞守愚, courtesy name Weiming, was registered in a civilian household in Yiwu County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked 164th in his family and was forty-one years old, born on the fifth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Run; his grandfather was Zang 葬 [?]; his father was Shangli; and his mother was née He. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Shoulu, Shoumeng, Shoude, Shoudao, Shouyuan, and Shouheng. He married a woman née Huang. He placed eighty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 355th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Zhong 陳仲, courtesy name Shizhong, was registered in an artisan household in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian. A county school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked second in his family and was thirty-eight years old, born on the sixteenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Xiansheng; his grandfather was Qi, Chief of a Transport Office; his father was Fu, an honorary official recognized for philanthropy; and his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Bo; his younger brothers were Fu, Jie, Zuo, and You. He married a woman née Li. He placed seventy-sixth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 192nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xie Yinglong 謝應龍, courtesy name Yunqing, was registered in a civilian household in Qimen County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region (Zhili). A county school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked twelfth in his family and was thirty-seven years old, born on the twenty-fifth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Jin 䫴, an honorary official recognized for longevity; his grandfather was Heng; his father was Xuan; and his mother was née Wang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Yingchun and Yingkui; his younger brothers were Yingfeng, Yinglin, Yingzhong, Yingzhen, Yingshi, Yingxiong, Jilu, Ji, Dou, Mao, Bi, and Yingchun. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née Jiang. He placed thirteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 360th in the Metropolitan Examination.

黃直〔貫江西撫州府金谿縣軍籍，國子生，治易經，字以方，行十二，年三十五，四月初五日生〕。曾祖廷憲，祖録，父琳，母徐氏。嚴侍下，兄儃，弟仰、儀、俸、胄、倬、价，娶徐氏，繼娶李氏。江西鄉試第七十七名，會試第二百六十四名。
translation_en:
Wang Dao 王道, courtesy name Hongji, was registered in a military household of Zhuolu Guard in the directly administered metropolitan region and was a native of Haining County, Zhejiang. A student of the Zhuozhou government school, he specialized in the Classic of Poetry. He ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-four years old, born on the ninth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sheng; his grandfather, Xuan; his father, Qing; his mother, née Ji; and his stepmother, née Tian. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Qian and Xun. He married a woman née Li and subsequently a woman née Gu. He placed fortieth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Rui 楊銳, courtesy name Kecheng, was registered in an official household of the Embroidered-uniform Guard and was a native of Fangshan County, Shuntian Prefecture. An Imperial University student, he specialized in the Classic of Documents. He ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-eight years old, born on the nineteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Dechun. His grandfather, Qing, was posthumously granted the title General of Military Strategy and the office of troop-commanding Vice Chiliarch. His father, Li, was a Centurion of the Embroidered-uniform Guard, formerly a Vice Chiliarch, and was granted the title General of Military Strategy. His mother, née Tian, was posthumously granted the title Lady of Suitability. His father alone was living. His elder brother, whose given name is written 𨯔 [?], was a Bureau Director in the Ministry of Revenue; his younger brother, Yi, was formerly a Centurion of the Embroidered-uniform Guard. He married a woman née Chen. He placed twenty-sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and ninety-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fan An 范安, courtesy name Ziren, was registered in an artisan household of Henei County, Huaiqing Prefecture, Henan. An Imperial University student, he specialized in the Classic of Changes. He ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-two years old, born on the twelfth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shun; his grandfather, Gong; his father, Huai; and his mother, née Cui. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Shi. He placed fifty-second in the Henan Provincial Examination and three hundred thirty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Zhi 黃直, courtesy name Yifang, was registered in a military household of Jinxi County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi. An Imperial University student, he specialized in the Classic of Changes. He ranked twelfth among his brothers and was thirty-five years old, born on the fifth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tingxian; his grandfather, Lu; his father, Lin; and his mother, née Xu. His father alone was living. His elder brother was Chan 儃; his younger brothers were Yang, Yi, Feng, Zhou, Zhuo, and Jie. He married a woman née Xu and subsequently a woman née Li. He placed seventy-seventh in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and two hundred sixty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

曾祖重鉉　祖默〔知縣〕　父槩　母夏氏
重慶下　弟良政　良器　良茂　娶甘氏
江西鄉試第三十二名　會試第一百九十六名
punctuated:
金克厚〔貫浙江台州府僊居縣，民籍，縣學生，治詩經，字弘載，行二，年四十，正月初七日生〕。曾祖存心〔壽官〕，祖謨，父渟，母汪氏。具慶下，弟克恭、克訓、克昌、克勝，娶林氏，繼娶蔣氏。浙江鄉試第四十二名，會試第四十二名。

楊大章〔貫浙江紹興府餘姚縣，軍籍，國子生，治書經，字章之，行一，年三十三，八月二十八日生〕。曾祖宜振〔贈工部主事〕，祖榮〔工部郎中〕，父策〔訓導〕，母史氏。重慶下，弟大韶、大夏，娶張氏，繼聘汪氏。浙江鄉試第十九名，會試第一百四十名。

薛僑〔貫廣東潮州府揭陽縣，民籍，府學生，治書經，字尚遷，行六，年二十四，七月初十日生〕。曾祖田，祖志安，父驥，母曾氏。慈侍下，兄俊〔國子監學正〕、傑、侃〔行人司行人〕、僎、偉，娶黃氏。廣東鄉試第六名，會試第六十名。

魏良弼〔貫江西南昌府新建縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字師說，行三，年三十二，八月初七日生〕。曾祖重鋐，祖默〔知縣〕，父槩，母夏氏。重慶下，弟良政、良器、良茂，娶甘氏。江西鄉試第三十二名，會試第一百九十六名。
translation_en:
Jin Kehou 金克厚 was registered in Xianju County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household. A county school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he had the courtesy name Hongzai and ranked second among his brothers; he was forty years old and was born on the seventh day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cunxin, who held an honorary official title for longevity; his grandfather was Mo; his father was Ting; and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Kegong, Kexun, Kechang, and Kesheng. He married a woman née Lin and subsequently a woman née Jiang. He placed forty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and forty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Dazhang 楊大章 was registered in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a military household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Documents, he had the courtesy name Zhangzhi and ranked first among his brothers; he was thirty-three years old and was born on the twenty-eighth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yizhen, posthumously granted the title of Secretary in the Ministry of Works; his grandfather was Rong, a Bureau Director in the Ministry of Works; his father was Ce, an Assistant Instructor; and his mother was née Shi. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Dashao and Daxia. He married a woman née Zhang and was subsequently betrothed to a woman née Wang. He placed nineteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and one hundred fortieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xue Qiao 薛僑 was registered in Jieyang County, Chaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong, in a civilian household. A prefectural school student specializing in the Classic of Documents, he had the courtesy name Shangqian and ranked sixth among his brothers; he was twenty-four years old and was born on the tenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tian; his grandfather was Zhi’an; his father was Ji; and his mother was née Zeng. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Jun, an Instructor at the Imperial University; Jie; Kan, a Messenger in the Messenger Office; Zhuan; and Wei. He married a woman née Huang. He placed sixth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and sixtieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wei Liangbi 魏良弼 was registered in Xinjian County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he had the courtesy name Shishuo and ranked third among his brothers; he was thirty-two years old and was born on the seventh day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chonghong; his grandfather was Mo, a District Magistrate; his father was Gai; and his mother was née Xia. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Liangzheng, Liangqi, and Liangmao. He married a woman née Gan. He placed thirty-second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and one hundred ninety-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
方遠宜〔貫直隸徽州府歙縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字伯時，行五，年四十，正月初一日生〕。曾祖道泰，祖植，父壽饒，母吳氏，繼母孫氏。永感下。兄遠守、遠宏，弟遠宣、遠富、遠寯、遠容。娶鮑氏。應天府鄉試第一百十名，會試第二十名。

曾烶〔貫湖廣黃州府麻城縣，軍籍，縣學生，治禮記，字日宣，行六，年三十二，八月初十日生〕。曾祖應通，祖啓〔教諭，贈知縣〕，父大顯〔按察司僉事〕，母李氏，繼母張氏。具慶下。兄煥〔推官〕、焞、熺、煌、煃〔監生〕，弟焀、燸、烺、炳。娶喻氏。湖廣鄉試第三十七名，會試第三百二十名。

余昇〔貫大寧營州右屯衛，軍籍，浙江開化縣人，國子生，治書經，字德陽，行二，年三十六，十二月十八日生〕。曾祖谷祥，祖諒，父惠，母李氏。永感下。兄昂，弟昊。娶張氏，繼娶劉氏、潘氏。順天府鄉試第一百十九名，會試第八十五名。

胡瀹〔貫河南河南府洛陽縣，民籍，府學生，治易經，字新甫，行二，年三十七，八月初三日生〕。曾祖宏〔知州〕，祖惟善，父遠〔教諭〕，前母楊氏、劉氏，母焦氏。永感下。兄天錫。娶索氏。河南鄉試第十名，會試第一百六十三名。
translation_en:
Fang Yuanyi 方遠宜 was registered in She County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region, in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Boshi; he ranked fifth in the family and was forty years old, born on the first day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Daotai, his grandfather Zhi, and his father Shourao; his mother was née Wu and his stepmother née Sun. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Yuanshou and Yuanhong, and his younger brothers Yuanxuan, Yuanfu, Yuanjun, and Yuanrong. His wife was née Bao. He placed 110th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twentieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zeng Ting 曾烶 was registered in Macheng County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang, in a military household. A county government school student, he specialized in the Record of Rites. His courtesy name was Rixuan; he ranked sixth in the family and was thirty-two years old, born on the tenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yingtong; his grandfather Qi was an Education Instructor, posthumously appointed District Magistrate; and his father Daxian was an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner. His mother was née Li and his stepmother née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Huan 煥, a Prefectural Judge, Tun 焞, Xi 熺, Huang 煌, and Kui 煃, a student of the Directorate of Education; his younger brothers were Hu 焀, Ru 燸, Lang 烺, and Bing 炳. His wife was née Yu. He placed thirty-seventh in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 320th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Sheng 余昇 was registered in the Yingzhou Right Garrison Guard of Daning, in a military household, and was a native of Kaihua County, Zhejiang. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Deyang; he ranked second in the family and was thirty-six years old, born on the eighteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Guxiang, his grandfather Liang, and his father Hui; his mother was née Li. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Ang and his younger brother Hao. His wife was née Zhang; he subsequently married women née Liu and née Pan. He placed 119th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Yue 胡瀹 was registered in Luoyang County, Henan Prefecture, Henan, in a civilian household. A prefectural government school student, he specialized in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Xinfu; he ranked second in the family and was thirty-seven years old, born on the third day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather Hong was a Department Magistrate; his grandfather was Weishan, and his father Yuan was an Education Instructor. His father's former wives were née Yang and née Liu; his mother was née Jiao. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Tianxi. His wife was née Suo. He placed tenth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 163rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

龔輝〔貫浙江紹興府餘姚縣，民籍，國子生，治《詩經》，字實卿，行一，年三十九，九月二十五日生〕。曾祖志顯，祖璋，父森〔縣丞〕，母方氏。具慶下，弟晃、耀、蘭、豸、京，娶周氏。浙江鄉試第二名，會試第八十四名。

張景獻〔貫廣東廣州府順德縣，軍籍，國子生，治《詩經》，字廷哲，行三，年三十八，八月二十日生〕。曾祖克新，祖天成〔壽官〕，父遠，母鄧氏。永感下，兄景晨、景昭，弟景明、景旦、景昂、景用、景衛、景雲，娶陳氏。廣東鄉試第十六名，會試第二百十八名。

屠楷〔貫廣西桂林府臨桂縣，軍籍，國子生，治《書經》，字良植，行二，年三十四，閏九月初六日生〕。曾祖侃，祖仲華，父謙〔貢士〕，母王氏。慈侍下，兄格，弟梓、材、櫪、杞、楠、槐，娶張氏。廣西鄉試第一名，會試第一百十二名。

康天爵〔貫山西平陽府臨汾縣，軍籍，國子生，治《禮記》，字汝脩，行二，年三十五，二月十六日生〕。曾祖勵，祖子厚，父欽〔監生〕，母羅氏。慈侍下，兄天璽，弟天濟、天澤、天壽，娶刁氏。山西鄉試第五名，會試第三百二十七名。
translation_en:
Gong Hui 龔輝, registered in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the National University specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shiqing; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-nine, and born on the twenty-fifth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhixian, his grandfather Zhang, and his father Sen, a County Vice Magistrate; his mother was née Fang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Huang, Yao, Lan, Zhi, and Jing. He married a woman née Zhou. He placed second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and eighty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Jingxian 張景獻, registered in Shunde County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, belonged to a military household and was a student of the National University specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Tingzhe; he was third in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the twentieth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kexin, his grandfather Tiancheng, who held an honorary official title conferred for longevity, and his father Yuan; his mother was née Deng. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Jingchen and Jingzhao; his younger brothers were Jingming, Jingdan, Jingang, Jingyong, Jingwei, and Jingyun. He married a woman née Chen. He placed sixteenth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and two hundred eighteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tu Kai 屠楷, registered in Lingui County, Guilin Prefecture, Guangxi, belonged to a military household and was a student of the National University specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Liangzhi; he was second in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the sixth day of the intercalary ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kan, his grandfather Zhonghua, and his father Qian, a tribute student; his mother was née Wang. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother was Ge; his younger brothers were Zi, Cai, Li, Qi, Nan, and Huai. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed first in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and one hundred twelfth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Kang Tianjue 康天爵, registered in Linfen County, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, belonged to a military household and was a student of the National University specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Ruxiu; he was second in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the sixteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Li, his grandfather Zihou, and his father Qin, a student of the National University; his mother was née Luo. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother was Tianxi; his younger brothers were Tianji, Tianze, and Tianshou. He married a woman née Diao. He placed fifth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and three hundred twenty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

title: 嘉靖二年進士登科錄

王從善〔貫湖廣襄陽府襄陽縣官籍，陝西南鄭縣人，國子生，治詩經，字承吉，行二，年二十二，四月十四日生〕。曾祖文貴〔贈鎮國將軍、都指揮同知〕，祖忠〔正千戶，贈鎮國將軍、都指揮同知〕，父信〔後軍都督府都督同知，充漕運總兵官〕，前母賀氏〔贈夫人〕，母楊氏，繼母應氏〔封夫人〕。永感下，兄為善〔義官〕，弟繼善〔署都指揮僉事〕、復善、明善、至善〔南京兵部郎中〕、巨善。娶曹氏。湖廣鄉試第二十九名，會試第二百二名。

陳璣〔貫河南開封府許州郾城縣軍籍，縣學生，治書經，字天儀，行二，年三十三，五月十二日生〕。曾祖原，祖昭，父鸞，母于氏，繼母王氏。具慶下，兄珠，弟琉、𤣱、瑚。娶曹氏。河南鄉試第十二名，會試第一百九十名。

方一桂〔貫福建興化府莆田縣軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字世芬，行一，年三十，二月十六日生〕。曾祖新〔府同知，進階中順大夫〕，祖昪，父宜賢〔知縣〕，母吳氏。具慶下，弟一蘭〔同科進士〕、一梧。娶陳氏。福建鄉試第七十一名，會試第五十二名。

趙綸〔貫直隸松江府上海縣民籍，縣學增廣生，治詩經，字廷言，行二，年三十六，七月十四日生〕。曾祖圭，祖仁，父霽，母潘氏。嚴侍下，兄經、相、朴，弟紳。娶陸氏。應天府鄉試第一百十八名，會試第二百十名。
translation_en:
Wang Congshan, registered in an official household in Xiangyang County, Xiangyang Prefecture, Huguang, was originally from Nanzheng County, Shaanxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he had the courtesy name Chengji, was second in birth order, and was aged twenty-two, born on the fourteenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather Wengui was posthumously awarded the titles General Who Guards the State and Regional Military Vice Commissioner; his grandfather Zhong was a Battalion Commander and received the same posthumous titles. His father Xin was Vice Commissioner-in-Chief of the Chief Military Commission of the Rear, serving as Regional Commander for Grain Transport. His father's former wife, née He, was posthumously granted the title Lady; his mother was née Yang, and his stepmother, née Ying, was granted the title Lady. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother Weishan was an honorary official; his younger brothers were Jishan, acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioner; Fushan; Mingshan; Zhishan, a Bureau Director in the Nanjing Ministry of War; and Jushan. He married a woman née Cao. He ranked twenty-ninth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 202nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Ji was registered in a military household in Yancheng County, Xuzhou Subprefecture, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan. A county school student specializing in the Classic of Documents, he had the courtesy name Tianyi, was second in birth order, and was aged thirty-three, born on the twelfth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Yuan, his grandfather Zhao, and his father Luan; his mother was née Yu and his stepmother née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Zhu, and his younger brothers were Liu, 𤣱 [reading uncertain], and Hu. He married a woman née Cao. He ranked twelfth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 190th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fang Yigui was registered in a military household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he had the courtesy name Shifen, was first in birth order, and was aged thirty, born on the sixteenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather Xin was a Prefectural Vice Prefect, advanced to the prestige title Grand Master of Central Compliance; his grandfather was Bian, and his father Yixian was a County Magistrate. His mother was née Wu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yilan, a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the same examination cohort, and Yiwu. He married a woman née Chen. He ranked seventy-first in the Fujian Provincial Examination and fifty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Lun was registered in a civilian household in Shanghai County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An added-quota county school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he had the courtesy name Tingyan, was second in birth order, and was aged thirty-six, born on the fourteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Gui, his grandfather Ren, and his father Ji; his mother was née Pan. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Jing, Xiang, and Pu, and his younger brother was Shen. He married a woman née Lu. He ranked 118th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 210th in the Metropolitan Examination.

王獻〔貫陝西西安府咸陽縣，軍籍，國子生，治易經，字惟臣，行三，年三十六，正月二十七日生〕。曾祖三，祖整，父才，母岳氏。具慶下，兄森、武，弟績、安、猷，娶馮氏。陝西鄉試第七名，會試第三十七名。

胡伯鰲〔貫浙江杭州府臨安縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字應元，行十，年四十四，四月二十六日生〕。曾祖才，祖琬，父澤，前母洪氏，母錢氏，繼母俞氏。永感下，兄伯真、伯良、伯瞻、伯參、伯麟，娶高氏。浙江鄉試第六十五名，會試第三百八名。

孫允中〔貫魯府儀衛司，官籍，直隸合肥縣人，兗州府學生，治詩經，字信道，行三，年二十七，四月十二日生〕。曾祖斅〔副千戶〕，祖永〔副千戶〕，父胤〔儀衛副〕，母孔氏〔封宜人〕。慈侍下，兄執中〔儀衛副〕、用中，弟守中、時中、一中、建中、惟中，娶梁氏。山東鄉試第十七名，會試第一百七十九名。

單鉞〔貫武功中衛，匠籍，直隸嘉定縣人，國子生，治書經，字廷儀，行三，年三十六，八月初二日生〕。曾祖信，祖政，父紀，母姜氏。慈侍下，兄欽、鑑，弟錦、鐘、鎧、鎰、銳、鉷、鐶、鑾、銓、鈞，娶蘇氏。順天府鄉試第一百十四名，會試第八十一名。
translation_en:
Wang Xian 王獻 was registered in Xianyang County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, in a military household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Weichen and ranked third among his brothers. He was aged thirty-six and born on the twenty-seventh day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was San, his grandfather Zheng, and his father Cai; his mother was née Yue. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Sen and Wu, and his younger brothers Ji, An, and You. His wife was née Feng. He placed seventh in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and thirty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Bo’ao 胡伯鰲 was registered in Lin’an County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Yingyuan and ranked tenth among his brothers. He was aged forty-four and born on the twenty-sixth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cai, his grandfather Wan, and his father Ze. His father’s former wife was née Hong, his mother née Qian, and his stepmother née Yu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Bozhen, Boliang, Bozhan, Bocan, and Bolin. His wife was née Gao. He placed sixty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and three hundred eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Yunzhong 孫允中 was registered in an official household attached to the Ceremonial Guard Office of the princely establishment of Lu and was a native of Hefei County, Zhili. A student of the Yanzhou Prefectural School specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Xindao and ranked third among his brothers. He was aged twenty-seven and born on the twelfth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather Xiao and grandfather Yong were both Vice Battalion Commanders. His father Yin was Vice Director of the Ceremonial Guard; his mother, née Kong, had been granted the title Lady of Suitability. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Zhizhong, Vice Director of the Ceremonial Guard, and Yongzhong; his younger brothers were Shouzhong, Shizhong, Yizhong, Jianzhong, and Weizhong. His wife was née Liang. He placed seventeenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and one hundred seventy-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shan Yue 單鉞 was registered in an artisan household of the Wugong Central Guard and was a native of Jiading County, Zhili. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he had the courtesy name Tingyi and ranked third among his brothers. He was aged thirty-six and born on the second day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xin, his grandfather Zheng, and his father Ji; his mother was née Jiang. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Qin and Jian; his younger brothers were Jin, Zhong, Kai, Yi, Rui, Hong, Huan, Luan, Quan, and Jun. His wife was née Su. He placed one hundred fourteenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

王學古〔貫陝西寧夏衛軍籍，直隸金壇縣人，衛學生，治禮記，字克誠，行二，年三十一，十月初五日生〕。曾祖順，祖貴，父琇，母韓氏，繼母郭氏。具慶下，兄師古〔坫貢〕，弟稽古，娶呂氏，繼娶劉氏、陳氏。陝西鄉試第十一名，會試第二百五十二名。

translation_en:
Bai Qing was registered in a military household in Lingbao County, Shanzhou, Henan Prefecture, Henan. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Rites, he had the courtesy name Yingqian and was second in birth order, aged thirty-eight [?; the age formula is garbled], born on the twenty-seventh day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Wu, his grandfather Jing, his father He, and his mother née Guo. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Lian; his younger brothers were Xian, Ning, and Ding. He married a woman née Kang. He placed thirty-first in the Henan Provincial Examination and 297th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Gao was registered with the Guilin Right Guard in Guangxi and was a native of Guanyang County. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Yangzhi and was second in birth order, aged thirty-four, born on the twelfth day of the intercalary ninth month. His great-grandfather was Fu, his grandfather Zhiqing, and his father Fasen; his father's former wife was née Zhou, and his mother was née Bin. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Tong and his younger brother Shan. He married a woman née Deng. He placed eighth in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and 354th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Xuegu was registered in a military household of the Ningxia Guard in Shaanxi and was a native of Jintan County in the directly administered metropolitan region. A guard school student specializing in the Book of Rites, he had the courtesy name Kecheng and was second in birth order, aged thirty-one, born on the fifth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Shun, his grandfather Gui, his father Xiu, his mother née Han, and his stepmother née Guo. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Shigu, whose status is recorded as 坫貢 [?], and his younger brother was Jigu. He married a woman née Lü and subsequently women née Liu and née Chen. He placed eleventh in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 252nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Zuo was registered in an official household of the Left Battalion of the Chengdu Right Guard in Sichuan and was a native of Dingyuan County in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Daofu and was first in birth order, aged forty-one, born on the thirtieth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Xin, his grandfather Xuan, and his father Qin; his father's former wife was née Ren, and his mother was née Chang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Shi, Director of Food Services; Zhong; Yi; Hua; Jie; Chuan, Director of Food Services; and Cheng. He married a woman née Chen. He placed nineteenth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 117th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Huang Jin, registered in an artisan household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, was an additional student of the prefectural school and specialized in the Book of Odes (Shijing). His courtesy name was Tingsheng; he ranked seventh among his brothers and was twenty-eight years old, born on the nineteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Mengxun, his grandfather Deyu, his father Ruling, and his mother née Lin. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Liang, Yuan, and Zhong, and his younger brothers Yu and Hu. He married a woman née Chen and subsequently a woman née Weng. He placed eighteenth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 186th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Han, registered in a civilian household in Yibin County, Xuzhou Prefecture, Sichuan, was a student of the Imperial University and specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shizhao; he ranked first among his brothers and was forty-one years old, born on the first day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhong, a prefectural Clerk; his grandfather was Jun, his father Jinghe, and his mother née Shi. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed twenty-fifth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 177th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liang Ying, registered in a civilian household in Xiangfu County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, was a student of the Imperial University and specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Bangyan; he ranked first among his brothers and was forty-three years old, born on the first day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ju, his grandfather Zeng, his father Mei, his mother née Liu, and his stepmother née Li. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Xiong. He married a woman née Lu. He placed seventy-eighth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 335th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Wenzhi, registered in a civilian household in Dongping Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, was a student of the Imperial University and specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yuanzheng; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-four years old, born on the sixth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jin, his grandfather Cong, his father Ang, his mother née Zhang, and his stepmother née Wang. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Wenlan. He married a woman née Liu. He placed seventy-first in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 170th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Guan Jiazhen, courtesy name Jifu, was from Gaomi County, Laizhou Prefecture, Shandong, registered in an artisan household. A county government school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-three, and born on the twenty-eighth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jin; his grandfather, Hui; his father, Jiuyun, an Assistant Instructor; and his mother, née Wang. His grandfather and both parents were living. His younger brothers were Jiayou, Jiafu, Jiazhi, Jiaxiang, and Jiamo, and his wife was née Li. He placed twenty-fourth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 306th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Rang, courtesy name Kerang, was from Zhucheng County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, registered in a military officer household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the twenty-sixth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Quan; his grandfather, Qing; and his father, Zheng. His father's former wife was née Qin, his mother was née Liu, and his stepmother was née Zhang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Liang and Gong. He married a woman née Jiang and subsequently a woman née Ding. He placed fifty-third in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 103rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hao Shouzheng, courtesy name Zhongfu, was from Qizhou, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang, registered in a civilian household. A subprefectural government school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the seventeenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zijiao; his grandfather, Zhi'an; his father, Yuan; and his mother, née Xu. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brothers were Shoudao and Shoulu, and his wife was née Chen. He placed thirty-sixth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 222nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cao Zuru, courtesy name Yixue, was from Huojia County, Weihui Prefecture, Henan, registered in a civilian household. A prefectural government school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the first day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xiang, a Surveillance Vice Commissioner; his grandfather, Ang, an Instructor; and his father, Fengyi, an Imperial University student. His mother was née Li and his stepmother née Ji. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zuwu, Zuren, Zuxian, and Zuyan, and his wife was née Wang. He placed twenty-eighth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 400th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Liu Yu 劉隅, courtesy name Shuzheng, was registered in a civilian household in Dong’e County, Dongping Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong. An additional student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the tenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Lian, an Instructor; his grandfather was Guan, posthumously appointed Director in the Ministry of Personnel; his father was Yue, Right Administration Vice Commissioner; and his mother, née Xu, was granted the title Lady of Virtue. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Tian, Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue, Gu, Ze, and Pei; his younger brothers were Jie, Mu, Yuan, and Gang. His wife was née Zhai. He placed eighth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and nineteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Tiyuan 劉體元, courtesy name Haofu, was registered in a civilian household in Nanhai County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong. A Confucian scholar specializing in the Classic of Changes, he was third in birth order, aged twenty-seven, and born on the thirteenth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Fang, his grandfather Guangcheng, his father Yin, and his mother née Zeng. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Mengyuan and Zhongyuan; his younger brothers were Xun, Kan, and Yi. His wife was née Lao. He placed thirty-fourth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 319th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Xingjian 徐行健, courtesy name Qianfu, was registered in an officer household of Changhuai Guard at Zhongdu and was a native of Nanfeng County, Jiangxi. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged forty-two, and born on the nineteenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Jingren; his grandfather was Jingchun, a Company Commander promoted to the prestige title General of Military Strategy; his father was Ji, a Company Commander; and his mother was née Gao. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Jiusi, a Company Commander; his younger brothers were Xingshu, Xingyi, Xingzhong, and Xingji. His wife was née Zhou. He placed 116th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and forty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shan Wenbiao 單文彪, courtesy name Daochong, was registered in a civilian household in Shan County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong. A student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Classic of Documents, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the twenty-second day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Ai, his grandfather Cong, his father Ting, and his mother née Wang. His father was deceased and his mother living. The entry then lists “Yuan Long Yu” [?], with the relationships and division of names unclear. His wife was née Guo. He placed fifteenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 136th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Min 王民 was registered in a military household in Gucheng County, Jingzhou, Hejian Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region (Zhili). An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Jingfu and ranked first among his brothers. He was thirty-seven, born on the nineteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Juzheng, his grandfather Ying, and his father Lian; his mother was née Li. His father was living and his mother deceased. His wife was née Ma. He placed 123rd in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 276th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Bing 王昺 was registered in a military household in Zhangqiu County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Chenghui and ranked fourth among his brothers. He was thirty-three, born on the eighteenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Di, his grandfather Jian, and his father Jin, who held an honorary title for longevity. His mother and stepmother were both née Liu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Sheng, an Imperial University student, Dan, and Yu. His wife was née Guo. He placed seventy-fifth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 253rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Yue 王瀹 was registered in a civilian household in Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili, and was a native of Kunshan County. A county government school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Zhongmei and ranked first among his brothers. He was twenty, born on the twenty-first day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Ming, his grandfather Tang, and his father Chao; his mother was née Li. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Can and Zhao. His wife was née Jin. He placed 109th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and forty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Li 沈澧 was registered in a military household in Shanyin County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he had the courtesy name Wenlan and ranked fifth among his brothers. He was thirty-nine, born on the fourteenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Heng, and his grandfather Bing was posthumously appointed Office Manager in the Registry of the Censorate. His father Qin was an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner, advanced to the rank of Grand Master for Court Attendance. His mother, née Zhang, was granted the title Lady (Ruren). Both parents were living. His younger brother Song was a Ceremonial Usher. His wife was née Wang; he subsequently married women née Hu and née Zhang. He placed eightieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 180th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Lin Zhong 林鍾, courtesy name Dahe, was registered in a civilian household in Gaoyao County, Zhaoqing Prefecture, Guangdong. A county school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-seventh day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Di; his grandfather, Daoyuan, was a prefectural Registrar; and his father, Gao, was a Records Examiner. His father's former wife was née Su, and his mother was née Tang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Zongshan, his younger brother was Kai, and his wife was née Deng. He placed fourteenth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 303rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wei Jingxing 魏景星, courtesy name Wenrui, was registered in a civilian household in Xuancheng County, Ningguo Prefecture, Zhili. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked fifth among his brothers and was aged forty, born on the twenty-first day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yanwan; his grandfather was Zhimin; and his father, Shiqi, was a District Magistrate. His mother was née Xie. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Jingkui, Jingyang, Jingquan, and Jinghong, and his wife was née Zhao. He placed seventy-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 342nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Chun 李錞, courtesy name Bohe, was registered in an official household in Tongzhou, Shuntian Prefecture, and was a native of Jingning County, Zhejiang. An attached student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged twenty-five, born on the sixteenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather, Xin, was posthumously granted the title of Company Commander; his grandfather, Gui, was a Company Commander; and his father, Zhang, was Right Provincial Administration Commissioner. His father's former wife, née Qi, was posthumously granted the title of Lady of Repose; his mother, née Zhao, was granted the same title. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ruqin, a tribute scholar (gongshi); Xuan, an honorary official; Yue; Kai; and Zhen. His younger brother was Bing, and his wife was née Zhang. He placed 123rd in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 344th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cheng Xu 程緒, courtesy name Zhengfu, was registered in a military household in Baoji County, Fengxiang Prefecture, Shaanxi. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked third among his brothers and was aged thirty-seven, born on the twenty-fifth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rong; his grandfather was Xuan; and his father, Zhang, was a District Vice Magistrate. His mother was née Chang, and his stepmother was née Gao. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ji and Lun, and his wife was née Mao. He placed twenty-second in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 301st in the Metropolitan Examination.

郭弘化〔貫江西吉安府安福縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字子弼，行六，年四十三，正月二十日生〕。曾祖敬肅，祖濬川，父乾厲，母陳氏。慈侍下，兄弘善，弟弘富、弘倫，娶鄧氏，要彭氏。江西鄉試第七十四名，會試第三百七十二名。

王邦裕〔貫山東東昌府堂邑縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字子修，行二，年三十五，四月十七日生〕。曾祖政，祖玉〔監生，贈奉直大夫、後軍都督府經歷〕，父臣〔戶部郎中〕，母張氏〔封宜人〕。具慶下，兄邦聘，弟邦禎〔監生〕、邦祉〔監生〕、邦佑、邦禮、邦祚，娶侯氏，繼娶張氏、張氏。山東鄉試第五十六名，會試第一百二十三名。
translation_en:
Zhao Jixun 趙繼勲 was registered in Ruyang County, Runing Prefecture, Henan, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he had the courtesy name Chongzhi and was third in family order, aged forty-four, born on the eighteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather Kuan was an Investigating Censor; his grandfather Tong was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi); and his father was Sheng. His father's former wife was Lady Lin, and his mother was Lady Ni. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Jizhe and Jiwu, the latter a Station Master; his younger brother was Jizan. He married Lady Tie and subsequently Lady Zhou. He ranked seventy-ninth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 305th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dong Yin 董寅 was registered in Hanyang County, Hanyang Prefecture, Huguang, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Xuanliang and was first in family order, aged thirty-four, born on the eighteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shigao; his grandfather Chen was an Imperial University student; his father Wenxian was an Assistant Instructor; and his mother was Lady Zhou. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brother was Cai, and he married Lady Zhang. He ranked sixty-fifth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 226th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Honghua 郭弘化 was registered in Anfu County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Zibi and was sixth in family order, aged forty-three, born on the twentieth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jingsu; his grandfather was Junchuan; his father was Qianli; and his mother was Lady Chen. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Hongshan, and his younger brothers were Hongfu and Honglun. He married Lady Deng; the text also mentions Lady Peng, apparently as another wife [?]. He ranked seventy-fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 372nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Bangyu 王邦裕 was registered in Tangyi County, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Zixiu and was second in family order, aged thirty-five, born on the seventeenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zheng. His grandfather Yu was an Imperial University student, posthumously granted the title Grand Master for Upright Service and the office of Registrar in the Chief Military Commission of the Rear. His father Chen was a Bureau Director in the Ministry of Revenue, and his mother, Lady Zhang, was granted the title Lady of Suitability. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Bangpin; his younger brothers were Bangzhen and Bangzhi, both Imperial University students, and Bangyou, Bangli, and Bangzuo. He married Lady Hou and subsequently Lady Zhang and another Lady Zhang [the surname is repeated in the text; ?]. He ranked fifty-sixth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 123rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

李新芳〔貫山西潞州，民籍，國子生，治《書經》，字元德，行十一，年三十四，七月二十八日生〕。曾祖璉，祖格，父清〔倉副使〕，母王氏，繼母楊氏。具慶下，娶孫氏。山西鄉試第二名，會試第五十七名。

張文泰〔貫陝西臨洮府渭源縣，軍籍，國子生，治《書經》，字用亨，行二，年三十七，正月初三日生〕。曾祖善〔贈戶部員外郎〕，祖安〔太僕寺少卿〕，父鶚〔知縣〕，前母傅氏，母黃氏。具慶下，兄文通〔義官〕，弟文顯，娶任氏，繼娶何氏。陝西鄉試第七十八名，會試第一百名。
translation_en:
Wang Pin 王聘, registered in a civilian household in Lijin County, Binzhou Subprefecture, Ji’nan Prefecture, Shandong, was a county government student specializing in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Nianjue; he ranked first in birth order, was twenty-nine, and was born on the fifth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sirang; his grandfather, Hong, held the title of honorary official; his father was Chen, and his mother was née Li. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His elder brother was Zhao, and his younger brothers were Zheng, Deng, and Yan. He married a woman née Liu. He placed seventieth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 143rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wei Shangchen 韋商臣, registered in a civilian household in Changxing County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a National University student specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Xiyin; he ranked fourth in birth order, was thirty-four, and was born on the twenty-ninth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qian; his grandfather, Ling, was posthumously appointed Magistrate; and his father, Hou, was a Prefectural Vice Prefect. His father’s former wife, née Wu, was posthumously granted the title Lady (ruren), and his mother, née Hu, was granted the same title. Both his parents were deceased. His elder brother, Yaochen, was an annual tribute student; his younger brothers were Tangchen and Shuchen. He married a woman née Cai. He placed eighty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 176th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Xinfang 李新芳, registered in a civilian household in Luzhou Subprefecture, Shanxi, was a National University student specializing in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Yuande; he ranked eleventh in birth order, was thirty-four, and was born on the twenty-eighth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lian; his grandfather was Ge; and his father, Qing, was a Granary Vice Commissioner. His mother was née Wang, and his stepmother was née Yang. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Sun. He placed second in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and fifty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Wentai 張文泰, registered in a military household in Weiyuan County, Lintao Prefecture, Shaanxi, was a National University student specializing in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Yongheng; he ranked second in birth order, was thirty-seven, and was born on the third day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather, Shan, was posthumously appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue; his grandfather, An, was Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud; and his father, E, was a Magistrate. His father’s former wife was née Fu, and his mother was née Huang. Both parents were living. His elder brother, Wentong, held the title of honorary official, and his younger brother was Wenxian. He married a woman née Ren and subsequently married a woman née He. He placed seventy-eighth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and one hundredth in the Metropolitan Examination.

title: 嘉靖二年進士登科錄

translation_en:
Zhang Wenzhi, registered in Qingyun County, Cangzhou, Hejian Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a county government student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Zishen; he ranked third among his brothers and was aged twenty-nine, born on the nineteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhongli; his grandfather, Rong; and his father, Cong, a Sacrificial Official; his mother was née Xu. His mother alone was living. His elder brothers were Xiang and Xuezhi. He married a woman née Chen and subsequently a woman née Ma. He placed ninety-eighth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 216th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xing En, registered in Nanzheng County, Hanzhong Prefecture, Shaanxi, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Yuncheng; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged forty-six, born on the first day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Duan, a County Magistrate; his grandfather, Shu, a Medical Officer; and his father, Jixian, a Subprefectural Vice Magistrate. His mother was née Cui, and his stepmother was née Xiong. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Ze, Lin, Yu, Jing, Lun, Wan, Jin, Shen, Shou, Qi, and Ji. He married a woman née Han and subsequently a woman née Shen. He placed 130th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 398th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Meng Juren, registered in Liaozhou, Shanxi, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Tiyuan; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-five, born on the twenty-fifth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Duan, a tribute student; his grandfather, Xian, an honorary official recognized for longevity; and his father, Long, an Assistant Prefect. His mother was née Zhang. His mother alone was living. His younger brothers were Siren and Cunren. He married a woman née Yuan. He placed forty-second in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 374th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Tiguan, registered in Luling County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a county government student specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Xingzhong; he ranked fourth among his brothers and was aged thirty-three, born on the seventeenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Pimo; his grandfather, Wulun; and his father, Jing. His mother was née Zeng. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Tizhen, Tikan, and Tigen. He married a woman née Peng. He placed forty-ninth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and thirty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
李士翱〔貫山東濟南府長山縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字如翰，行一，年三十六，五月二十三日生〕。曾祖文秀，祖廣，父宗明，母張氏。永感下，弟士羽、士翼，娶張氏，繼娶曲氏。山東鄉試第六十六名，會試第一百五十名。

董紹〔貫直隸常州府武進縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字宗遠，行一，年四十一，八月二十一日生〕。曾祖志全，祖珍，父尚彬〔七品散官〕，母何氏。永感下，弟約〔監生〕，娶徐氏，繼娶陳氏。應天府鄉試第三十八名，會試第二百三十三名。

陳大用〔貫福建福州府長樂縣，軍籍，縣學附學生，治詩經，字則可，行四，年二十二，八月十五日生〕。曾祖育，祖英，父鋈，母高氏。慈侍下，兄大猷、大倫、大夏，弟大濩〔知縣〕、大全，娶林氏。福建鄉試第五十八名，會試第一百八十一名。

陳情〔貫河南河南衛，官籍，直隸來安縣人，國子生，治易經，字子孝，行三，年四十，二月二十一日生〕。曾祖鏞〔指揮僉事〕，祖源，父欒，前母杜氏，母傅氏。慈侍下，兄言、力，弟誥、謨，娶王氏。河南鄉試第三十三名，會試第二百八十九名。
translation_en:
Li Shi'ao 李士翱, courtesy name Ruhan, was registered in Changshan County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the twenty-third day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenxiu; his grandfather, Guang; his father, Zongming; and his mother, née Zhang. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Shiyu and Shiyi. He married a woman née Zhang and subsequently a woman née Qu. He placed sixty-sixth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 150th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dong Shao 董紹, courtesy name Zongyuan, was registered in Wujin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged forty-one, and born on the twenty-first day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhiquan; his grandfather, Zhen; his father, Shangbin, a prestige official of the seventh rank; and his mother, née He. Both parents were deceased. His younger brother Yue was an Imperial University student. He married a woman née Xu and subsequently a woman née Chen. He placed thirty-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 233rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Dayong 陳大用, courtesy name Zeke, was registered in Changle County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, in a military household. An additional student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Book of Odes, he was fourth in birth order, aged twenty-two, and born on the fifteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yu; his grandfather, Ying; his father, Wu 鋈; and his mother, née Gao. His father was deceased, and he served his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Dayou, Dalun, and Daxia; his younger brothers were Dahuo, a county magistrate, and Daquan. He married a woman née Lin. He placed fifty-eighth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 181st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Qing 陳情, courtesy name Zixiao, was registered in Henan Guard, Henan, in an official household, and was a native of Lai'an County in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was third in birth order, aged forty, and born on the twenty-first day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yong, an Assistant Commander; his grandfather, Yuan; and his father, Luan. His father's former wife was née Du, and his mother was née Fu. His father was deceased, and he served his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Yan and Li; his younger brothers were Gao and Mo. He married a woman née Wang. He placed thirty-third in the Henan Provincial Examination and 289th in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
王誥〔貫河南汝寧府西平縣，軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字公遇，行一，年二十六，八月二十日生。〕曾祖聰〔贈衞經歷〕，祖清〔衞經歷〕，父志德〔教諭〕，母李氏。重慶下，弟訓、訥，娶李氏。河南鄉試第三十五名，會試第二百九名。

俞朝妥〔貫浙江紹興府新昌縣，民籍，國子生，治書經，字寵之，行二十六，年三十六，九月二十五日生。〕曾祖用直，祖叔安〔封監察御史〕，父振忠〔陰陽訓術〕，母呂氏。慈侍下，弟朝孚，娶呂氏，繼娶張氏。浙江鄉試第六十三名，會試第三百八十二名。

陸夢麟〔貫江西南昌府豐城縣，軍籍，府學增廣生，治詩經，字文瑞，行五，年二十九，十二月二十一日生。〕曾祖具載〔旌表義官〕，祖德美，父時敘，母杜氏。具慶下，弟夢豹，娶熊氏，繼娶李氏。江西鄉試第三十五名，會試第二百七十七名。

謝朝輔〔貫陝西西安左衞，軍籍，直隸臨淮縣人，咸寧縣學生，治易經，字汝載，行五，年三十四，七月二十四日生。〕曾祖海，祖德，父恩〔教諭，封監察御史〕，母馬氏〔封孺人〕。永感下，兄朝宣〔按察使〕、朝黼、朝政、朝紳，娶查氏。陝西鄉試第六名，會試第二百七名。
translation_en:
Wang Gao, courtesy name Gongyu, was registered in a military household in Xiping County, Runing Prefecture, Henan, and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes. He ranked first among his brothers and male cousins and was aged twenty-six, born on the twentieth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cong, posthumously granted the title of Guard Registrar; his grandfather was Qing, a Guard Registrar; his father was Zhide, an Instructor; and his mother was née Li. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Xun and Ne, and his wife was née Li. He placed thirty-fifth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 209th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Chaotuo, courtesy name Chongzhi, was registered in a civilian household in Xinchang County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents. He ranked twenty-sixth among his brothers and male cousins and was aged thirty-six, born on the twenty-fifth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yongzhi; his grandfather was Shu’an, granted the title of Investigating Censor; his father was Zhenzhong, an Instructor in the School of Yin and Yang; and his mother was née Lü. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brother was Chaofu. His wife was née Lü, and he subsequently married a woman née Zhang. He placed sixty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 382nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Menglin, courtesy name Wenrui, was registered in a military household in Fengcheng County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, and was an added-quota student at the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Odes. He ranked fifth among his brothers and male cousins and was aged twenty-nine, born on the twenty-first day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Juzai, officially commended as an Officer of Righteousness; his grandfather was Demei; his father was Shixu; and his mother was née Du. Both his parents were living. His younger brother was Mengbao. His wife was née Xiong, and he subsequently married a woman née Li. He placed thirty-fifth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 277th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xie Chaofu, courtesy name Ruzai, was registered in a military household of the Xi’an Left Guard in Shaanxi and was a native of Linhuai County in the directly administered metropolitan region. He was a student at the Xianning County school specializing in the Book of Changes. He ranked fifth among his brothers and male cousins and was aged thirty-four, born on the twenty-fourth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hai; his grandfather was De; his father was En, an Instructor granted the title of Investigating Censor; and his mother was née Ma, granted the title of Lady. Both his parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Chaoxuan, a Surveillance Commissioner, Chaofu 朝黼, Chaozheng, and Chaoshen. His wife was née Zha. He placed sixth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 207th in the Metropolitan Examination.

應果〔貫浙江處州府遂昌縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字子陽，行二，年三十五，十一月十八日生〕。曾祖存琳，祖世鎰，父湛，母潘氏。具慶下，兄楷，弟檣、榦，娶勞氏。浙江鄉試第八十三名，會試第二百五十五名。

translation_en:
Qian Xuekong, courtesy name Yishi, was registered in a civilian household in Jinhua County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang. A county school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked 112th in his family’s birth order and was aged forty-two, born on the twenty-third day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhi; his grandfather, Sheng; and his father, Ying, a prefectural Vice Prefect advanced to the rank of Grand Master for Court Service. His mother was née Zhu, and his stepmother née Jin. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Xuezheng and Xueli, and his younger brother was Xueshi. He married a woman née Wang. He placed seventy-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 258th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Peng, courtesy name Bohua, was registered in an official household of the Zhuolu Left Guard in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Documents, he ranked first in his family’s birth order and was aged twenty-six, born on the twenty-seventh day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Li; his grandfather, Jing; his father, Yu; and his mother, née Ye. His father was living, and his mother was deceased. He married a woman née Li and subsequently a woman née Wang. He placed 133rd in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 162nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ying Guo, courtesy name Ziyang, was registered in a civilian household in Suichang County, Chuzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked second in his family’s birth order and was aged thirty-five, born on the eighteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cunlin; his grandfather, Shiyi; his father, Zhan; and his mother, née Pan. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Kai, and his younger brothers were Qiang and Gan. He married a woman née Lao. He placed eighty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 255th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Daolan, courtesy name Shuguan, was registered in a salt-transport household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian. A county school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked third in his family’s birth order and was aged thirty-eight, born on the nineteenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xizhe; his grandfather, Shiwang, held the honorary designation of Philanthropic Official; his father was Bangyong; and his mother was née Huang. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Daoben and Daoming, and his younger brothers were Daozhou, Daozong, Daohong, and Daotong. He married a woman née Wu. He placed sixty-ninth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and eighty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
She Mianxue 佘勉學, courtesy name Xingfu, was registered in an official household of Liuzhou Guard, Guangxi, and was a native of Xiaogan County, Huguang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the nineteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Mao; his grandfather, She, was a tribute student; his father, Chongfeng, was a prefect; and his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His wife was née Luo. He ranked tenth in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and 198th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liang Jianchen 梁建辰, courtesy name Maoyang, was registered in a military household in Panyu County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the fifth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Derun; his grandfather was An; his father, Yi, held honorary official status granted for longevity; and his mother was née Wu. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Jianyu, Jianxuan, and Jianhong, and his wife was née Yan. He ranked fifteenth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 250th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Tang 張鏜, courtesy name Deyang, was registered in an artisan household of Wugong Central Guard and was a native of Yuyao County, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was fourth in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the third day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was An; his grandfather was Hua; and his father was Kui, whose annotation reads guan shou, probably indicating honorary official status granted for longevity [?]. His father's former wife was née Chen, and his mother was née Yu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yi, Yue, and Ming, and his wife was née Xu. He ranked ninety-seventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 388th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cheng Jiaxing 程嘉行, courtesy name Gongmin, was registered in a military household in Leping County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was sixteenth in birth order, aged forty-four, and born on the sixteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Benli; his grandfather, Lin, was an assistant magistrate; his father was Tingbiao; and his mother was née Fan. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Jiarou, Jiaxian, Jiashan, Jiake, Jiayan, and Jiawang, and his wife was née Han. He ranked fifty-first in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 116th in the Metropolitan Examination.
